title: Updated Ravens 53-Man Roster After Second Preseason Game
full_text:
A few more practices. One more preseason game.
That’s it until we have a 53-man roster for real. It’s almost here.
Of course, that first 53-man that formulates next weekend doesn’t amount to much as the Ravens will be adding players from other rosters and trying to make various moves. And then we get the 53 that starts practicing and moving to Week 1. (And, yes, we already have some practice squad projections, too).
We have a few shakeups in this projection; more than most other recent iterations. All of the mystery really remains on one side of the ball. And than will continue into the season, with so much new and uncertain and unproven with Declan Doyle’s offense, while Jesse Minter's defense best be ready to perform in midseason form a few weeks from now.
Don't expect many players truly on the roster bubble, let alone on the roster, to do much of anything Friday night against the Commanders and that's mostly practice squad spots at stake.
All of a sudden things got complicated for this group. The trip to Minnesota resulted in some minor injuries and their first major injury with Danny Pinter’s patella tendon, and also the first dark cloud of legal matters with Rashod Bateman, whose always seemed like damaged goods to me, having his arrest from June come to light.
QB (2) – Lamar Jackson, Snoop Huntley: Joe Fagnone did it again. Pretty amazing stuff from an undrafted kid from UCONN.
RB (4) – Derrick Henry, Justice Hill, Adam Randall, Rasheen Ali: Both Randall and Ali banged up isn’t great. Jonathan Ward probably isn’t a great fit but he might have a chance here pending these medicals. Regardless, I think they are going to need some numbers here and I’m no longer going with a three-man projection.
TE (4) – Mark Andrews, Durham Smythe, Matthew Hibner, Josh Cuevas: I think they’ll regret not signing Darren Waller and going so inexperienced here.
WR (6) - Zay Flowers, WAIVER CLAIM/signing/trade, Ja’Kobi Lane, Elijah Sarratt, Devontez Walker, LaJohntay Wester: The allegations around Rashod Bateman’s arrest for family violence are ugly. The NFL created the Commissioner’s Exempt List with these types of situations in mind. Maybe they trade a corner for a depth receiver or sign someone cut elsewhere.
OL (9) - Ronnie Stanley, Vega Ioane, John Simpson, Roger Rosengarten, Ehtan Pocic, Jovaughn Gwyn, Carson Vinson, Emery Jones, Andrew Vorhees: I was skeptical about Gwyn being more than a practice squad guy before Pinter suffered a season-ending injury. Pocic was always going to be the starting center.
There just doesn't seem to be too much to wring your hands over on this side fo the ball. They have more corners than they know what to do with. They have a lot of deep depth at some other spots but those decisions will be more about whether to cut them or put them on the practice squad, not so much for the 53-man itself.
DL (7) – Nnamdi Madubuike, Travis Jones, Calais Campbell, Broderick Washington, John Jenkins, Rayshaun Benny, Adisa Isaac: Does Aeneas Peebles having a four-pressure game change the math? I’m still slotting him to the practice squad but many that is Isaac.
LB (7) – Trey Hendrickson, Roquan Smith, Teddye Buchanan, Zion Young, Mike Green, Tavius Robinson, Trenton Simpson: Wonder if Buchanan needs a few weeks inactive until he is good to go with so much time he missed.
CB (6) – Nate Wiggins, Chidobe Awuzie, Marlon Humphrey, Chandler Rivers, TJ Tampa, Keyon Martin: Somebody is getting dealt and maybe it’s someone listed above, and maybe not. Hope Amani Oruwariye makes it to the practice squad .
S (5) – Kyle Hamilton, Malaki Starks, Jaylinn Hawkins, K’Von Wallace, Keondre Jackson: Said it before and will say it again - it’s a loaded group. Going to see some interesting blitzes from this group and not just Hamilton.
K – Tyler Loop – Would like to see him try some from 50 plus on Friday.
P – Ryan Eckley – Monster game from him Saturday. Love to see it.
LS – Nick Moore – Steady Eady. Er, Steady Nick.

title: 4 Biggest Takeaways From Ravens Preseason Week 2 Victory
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens grinded to the second win of the Jesse Minter era as head coach in dominant defensive fashion with a decisive 13-3 win over the hosting Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on Saturday afternoon.
This exhibition bout followed two days of highly productive joint practices between the two teams, and it followed the same theme as those practices. Defense led the way for both teams, but in the end, it was the visiting Ravens who managed to do just enough on offense to emerge victorious.
"I'm proud of our guys [for] the way they played in that game," Minter said. "I thought we, especially in the second half, were able to kind of play the game the way we wanted to play a little bit more [and] control the ball a little bit more. [We] did a nice job on defense [in the] red zone [and] got a couple turnovers which we wanted to get"
Here are four of the biggest takeaways from the Ravens' preseason win over the Vikings:
Last week in the opener, it was the Ravens' second-stringers on defense who led the charge for their domination of the Philadelphia Eagles. This time around, it was players who didn't appear in that game until the fourth quarter or were just penciled in at third and fourth on the depth chart who stepped up and made pivotal splash plays.
Up front, they got 1.5 sacks, a tackle for loss and several run-stuffs from rotational interior defensive linemen C.J. Okoye, Rayshaun Benny and David Olajiga. On the edge, Kaimon Rucker had some nice pressures and a quarterback hit, while undrafted rookie Ethan Burke had the game of his life as a pro with three solo tackles, a sack, a tackle for loss, two quarterback hits, two batted passes and a forced fumble.
Ravens undrafted rookie OLB Ethan Burke: 34 snaps 2 tackles 2 pressures 1 sack 1 forced fumble 1 PBU pic.twitter.com/nJhwNUIjjy
At the second level, Jay Higgins IV made his return from a concussion, started the game, wore the green dot for the whole game, and recorded four total tackles, including three solos. Starting and playing next to him for all but nine snaps was undrafted rookie Dominic DeLuca, who also recorded four tackles, including one for a loss early in the game.
In the secondary, the three brightest standouts were second-year safety Keondre Jackson, fifth-round nickel Chandler Rivers and undrafted safety Silas Walters. The latter two didn't see any playing time until the fourth quarter last week but were on the field early and often in this game. Each of them recorded a pass breakup, five-plus tackles and a splash play, with Rivers' being a splitting a sack with Olajiga and Walters making up for an earlier blunder with a late interception to ice the game and secure a double-digit margin of victory. Jackson was all over the field on defense and special teams, finishing with a game-high eight total tackles, including two for a loss, a sack and a quarterback hit.
"We preach not having a drop-off on our backend, and on the defense," Jackson said. "So, the 'ones' hold us accountable; they go out there and play great. The 'twos' and 'threes,' we want to follow suit because you're just as good as your weakest link. Not saying that we have a weak link, but [we want] no drop-offs with that."
Coming out of the preseason opener, a dark horse emerged as a deserving candidate to start receiving first-team reps: Jovaughn Gwyn. Even before Danny Pinter went down with a season-ending injury on the first day of joint practices against the Vikings, the fourth-year pro was receiving a groundswell of support amongst the film-watchers for the impressive tape he put together against the Eagles in live action and against Minnesota's starters.
Unfortunately for Gwyn, he didn't carry over that momentum into the second preseason game despite getting the starting nod. This left the door open for 10th-year veteran Ethan Pocic to reemerge as the favorite to replace three-time Pro Bowler Tyler Linderbaum, as was widely expected following his signing at the onset of training camp.
The team has been gradually increasing Pocic's involvement in practices and games, given that he suffered a torn Achilles late last season, and he performed quite well in relief duty, starting in the second quarter this time around after not checking in until the fourth in the opener. With one preseason game left, Pocic will likely get to make his first start as a Raven and will likely get to play most of the first half, during which he can cement himself as the victor of the team's most anticipated and closely contested position battle.
Pocic's anchor looks as advertised. Hell of a drop against Big Citrus. #RavensFlock pic.twitter.com/OO3j4xKfcA
Even though he's not projected to be a full-time starter heading into his second season in the league, expectations for the 2025 second-rounder are sky-high given his talent and improved environment from both schematic and player-personnel aspects. Against the Vikings, he showed some proof of concept to support the hype he's been getting all summer with his performance in the first half.
Green completely derailed Minnesota's offensive possession of the game when he recorded a sack on second down for a loss of six yards and followed it up by drawing a holding penalty on third down that negated a 19-yard gain that would've gone for a first down. Both rushes came off the left side of the line and saw him show great bend and explosion around the edge on the sack and a nice inside move on the second play that likely would've led to a second straight sack had he not gotten held.
Practice paying off for Mike Green! For more highlights, visit https://t.co/ciLFizvHBw . pic.twitter.com/CN9q1kfB7P
"Regardless [of] what game it is, it is still a confidence boost, and it shows you that the work that you put in [and] the moves that I have been practicing [have been] paying off," Green said. "[I'm] trying to work on [my] craft in practice, [so] being able to go out there in the game and be successful with it, it means a lot."
For the second week in a row, arguably the brightest standout on offense for the Ravens was undrafted rookie signal caller Joe Fagnano. Once again, he led multiple scoring drives, was highly efficient, completing 15-of-20 attempts and produced a pass rating of over 90 with a game-high 106.9. His 123 passing yards were the most of any quarterback who touched the field in his game, and he was the only one to throw for a touchdown.
"[The Vikings] got [to] me a couple of times [and] showed a couple of different looks," Fagnano said. "It's kind of what their defense is known for, and they play really sound, really good defense. They try to confuse you and make you speed up your feet, and that's kind of the big emphasis for me is just playing my game, taking it one play at a time and taking what they gave me."
Joe Fagnano links up with Devontez Walker to get the @Ravens in the redzone Steam on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Ju3bX0SkZW
The most impressive aspect of Fagnano's performance was how calm and poised he stayed under pressure, not letting himself get rattled or caught off guard. He didn't put the ball in harm's way and continues to show a high-level ability as a processor. Even though he's an older rookie at 25 years old, he's still just a first-year pro and is already showing the maturity and other alluring traits of a veteran reserve.
"I thought Joe [Fagnano] came in again — [the] second week in a row — and just kind of managed the offense really well," Minter said. "[He] got us down there a few times, made some really key plays throwing the ball, [and] guys made some nice catches for him."
It's been half a decade since the Ravens opened a season with three quarterbacks on their roster, and after being viewed as an afterthought when he was initially brought in as a rookie minicamp tryout, Fagnano is playing himself into no worse than a prime practice squad candidate, if not an initial 53-man roster consideration.

title: Stop Me If You've Heard This Before, But The Ravens Might Have A Receiver Problem
full_text:
The Ravens have always looked like a team at least one playmaker short on offense.
It appeared that way in March after some quality tight ends left the building in free agency. It seemed that way in April when they decided to stick with mercurial and pouty and largely ineffective Rashod Bateman as a potential starter rather than trade him. It looked that way in May, even after throwing a bunch of day two-and-three draft capital at potential pass catchers.
It looked that way a few weeks into training camp when even the Ravens coaches couldn’t really muster talking up any of these project tight ends as being close to ready to do actual assignments asked of real NFL tight ends ( the ability to block matters ), and if Mark Andrrews is anything close to as cooked as I believe he is, it’s going to be even more heightened in September, too.
Rookie head coach Jesse Minter is being uber conservative about how he approached the preseason, so his real offense and real offensive players did absolutely nothing in these games. And now that Bateman is facing three family violence charges in Georgia with word leaking out last week of his arrest, they probably need to get real about what this means for their football team.
Not sure Minter is going to be able to “no comment” his way through this situation, try as he might.
The allegations and details within the police report are disturbing. The NFL is looking into the matter and the NFL might decide that it’s in the league’s best interest to have a quasi-effective NFL player removed from the team and n longer representing that team and this league in its workplace and on its sidelines, by putting him on the Commissioner’s Exempt List.
Legal matters such as this can take quite some time to resolve, and as we know the NFL can take discipline even when the law does not. Bateman is a player I am on record that I would have traded for whatever you can get y ears ago and called it addition by subtraction. I’d have walked from him, and have urged the team to do in this space and others multiple times.
They’ve always been fooling themselves about this guy.
He doesn’t exude winning traits. He has only stuck around here this long because the general manager hates being ripped for years for failing with wide receivers and he’s a former first-round pick and he works cheap. He works cheap because of a shortsighted holdout a few years back, against the counsel he was receiving, which cost him service time.
He’s clashed with the team over his medicals and he’s felt aggrieved by coaches repeatedly, and seems to be forever basking in that next last chance. Again, he’s off my team years ago. I wouldn’t have had him on the plane back to Baltimore. I’d call the league and beg them to put him on that list ASAP. Pay him to stay away. It’s Roger’s way.
Bateman’s never clicked with a two-time MVP quarterback, Lamar Jackson, for any long period of time. His health tends to be iffy. Wouldn’t want him in my receiver room for a multitude of reasons. They got over on him with the contract, and seem to think that will motivate him to become something he never will be. Certainly not in Baltimore.
(When someone is the subject of this many trade rumors, it's for good reasons).
Instead, they built a roster in which he’s kinda got be a thing for this to work. Devontez Walker might be better than him, but we won’t know until he gets a real run in games that count, and he can’t stay healthy to this point. Ja’Kobi Lane looks like the real deal, but the learning curve tends to be steep, and consistency is usually elusive at first. Preseason can be a fickle indicator.
Zay Flowers is heck of a football player, but he’s not getting any taller.
Last week in Minnesota - losing the second-best center on the roster for the season and then with Bateman’s arrest coming to light - could prove to be significant for this offense months to come. A forward-thinking operation would have a plan to address the public’s concerns about a situation involving a three-month old child ready to roll out, as well as some options for finding capable replacements at receiver.

title: 13 Winners and  4 Losers From Ravens Preseason Win Over Vikings
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens played their second preseason game on Saturday and notched the first road win of the Jesse Minter era in a 13-3 triumph over the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium.
Once again, neither team played their star players, and with hardly any starters coming off an invaluable and fruitful two days of joint practices. The depth of the Ravens' defense at all three levels shone brightly and was the main catalyst that propelled them to the low-scoring victory.
Here are several Ravens players who showed out and a few who still have work to do after the second preseason game.
No player on either side of the ball or in any of the three phases of the game did more to help themselves and raise their respective stock than the undrafted rookie edge defender. All three of Burke's tackles were solos, including one for a loss, and he recorded a sack, two quarterback hits, two batted passes and generated the Ravens' first turnover of the preseason on a forced fumble to open the fourth quarter.
After watching his fellow rookie at the same position, Matthew Hibner , spark the offense with a big 20-plus-yard play last week, he got a chance to do the same against the Vikings. His 23-yard reception early in the second quarter jump-started the Ravens' first scoring drive of the game, and he finished with three catches for a team-leading 46 receiving yards.
If each half could have a Defensive Player of the Game, the second-year pro would be deserving of the first-half honors, based on a two-play sequence where he pretty much single-handedly torpedoed a promising Vikings drive. Late in the first quarter, he showed great bend and flexibility around the edge to sack J.J. McCarthy for a loss of six yards, and on the next play, he drew a holding penalty that backed them up even more after he beat the left tackle with an inside move.
The second-year pro didn't record a sack, quarterback hit or tackle for loss, but was a noticeably disruptive force when he was on the field, getting penetration into the backfield on run downs and generating pressure.
The undrafted rookie had another impressively solid and efficient outing, showing the most poise under pressure of the three Ravens signal callers who took the field in this game. He went 15-of-20 for 123 passing yards and a touchdown, with no turnovers and a passer rating of 106.9.
The sixth-round rookie made Ravens fans say, 'Jordan Stout, who?' during and after his masterful performance against the Vikings. Eckley was plenty busy in this game amid the lack of consistent offense from both squads, and he was a field-flipping weapon, averaging 55.3 yards per punt with a long of 60 and pinning Minnesota inside its own 10-yard line twice.
The second-year pro earned himself some much-needed redemption and good faith after going 2-for-2 on his field goal attempts. While his second was a chip shot, his first was from 49 yards out, the same distance he missed wide left from in the opener- but he drilled it down the middle this time. He also continues to appear to have solved his struggles with getting kickoffs in the landing zone after leading the league in infractions as a rookie.
The undrafted rookie had an up-and-down game, allowing the 36-yard completion that set up the Vikings' only points of the game in the first half on a pass he could've intercepted had he not tripped over his own feet. He made up for it by thwarting Minnesota's final scoring attempt when he recorded his first career interception in the fourth quarter and finished with six total tackles and a pass defense.
The fifth-round rookie saw a lot more playing time this time around compared to last week, when he didn't check into the game until the fourth quarter. He was on defense and making plays in the first half and finished with five total tackles, a pass breakup, a quarterback hit and half a sack.
The second-year pro flashed his all-purpose playmaking on offense by finishing as the team's leader in targets and receptions, hauling in 5-of-7 for 24 receiving yards and the only touchdown of the game. He was fearless going over the middle and held onto the ball despite being on the receiving end of some big hits. On special teams, he returned a kickoff for 29 yards and a pair of punts for 31 yards, with a long of 19.
The second-year pro was flying around all over the field on defense and special teams, playing downhill and with tremendous physicality. Jackson finished with sa game-high eight total tackles, including six solos and two for a loss, a quarterback hit and a drive-ending sack on a blitz.
The 10th-year veteran might've just played his way into the pole position to become the Ravens' next starting center in the wake of the season-ending injury suffered by Danny Pinter. Even though he didn't start for the second week in a row, he checked into the game much sooner than the final 14 plays, as he did in the opener, and this time around, he played the best of the three centers who took the field.
The seventh-round rookie flashed once again as an interior pass rusher, recording his first sack, a quarterback hit and a solo tackle for loss.
While Burke had a great bounce-back performance, the third-year pro continued to fade into obscurity and likely out of favor with the front office and coaches with another unimpactful outing. Isaac was the only edge defender who suited up for this game who didn't make their presence felt in a tangible way or even record so much as a tackle. At this point, the 2024 third-rounder will need one hell of a preseason finale to keep himself off either the trading or chopping block.
The fourth-year pro got to make his first start after impressing in relief duty in the opener, but he wasn't able to build on that performance and was in the middle of the blocking unit that struggled out of the gate. Instead of further proving that he should be the frontrunner to win the starting center job, he left the door open for Pocic to leapfrog him with a lackluster performance against the Vikings' second-team defensive line.
After only playing a handful of snaps on the first two drives in the opener, the first-round pick and starting right guard played the whole first quarter and then some, and wasn't nearly as impressive as he was in his debut, getting called for his first holding penalty as a pro on the Ravens' opening drive.
The second-year pro made his second straight at right tackle and played the bulk of offensive snaps, but unlike the opener, he was far from disciplined in his technique and execution. He led the team with three holding penalties, two of which came on the same drive on the Ravens' second-to-last possession. Lichtenhan will need a strong bounce-back performance in the finale to make a push for a roster spot.

title: When Will Bills Make Fans Happy By Wearing Beloved Red Helmets This NFL Season?
full_text:
There's been a vocal, growing faction of the Buffalo Bills ' fanbase that prefers the team to wear its traditional 1990s style red helmets as frequently as possible.
Last summer, quarterback Josh Allen sent spectators into a frenzy when he came out of the tunnel wearing the classic red lid for the 2025 Return of the Blue & Red practice.
The bliss reemerged when the Bills donned the vintage helmets against the New York Jets in what was the final game ever played at the old Highmark Stadium last Week 18.
In 2026, those red dome-loving fans' collective wish will become reality on Christmas Day .
When the Bills visit the Denver Broncos for a Netflix special on December 25 , the road team will wear their throwback red helmets with white jerseys and pants.
Last month, we wrote about the possibility of the return of the red helmets for the special holiday kickoff. As it turned out, Buffalo made the official announcement exactly four months from the game date.
The Broncos have announced that they will wear their "Midnight Navy" uniforms for the 4:30 p.m. ET kickoff on Christmas Day.
Allen has professed his adoration for the classic red helmet on multiple occasions.
"They're great," said Allen at the beginning of training camp 13 months ago.
The quarterback relished the opportunity to wear it in the 2025 regular season finale.
"Didn't realize how big of a thing it was for the fans really up until that point [when he first wore a red helmet at the open practice]," said Allen. "I think it's a cool opportunity, obviously, an ode to the past, and as players, anytime you get to wear something new, it's fun."
Instead of satisfying the fans' request by permanently switching back to the red helmets, which the franchise abandoned in 2010, the Bills are giving us "Nickel City" alternate uniforms this year.
The gray base and the royal blue "charge" helmet haven't exactly struck a chord with the vocal majority. In fact, the uniforms received so much criticism that Allen offered a defense for the change .
“Stop hating on the jerseys, guys” said Allen. “They’re honestly great. Speaking of new, it’s a new look, we understand that. We’ve gotta be new.”
The Bills will close out their preseason schedule by hosting the Pittsburgh Steelers on Saturday, August 27 at Highmark Stadium.

title: Three Most Intriguing Players to Watch in Bills' Final Exhibition vs. Steelers
full_text:
It's a short week for the Buffalo Bills as they host the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3 of the NFL preseason on Thursday night. The Bills are coming off two lopsided victories in the preseason and look to make it a clean sweep before turning their attention to the Houston Texans in Week 1.
Before they can focus on that, there are several questions the front office and coaching staff need to answer. They are looking for which players they can count on to make the 53-man roster , and where each player belongs on the depth chart.
All of this has been playing out throughout the preseason and fans have one more chance to watch these battles take place. With that said, here's a look at the three most intriguing players to watch against the Steelers.
For those wondering, franchise quarterback Josh Allen will not play on Thursday.
Not many players on the Buffalo roster have benefited more from the arrival of Jim Leonhard than Javon Solomon. The third-year pass rusher looks far more comfortable playing from the two-point stance as an outside linebacker than he did in the three-point stance as a defensive end.
In two preseason games, Solomon has eight tackles, one sack, and one quarterback hit. As impressive as he's been, the position is still very deep and he has to fight off Mike Danna, who had two sacks against Carolina. If Solomon can perform at the same level this week as he did against Cleveland, he will have a great chance of sealing his spot on the 53-man roster.
It's pretty rare to say that a kicker will be intriguing to watch, but Tyler Bass falls under that category. He missed the entire 2025 season due to injury and hasn't had the smoothest return. Bass missed a 45-yard field goal against the Panthers, but was 3-of-4 overall. He then had some misses in practice before hitting a 52-yarder against the Browns , although that one stayed inside the uprights by the narrowest of margins.
Overall, Bass is rounding back into form and the coaching staff is ready to put all their trust in him. He's not battling for a spot, but fans would breathe a sigh of relief if he has a solid outing to close out the preseason.
Rookie Skyler Bell returned to practice on Tuesday and is expected to make his debut against the Steelers. Head coach Joe Brady said after the practice that he wants to see the full version of Bell, adding that he was flying around the field. Josh Allen was also singing his praises, saying that the rookie continues to make plays .
On Thursday night, fans should get their first chance to see if Bell can live up to the hype. It's not often a fourth-round pick who is fighting for a WR5 spot gets this much attention, but Bell has a skill set tailor-made for this offense, which is why there's so much intrigue.

title: Legendary Bills Broadcaster Argues Joe Brady Could Hold Buffalo Back From Super Bowl
full_text:
Taking over a team as talented as the Buffalo Bills is a double-edged sword.
First-year head coach Joe Brady was selected as the successor to Sean McDermott and he inherits a roster ready to win now. They're led by 2024 NFL MVP Josh Allen and 2025 NFL rushing leader James Cook . Defensively, their roster might not be elite, but the pieces are there with leaders such as Ed Oliver and Christian Benford paving the way.
Any coach would love to start their career with such a roster. The only issue is that there will be no room for error.
While other rookie head coaches, such as Klint Kubiak with the Las Vegas Raiders, Mike LaFleur of the Arizona Cardinals, and Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins will be afforded time to build their rosters up, Brady is expected to win immediately.
Those lofty expectations will make things tough, and former Bills broadcaster John Murphy believes he might not be able to live up to them. Murphy said he's impressed with just about everything with the team, but believes Brady will hold them back .
"Only one thing is missing. One thing will hold them back this year," Murphy wrote. "Their head coach."
To be fair, he wasn't saying Brady was a bad hire. Instead, Murphy is saying it's too early. He's also leaning on NFL history, which has seen just two head coaches win a Super Bowl in their first season and both had far more experience in the coaching ranks than Brady before taking over.
"Two coaches in their first year as a head coach have won Super Bowls: Don McCafferty with the Baltimore Colts in Super Bowl V and George Seifert of the Super Bowl XXIV champion 49ers.  In Seifert’s case, he inherited a Super Bowl champion from Bill Walsh the year before. In both cases, both McCafferty and Seifert had at least a decade on the staffs of their teams before becoming head coach."
Murphy added that Brady is not only the youngest head coach in the league at age 36, but also that he has the least amount of experience in the NFL.
The good news for Buffalo fans is that coaches are finding success much quicker these days than in the past. One of the best examples is Mike Macdonald, who completely turned the Seattle Seahawks around in just two seasons.
Macdonald took over a team that was 9-8 the prior year, but had clearly hit a wall. He went 10-7 in his first season, then re-tooled the roster with a new quarterback and shipped off their No. 1 wideout. Macdonald then led Seattle to a 14-3 record and a Super Bowl win in his second season.
Brady takes control of a team that was in better shape than the one Macdonald inherited. He also has experience working with the offense and was able to get the most out of Josh Allen . Those are reasons to believe he can find success early.
That said, expecting a rookie head coach to bring home the title is a tough ask. Brady, however, understands what's at stake and is ready to prove he was the right man for the job.

title: Terrel Bernard and Other Buffalo Bills Injury Updates from Tuesday's Practice
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills were back on the practice field on Tuesday and head coach Joe Brady game some injury updates before the session.
One of the notable additions to the training camp injury report on Monday was linebackter Terrel Bernard, which obviously raised concern initially.
Brady confirmed Bernard's absence was injury-related, but he added that he's not concerned for the veteran linebacker and Bernard should be fine for Week 1.
"No," Brady said when asked if there's any concern for Bernard's injury. "(Terrel Bernard) is going to be good to."
Given his injury issues the past few campaigns , any time "Terrel Bernard" and "injury" are in the same sentence, it raises some concern, but it looks like he'll be fine this time around.
Michael Hoecht, who has been slowly but surely ramping up in his return from a torn Achilles, is a candidate to play on Thursday, something he and Brady will talk about after practice.
"He's gonna take a lot of reps (on Tuesday) and then we'll talk after practice," Brady said. "But I know he's a guy that would love to get out there and get on the field and be able to get some contact and hit on Thursday. And it's a matter of, is that the best thing for him as we kind of come away from today."
Here's the list of players who won't be taking part in practice on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Alaina Getzenberg .
OL Sedrick Van Pran-Granger C Connor McGovern OL Jude Bowry RB Ty Johnson WR Keon Coleman WR Khalil Shakir DT Ed Oliver OLB Javon Solomon ILB Terrel Bernard ILB Joe Andreessen S C.J. Gardner-Johnson
The new addition there is inside linebacker Joe Andreessen, who was not listed among the absent players on Monday.
Brady addressed the Bills' injuries along the offensive line and said he didn't envision any of them impacting the team's 53-man roster decisions, which will come down on Aug. 30.
When asked about the concern about the lack of practice time Gardner-Johnson and Cole Bishop have gotten together, which defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard expressed at least some concern about on Monday, Brady said he wouldn't use concern as the word to describe how he views things.
"I don't know if concern is the right word," he said. "But, yeah, the reality is you're in a new defense and between Maxwell (Hairston), Cole, C.J., you haven't had some of your starters in there on a consistent basis, but C.J's played a lot of football."
"It's really just the communication," he added. "We know they all can play the techniques and whatnot... are they all on the same page speaking, both verbally and non-verbally."
As far as running back Ty Johnson is concerned, Brady would not commit to him being ready for Week 1, but the Bills head coach is encouraged with the progress he has made thus far.
The Bills are hitting the practice field on Tuesday and will then turn their attention to the preseason finale against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night.

title: Joe Brady Makes Josh Allen Decision as 'Some Starters' Will Play Preseason Finale
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills close out their preseason schedule at home against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday, August 27, and they're going to need more than third-stringers to get through the game.
"The reality of it is you can't sit every starter. We gotta go out and play a football game," said Bills' rookie head coach Joe Brady on Tuesday morning in Orchard Park.
With two quarterbacks locked in a fierce battle for backup duties , however, Brady can comfortably sit franchise field general Josh Allen for the preseason finale.
"Josh will not be playing Thursday," said Brady.
After engineering two scoring drives in the August 15 opener , Allen was inactive for the August 22 road game against the Cleveland Browns.
While he won't see any live reps on Thursday, Allen will most definitely hone in on the action.
"He'll be right there with me [on the sideline]," said Brady. "Hopefully, I'll let him call some plays, maybe, on Thursday. He wants it all the time."
Allen, who referred to himself as an "explosive play caller," isn't convinced that he'll have the chance to make some calls while wearing a headset against the Steelers.
"We'll see. He talks a big game. He's promised me that the last few years, and it hasn't happened yet, so we'll see," said the franchise quarterback after Tuesday's practice.
Allen did not see any preseason game reps last summer, but it was apparently important for the five-time NFL MVP finalist to go through at least one dress rehearsal in the Bills' new stadium.
With the opener being at home, the Preseason Week 1 matchup against the Carolina Panthers provided the ideal opportunity for a dry run for the 30-year-old Allen.
"When guys do play in Week 1, if something were to happen in Week 1, there is more time for recovery. There's a lot that kinda goes into it," said Brady. "I know the first time of us going into that stadium, I didn't want the first time him walking in there just walking in there just to kind of be there. I wanted him to see himself kind of playing, and I thought he did a really job good with it."
Allen, who has more total touchdowns (301) than any player ever in his first eight seasons, has met Brady's expectations this summer.
"I love how he's spinning it, how's he's playing football right now. He's obviously the leader of our football team," said Brady. "Josh is in a really good place."
With multiple position battles still unsettled, the Bills will presumably use Thursday's exhibition as a final evaluation. Here's what we learned from Buffalo's snap counts last time out .
"There will be some guys that are starters that are gonna be playing in the game Who that is? That's gonna be a thing we're gonna talk through after today's practice," said Brady.
Alec Anderson and Austin Corbett, who are fighting for the starting left guard job , appear likely to see snaps against the Steelers.
Meanwhile, the competition between quarterbacks Kyle Allen and Shane Buechele will most certainly take center stage on Thursday.
"You're gonna see both of them on Thursday. Both of them played really good football. I have such confidence calling the game with them," said Brady.

title: Bills' Defensive Coordinator Jim Leonhard Expresses Concern With Buffalo's Secondary
full_text:
If you're a Buffalo Bills fan who has a concern about the secondary going into the 2026 season, just know you are not alone because even defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard is worried.
Leonhard's concern doesn't have anything to do with the talent in the group, but rather the lack of reps the secondary has gotten together this offseason due to injuries.
Of course, a lack of reps together could lead to communication and other issues, something Leonhard touched on before the team's practice on Monday.
"It's still concerning to me just the whole secondary because it has been limited snaps with everybody, right?" Leonhard said . "We had that in the offseason with the safeties being out, and now in camp, it's the same thing.
"Cole's (Bishop) missed time, C.J.'s (Gardner-Johnson) missed time, Max (Hairston) has been out for a lot. So, it's more just how they gel and how they communicate and continuing to build up reps here, from now until Houston. It's always concerning when you're not banking those reps with what you'd probably consider to be the starting group out there. But, it is what it is," he added.
Thankfully for the Bills, they are now mostly healthy in the secondary as the third preseason game approaches.
Dorian Strong remains on the non-football injury list with his neck issue. Gardner-Johnson suffered calf strain on Aug. 1 that forced his early exit from practice, he returned days later but suffered another injury after that.
While he isn't practicing, Gardner-Johnson has been present and was spotted riding a stationary bike a few days ago, so he looks to be progressing and could be nearing his return, although that has not been confirmed yet. There hasn't been any indication he's in danger of missing Week 1.
What makes the secondary's lack of reps together even more concerning is that there isn't a ton of familiarity in the group to begin with.
After all, Buffalo overhauled its unit in a big way this offseason, with the team subtracting Taron Johnson, Taylor Rapp, Dane Jackson and Tre'Davious White.
Gardner-Johnson is a new addition to the secondary, as is Geno Stone, Dee Alford, Davison Igbinosun, Jalon Kilgore and Toriano Pride Jr., with the latter three being picked up in the 2026 NFL Draft.
How this group ultimately gels remains to be seen, but Leonhard's concern isn't going to make Bills fans feel any better about things.

title: Buffalo Bills' 53-Man Roster Prediction Entering Preseason Week 3
full_text:
Week 2 of the NFL preseason is behind us and the Buffalo Bills are coming off another impressive win. This Saturday, they defeated the Cleveland Browns 31-7 and had players all throughout the depth chart show they can help contribute to an NFL team .
Still, there are only 53 spots available, so there will surely be some talented players who get waived ahead of the season opener. There is still time for those on the bubble to make an impact, but with the preseason finale coming on Thursday against the Pittsburgh Steelers, time is running low.
With only one exhibition game remaining, here's a prediction for the Bills' 53-man roster, which includes Buffalo exposing some talented players to waivers.
Notable cuts : Shane Buechele
Kyle Allen has silenced the doubters with a strong preseason performance. He's proven to be a quality QB2 and forces Shane Buechele off the roster, even though Buechele has also played very well .
Notable cuts: Frank Gore Jr., Ian Wheeler, Jackson Acker
Keeping Ian Wheeler as the primary backup to James Cook is incredibly tempting after his preseason performance, especially when considering the salary savings if they kept him over Ty Johnson. In the end, the Bills will probably play it safe and hope Wheeler and Frank Gore Jr. will be available for the practice squad.
Notable cuts: Trent Sherfield PUP: Tyrell Shavers
Mecole Hardman had a couple of drops in Week 2, which opened the door for Trent Sherfield who stood out against the Browns. As impressive as he was, Hardman's ability to help on returns helps since the WR6 won't be asked to do much outside of special teams.
There's not much drama here, since the Bills have three starting-caliber tight ends. Keleki Latu is one to watch after an impressive offseason. Buffalo might need to find a spot for him, since other teams will be interested should he hit waivers.
Notable cuts : Ar'Maj Reed-Adams, Sedrick Van Pran-Granger
Alec Anderson starts the year as the starter at left guard, while the rest of the O-line remains the same. The only change would be if Connor McGovern's injury lingers into the preseason, at which point, Lloyd Cushenberry would be the starter. Jude Bowry struggled in the win over Cleveland, but he's still a lock.
Notable cuts : DeWayne Carter Suspended: Phidarian Mathis
This might be the most concerning group on the depth chart and even the addition of Greg Gaines did little to improve things this weekend. Don't be surprised if the Bills keep a close eye on nose tackles who hit the waiver wire.
Mike Danna has the experience edge, but Javon Solomon has flashed enough to warrant a spot on the 53-man roster. He won't be heavy in the rotation with the talent ahead of him, but Solomon could be a special teams ace and has looked far more comfortable in Jim Leonhard's defense.
Notable cuts: Keonta Jenkins
Joe Andreesen had a game to remember against the Browns, which puts him back in control for the fourth and final spot at inside linebacker. Keonta Jenkins has proven to be a capable player, so he could still change this during the next week.
Notable cuts: Toriano Pride Jr., Te'Cory Couch
Undrafted free agent Kani Walker makes the team as does second-year player Jordan Hancock. What really helps Hancock make it is his versatility to play both corner and safety.
Notable cuts : Geno Stone, Jordan Dunbar
Damar Hamlin gave up a big play, but also had an interception this weekend. He edges out Geno Stone, although that could go either way. In the end, the coaching staff seems higher on Hamlin.
Notable cuts : Mitch Wishnowsky
Tyler Bass connected on a 52-yarder, but it barely made it through the uprights. The concerns surrounding him won't go away yet, but the Bills are sold. He's joined by rookie punter Tommy Doman and returning long snapper Reid Ferguson.

title: Bills Finally Receive Positive News on Injured Rookies Skyler Bell, Jalon Kilgore
full_text:
Fresh off an impressive 31-7 road victory over the Cleveland Browns during the team’s second preseason game, the Buffalo Bills returned to practice in Orchard Park on Monday morning as preparations for the regular season continue.
And, with Thursday night’s final preseason outing against the Pittsburgh Steelers just around the corner at the new Highmark Stadium prior to Sunday’s roster cut-down day, the Bills still have plenty of critical decisions left to make .
So far this summer Buffalo has been somewhat slammed by a lengthy injury report , particularly as of late , which has made the evaluation process a little harder for first-year head coach Joe Brady and general manager Brandon Beane.
Even still, the team has been impressive in its two exhibition matchups this month as the Bills have outscored their opponents 60-21.
We wrote about the 10 players who did not practice on Monday, including four new additions to the injury list .
But, be that as it may, on Monday there was actually also a bit of good news for Buffalo as rookie wide receiver Skyler Bell and rookie defensive back Jalon Kilgore returned to the practice field after a somewhat lengthy stay on the sidelines this month, especially for Bell, who hadn’t practiced since before the team’s “Return of the Blue and Red” scrimmage on Saturday, August 8. Fellow receiver Dante Pettis also returned to action after missing the preseason game against Cleveland .
Despite some important players still being out, it’s at least a good sign for Bell and Kilgore, two players who were once thought to possibly have fairly large roles during their rookie seasons in Western New York.
Not practicing today for the Bills: Sedrick Van Pran-Granger Connor McGovern Jude Bowry Ty Johnson Keon Coleman Khalil Shakir Ed Oliver Javon Solomon Terrel Bernard CJ Gardner-Johnson Returning: Jalon Kilgore, Dante Pettis, Skyler Bell
Kilgore will still presumably be stuck behind fellow safeties Cole Bishop and C.J. Gardner-Johnson for most of the season, but Bell has a chance to reclaim a top role this year that many thought was going to be his in Buffalo after he was drafted by the team earlier this spring.
Fellow wideouts Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir remained out with injuries on Monday, which means the 2026 fourth-rounder out of University of Connecticut can make up some ground during the team’s final preseason game against Pittsburgh in just a few days.
The 5-foot-11, 192-pounder finished second in the entire FBS for receiving yardage during his senior collegiate season in 2025 for the Huskies by racking up 1,278 receiving yards and 13 receiving touchdowns on 101 receptions.
He has the talent: there’s a reason why the Bills selected him early on Day 3 of this April’s draft.
But, Bell was hampered by a hamstring injury during the spring, and the injury bug subsequently followed him into the summer as he’s been dealing with a separate groin issue lately.
However, the fact that he was able to finally return to action after more than two weeks away due to the ailment is definitely a sight for sore eyes amongst the coaches and the fanbase.
Now, it’s just a matter of Bell getting quickly back up to speed in order to contribute when the regular season rolls around.
The game against Houston will be here quicker than anyone realizes, so fans will have to keep a close eye on how things progress with the rookie moving forward.

title: Bills' History, Roster Underdog's Play Suggest Fullback Remains in Joe Brady's Plans
full_text:
They've been an endangered species in NFL circles for more than a decade now, but the Buffalo Bills have bucked the trend.
The Bills are one of the few teams who haven't, even partially, abandoned the fullback.
Whether it was former Pro Bowler Pat DiMarco for the first three years of general manager Brandon Beane's tenure or Reggie Gilliam for the next six seasons, the Bills have consistently kept a fullback in their arsenal. It's worth noting that Buffalo employed four different offensive coordinators over the aforementioned nine-year span, and the fullback position survived every change.
Needing to identify a replacement for Gilliam , who left in free agency, the Bills entered training camp with two fullbacks on the 90-man roster.
When they cut undrafted rookie Jackson Acker, leaving converted linebacker Ben VanSumeren as the only fullback on the 90-man roster, however, it raised the question of whether or not a fullback would be in the team's regular season plans .
"I would have loved to have kept two even through this point, but with some of the injury situations, some of the moves, it was unfortunate that we had to make a move," said rookie head coach Joe Brady. "We're still evaluating is it a position and a role that we'll be able to have on our football team."
During the 2025 season with Brady as the offensive coordinator, the Bills deployed Gilliam for 21 percent of the offense's snaps. Brady made it a point to highlight Gilliam's value on two separate occasions last summer with his comments suggesting an appreciation for the position.
The Bills took a hard look at VanSumeren during the August 22 preseason road game against the Cleveland Browns.
Buffalo used a fullback on 19 offensive snaps , equating to 32 percent of the time, and VanSumeren proved valuable in the run game.
"Ben has a great mentality of the way that he plays football, and he's still learning the position," said Brady. "The more opportunities he has at it, the more he has an opportunity to display if that can be a vision and a role for him."
If the Bills are to use a roster spot for a fullback, it will almost certainly come with the expectation of contributing to the kicking and return units. In a positive sign, VanSumeren logged a team-high 16 special teams reps against the Browns.
It's worth noting that Bills' new offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael kept a fullback in his arsenal when coaching quarterback Drew Brees and the New Orleans Saints.
The Saints gave Heath Evans a heavy volume of reps, especially in the run game, during the 2009 and 2010 seasons with Carmichael serving as offensive coordinator under Sean Payton.
Next, Jed Collins played more than 30 percent of snaps for the Saints from 2011 through 2013.
Add it all up, and VanSumeren is no longer a roster long shot.

title: Six Bills' Questions Still Lingering With Six Days Until Final Roster Cuts
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills had a busy few days last week— for many reasons —but in the midst of it all the team managed to come together for a 31-7 victory over the Cleveland Browns to move its preseason record to 2-0 under first-year head coach Joe Brady.
And, despite a bit of a slow start defensively , the Bills were quite dominant during their outing with the Browns at Huntington Bank Field on Saturday afternoon, which was clearly evidenced by the lopsided victory.
Even still, there are some things left unanswered from Brady’s squad as Buffalo prepares this week for its final preseason game with the Pittsburgh Steelers at the new Highmark Stadium on Thursday at 7 p.m. ET in Orchard Park, New York.
Final roster cuts must be made by August 30, so the matchup with Pittsburgh will loom large for a few of the veterans currently on the roster fringe.
Here are six questions that must be answered by the Bills before September rolls around in the coming days.
Like seemingly every summer, there have been more than a few surprise players thus far in training camp for the Bills that have made a positive impression.
Most of the time, however, those fan favorites tend to fade away come final roster cut-down day. Will that happen again this time around when the deadline approaches on August 30? Or will some of these stellar summer standouts hold onto a 53-man roster spot?
Bills Mafia will have to wait and find out after Buffalo’s upcoming game with Pittsburgh, but some names to monitor are rookie cornerback Kani Walker , former undrafted veteran linebackers Joe Andreessen and Keonta Jenkins, as well as receivers Mecole Hardman Jr., Dante Pettis, and Trent Sherfield Sr., who made his presence felt against the Browns in a major way by raking in a game-high four catches for 54 yards.
Veteran fullback Ben VanSumeren is also one player who fans should keep a close eye on over the next few days.
Honestly, for as much flak as these two players caught from fans and outside observers heading into training camp, both Kyle Allen and Shane Buechele have performed quite admirably for the majority of this summer.
The two backups had a slightly shaky start to camp at St. John Fisher University in Pittsford, New York, but both Allen and Buechele have done fairly well since being back at One Bills Drive.
They’ve also held up their end of the bargain in the two preseason games, as well, which is showcased by the team’s 60-21 scoring differential in the exhibition contests against the Carolina Panthers and Cleveland Browns.
And, their most recent performances against the Browns might’ve been the best either player has ever looked while wearing a Bills’ uniform.
Allen finished his day 10-of-12 for 128 yards and one touchdown, while Buechele went 5-for-10 for 111 yards and one passing touchdown in addition to tallying a rushing touchdown.
If Allen doesn’t play at all on Thursday against the Steelers, then it’s likely that the backup quarterback role on Buffalo’s roster is his for 2026.
However, if he sees the field, then it’ll mean it’s still a competition. And, if that’s the case, then who knows?
Maybe Buechele can surprise everyone and earn the Bills’ No. 2 spot seemingly out of nowhere.
Coming into Bills’ training camp, it was thought by many that 2025 second-round pick T.J. Sanders was going to assume the third starting defensive lineman role alongside fellow defenders Ed Oliver and Deone Walker this season in the team’s new 3-4 scheme under first-year NFL defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard .
However, it’s been a hot-and-cold summer so far from the former South Carolina Gamecock, and he hasn’t taken a firm grasp of the opportunity that was put before him by the Bills at the start of camp at St. John Fisher University .
Instead, somewhat shockingly, it’s been fellow second-year defensive lineman Landon Jackson who has seemingly stolen the spotlight away from Sanders through this portion of August.
It’s been a pleasant surprise from Jackson, to say the least, and it has put immense pressure on Sanders to step up in a big way over this final stretch before Week 1 rolls around on September 13.
It’ll be interesting to see if Jackson completes his hijacking of the vacant starting job, or if Sanders can reclaim relevancy on the roster for 2026.
Every offseason around this time, the thought comes around from fans that team president/ general manager Brandon Beane will be able to pull off some “ Beane After Dark ” magic and slyly trade away a few players to unsuspecting teams around the league in return for draft compensation instead of having to trim those same players from the final 53-man roster on cut-down day.
I mean, he’s done it before . . . remember former Bills’ offensive lineman Russell Bodine, anyone?
Anyway, be that as it may—while those types of moves are few and far between—the thought still remains the same this summer.
Some names to keep in mind are veteran interior offensive linemen Sedrick Van Pran-Granger and Chase Lundt, safeties Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone, as well as running back Ty Johnson, who has failed to practice since August 8 due to a soft-tissue injury, which has created quite the pathway for players like Frank Gore Jr. and Ian Wheeler to make some noise this preseason.
Let’s watch these possible developments closely, shall we?
Like with the backup quarterbacks that were previously mentioned, there are many other undecided roster battles ongoing in Western New York this month.
And, they’re at critical starting positions, nonetheless.
Starting spots at left guard , inside linebacker , and punter are all seemingly still without a winner, and the regular season starts in less than three weeks.
It’s getting time for head coach Joe Brady to start making some tough decisions.
This was a question that was also posed last week from us over here at Bills ON SI, but it’s still lingering: where are new defensive/offensive coordinators Jim Leonhard and Pete Carmichael Jr. going to be during the games this regular season?
Will they both be in the box? On the sideline beside head coach Joe Brady?
Well, so far the two coaches have split their time between the booth and the sideline during the first two preseason games, so it will be interesting to see which way they lean for the final exhibition game against the Steelers on Thursday.
Presumably, one would think that after doing one of each against Carolina and Cleveland, that the two coaches would choose their preferred destination for this third game in order to get one final true test run against Pittsburgh before the regular season starts in September.

title: Panthers Should Keep Tabs on Chiefs Player Who Might Get Cut
full_text:
The deadline for NFL teams to have their rosters reduced to 53 players is 6:00 pm on Sunday, August 30. There will certainly be some surprises, per usual.
Gary Davenport of Bleacher Report picked out a half-dozen players that could wind up being available to teams after clubs make their cuts. One happened to be a former second-round draft choice who has now played for three different franchises the since 2023.
Cornerback Kristian Fulton was the 61st overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft by the Tennessee Titans. In four seasons and a total of 44 contests with the club (including playoffs), he totaled four interceptions, one sack, a fumble recovery and was credited with 25 passes defensed.
The former LSU standout signed a one-year deal with the Chargers in 2024 and enjoyed a solid year for Jim Harbaugh’s playoff-bound team. There was a personal-best 51 tackles and one pick. Fulton was on the move again last offseason, inking a two-year, $20 million contract with the Kansas City Chiefs.
Injuries proved to be a big factor as he was limited to only eight games (his fewest since his rookie season in 2020) and only two starts. He finished with 16 defensive stops and six passes defensed. Could he be the odd man out in a crowded Chiefs’ cornerback room?
“ Fulton wasn't terrible when he was on the field, ” explained Davenport. “His 81.7 passer rating against was his best since 2021—but he played just 208 snaps in his first season in Kansas City. And a $13 million cap hit is a lot for a subpackage corner.”
The reigning NFC South champions own one of the better secondaries in the league . The unit is led by one of the top cornerback tandems in the NFL. Jaycee Horn was named to his second Pro Bowl in 2025 and led the team with a career-best five interceptions.
Seven-year pro Mike Jackson has started every game for Carolina since being acquired by trade from Seattle in 2024. He has a total of seven interceptions, including a pick of Rams’ quarterback Matthew Stafford in January’s playoff clash.
OUR BALL Chau Smith-Wade with the INT 📺: WSOC 📻  : @997TheFox 📲 : In-market in the Panthers app pic.twitter.com/t83TGbwSqX
Other key member of the Panthers’ cornerback room include Corey Thornton (3 interceptions in 2025) and Chau Smith-Wade (interception return for TD in Week 3 vs. Falcons), while GM Dan Morgan used a fourth-round pick in April on Texas A&M’s Will Lee III. Is there room on Ejiro Evero’s defensive unit for a six-year pro who also has some playoff experience on his resume? Of course, Fulton has to hit the open market first.

title: One Trade Panthers Must Make to Address LB Concerns Before Preseason Ends
full_text:
The preseason is often about two things. First, it's about getting players important reps against NFL-level competition. Second, it's about learning, both about individual players and the team itself.
In that regard, we have learned a lot about the team: where Carolina's strengths lie, where the weaknesses have come up, where depth is and is not, what plays work, how well newcomers have meshed, and more.
One thing has become abundantly clear in all of this learning, though. The Panthers have exactly one viable linebacker on the roster, and it's Devin Lloyd . The problem is, they need two for a starting lineup . A trade might have to happen.
The Panthers badly need another linebacker, and it could be a good time to get one. For starters, there are some free agents, like Bobby Okereke or Bobby Wagner, still available, and signing one would be smart.
Those are, however, lackluster options. There's a reason no one has bothered to sign them less than a month from the opening week. They'd be decent additions in Carolina, but they won't fix the problem.
A trade, however, might, especially for players who could be getting cut soon. The Panthers would have all the leverage in that situation, and they could use it to sneak Ivan Pace Jr. away from the Minnesota Vikings.
FanSided's Zachary Rotman and Mark Powell wrote, "He recorded 102 tackles as a rookie in 2023, but missed time in 2024 due to injury and was only on the field for 30 percent of the team's defensive snaps in 2025...Pace can still make the team, [but] Minnesota could choose to go in another direction."
If the Vikings are going to cut Pace Jr., then they'd probably be thrilled with a sixth- or seventh-round draft pick from the Panthers. That's a low price to pay for the Panthers to fix their biggest issue and ensure they don't have competition to sign him on the open market or waivers.
Other options include Patrick Queen (though he's very expensive), Marist Liufau (who recently transitioned from ILB to EDGE, sadly), Blake Cashman, Pete Werner, and more. However, Pace Jr. probably makes the most sense out of all the options.
The Panthers could then start Pace opposite Devin Lloyd, moving both Trevin Wallace and Claudin Cherilus, who are waging the most uninteresting camp battle perhaps in the entire NFL, to the bench as backups, which is a much better situation for both players.

title: Why Jonathon Brooks is Among NFL's Biggest Week 2 Preseason Winners
full_text:
While the Carolina Panthers ' offseason has been defined by new additions and looming pressure on Bryce Young , one of the league's most inspirational stories in the league is still developing. One major question for the Panthers' offense is how the backfield will look after Rico Dowdle departed for Pittsburgh.
Chuba Hubbard is expected to be the lead back in 2026, reprising the bell-cow role he excelled in during 2024, but another RB has been grinding behind the scenes and is now ready to return to football.
Jonathon Brooks has had a tumultuous NFL career thus far. Drafted in 2024, the former Texas running back tore his ACL with the Longhorns in 2023, before being selected with the 46th pick overall. Brooks then tore his ACL once again in 2024, during his rookie season, while playing against the Eagles.
Now Brooks is trending back towards being a key piece of this Panthers offense and deserves all the credit in the world.
CBS Sports' analysts Zachary Pereles and Garrett Podell dropped their list of preseason Week 2 winners and losers on Sunday, and rightfully featured Brooks. Carolina's former second-round pick walked in a 1-yard rushing touchdown in a dominant victory against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
The score was Brooks' first since November 11th, 2023, when he was still in a Texas uniform playing for the Longhorns. Brooks even did his signature touchdown celebration for the first time in almost three years, pointing to his right forearm tattoo that honors his father, and making a heart with his hands.
This might as well be the definition of a feel-good story within sports, and while it's just preseason, Brooks' presence on the field is still a major leap in the right direction.
Now the focus is on putting together a full season of productivity, because the Panthers will need Brooks to relieve pressure from Bryce Young and the passing game.
Coming back from two ACL tears and creating a productive career isn't something that hasn't been done before. The most notable example of someone who has is Frank Gore. Tearing his ACL twice at Miami, Gore went on to have one of the longest NFL RB careers ever, remaining productive until he was 37 years old.
With RB1 Chuba Hubbard still recovering from a hamstring injury , theres a good chance that Brooks will see a large workload in Week 1, along with other RBs like AJ Dillon.

title: Dear Panthers: Stop Messing Around and Just Start Darren Waller
full_text:
As preseason and training camp are beginning to wind down, roster spots are being finalized , positional battles are being won, and guys are finding their roles. The Carolina Panthers added some more competition to the tight ends room on August 17th, signing former Pro Bowl tight end Darren Waller .
This move brings another body into the tight ends room and can add another element to this Panthers offense that looks to take another step forward. Well, that is, if Waller makes the roster, which is still not a guarantee at the moment.
Waller will continue to stake his claim throughout this week, as the August 30th cut date looms large. The resume he has is a great start, but it's fair for Dave Canales, and Brad Idzik to see what they have in the building since Waller is on the older side at 33 years old.
That being said, let's not kid ourselves into thinking Waller has real competition from a pass-catching perspective.
Is Waller the best blocking tight end? No, as far as Carolina's room specifically, that title would likely be held by Mitchell Evans, who stands 6'5 and weighs almost 260 pounds. As a pass catcher, it's not even close, though. In 2025, Waller signed with the Miami Dolphins midseason and played 9 games.
In just nine games, Waller posted more receiving yards than any individual Carolina tight end, with 283. Waller also totaled more touchdowns than the entire Panthers tight ends room combined, with 6, while Mitchell Evans, Tommy Tremble, and Ja'Tavion Sanders combined for 5.
Waller is still getting acclimated to Carolina's system and with Bryce Young, but even just watching him run routes and catch passes, it feels clear that he has an extra gear in that department than anyone else in the room.
More Waller individual reps. pic.twitter.com/50sFK8sOr6
Carolina needs another true red zone threat, a bigger body who can go up and snag the ball and come down with a touchdown catch. Waller brings that, along with better vertical speed and a more diverse route tree than the other tight ends can offer.
Waller finished the 2025 season with the second-highest PFF grade for receiving amongst tight ends, posting an 87.6, only trailing George Kittle.
There's no reason that a talent like Waller, even at his advanced age, can't start for the Panthers at tight end and become a security-blanket-type pass catcher for Young. There's already no reliability within the tight ends room right now, so Carolina might as well see what they have in Waller.

title: Carolina Panthers’ 53-Man Roster Projection After Blowout Win vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have one more week of preseason action to determine which players will and will not make the roster. The final cut day is looming, and it could be a painful one. The Panthers just wallopped the Jacksonville Jaguars , so where do things stand now?
Here's the 53-man roster projection as of now:
It's time to admit that AJ Dillon has a very strong case to make the final roster. He has arguably looked the best of the running backs. It will come at the cost of Ja'seem Reed, who has looked good but hasn't stood out on special teams like other WRs.
Trevor Etienne can be used as a receiving back to make up for taking one fewer wide receiver. Little else has changed here. Of course, Darren Waller has yet to play, but we have to assume the Panthers didn't sign him to cut him weeks later and roll with the clearly underwhelming TE room.
Here's the projection on defense:
For now, Aaron Hall remains just ahead of Elijah Garcia on the cut line, but it's close. That battle has swung back and forth and could still do so this weekend in the final preseason game. Corey Thornton has been thoroughly outplayed by Chau Smith-Wade, and his roster spot might be in jeopardy.
Isaiah Simmons had another good preseason game, this time on defense as well as special teams. The hybrid, versatile defender is all but assured of a spot on this roster Week 1.
As for special teams, JJ Jansen, Sam Martin, and Ryan Fitzgerald will take up their usual long snapper, punter, and kicker spots. There's no competition for any of them.

title: Dave Canales May Have Just Hinted at Haynes King's Roster Status with Panthers
full_text:
After practice on Monday, ahead of the final Carolina Panthers' joint practice and preseason game this week, Dave Canales offered a slew of updates on missing players.
Devin Lloyd didn't practice, but that was simply a veteran rest day. He's fine. Xavier Legette is out, and he will be in a boot until Thursday, but he's also fine. He won't play on Friday, though.
Canales: -Devin Lloyd vet day -Legette (foot) in boot til Thursday -Haynes King and Chuba Hubbard trending toward playing Week 1
Chuba Hubbard has been nursing a hamstring injury, and he's still out, but Canales believes he will be ready for Week 1. And in perhaps the most interesting news to Panthers fans, Canales said the exact same thing about Haynes King .
Haynes King suffered a hamstring injury late in the comeback win over the Arizona Cardinals all the way back in the Hall of Fame Game. It has bothered him throughout the rest of training camp, and he hasn't practiced or played since walking off the Cardinals on a literal last-second TD.
That seemed to put his chances of making the roster in less-than-ideal territory . Was one game, a truly meaningless game, against backups of backups for a team projected to be the worst in the NFL enough?
King looked great in that game. He looked like he belonged on an NFL field, but the trouble is, he quite literally hasn't been on the field since, and it's hard to know whether or not he's worth a roster spot as a third quarterback.
That spot could go to a seventh wide receiver, a fourth running back, an extra lineman, another defensive backup, or someone who, in other words, will actually see the field more than a third QB.
But based on Canales' comments, he seems to be implying that King is going to be on the roster and will be healthy for Week 1. Of course, he could be saying this just as a timeline update, not revealing his and Dan Morgan's plan, but that makes less sense.
He knows what King brings to the table, and he knows how he might be able to use him. Things can change in a week and this certainly isn't confirmation, but it sure looks like King is trending towards a roster spot.
That is ultimately a good thing, but it is unfortunate that a hurt player is going to take a roster spot from someone who might have played well in all four games by this time next week.

title: How the Panthers' Vaunted Secondary Stacks Up in NFL
full_text:
The reigning NFC South champions will play their final preseason game of 2026 on Friday when they host the Houston Texans. It’s the lone home contest of the summer for Dave Canales’s club, who owns a 2-1 record in its first three summertime tilts.
Last week, the staff at Pro Football Focus ranked the league’s 32 secondaries for 2026. The defending AFC champion New England Patriots own the top spot, with the Miami Dolphins bringing up the rear. Canales’s Carolina Panthers can be found in the middle of the pack at No. 14.
Mike Jackson intercepts Matthew Stafford for a Pick-6! LARvsCAR on FOX/FOX One https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/J2yeGsyNZK
“Carolina’s starting cornerback duo of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson is one of the best in football. We know all about Horn’s ability, but Jackson’s 85.8 PFF coverage grade was the second-best among cornerbacks last season, helped by his five interceptions. Carolina played the most zone coverage of any defense last season.”
Those five picks include a theft of Rams’ quarterback Matthew Stafford in Carolina’s home playoff loss to Sean McVay’s club. You may also recall that Jackson picked off the 2025 NFL MVP during a regular-season victory over the Rams in Week 13, returning the interception 48 yards for a score in the Panthers’ 31-28 victory. Meanwhile, Horn finished with a career-best five interceptions and was named to the Pro Bowl for the second consecutive year.
There was also positive news elsewhere in the defensive backfield. “At safety,” added the Pro Football Focus staff, “Tre’von Moehrig was tied for the most tackles for loss or no gain among defensive backs (12). His 17 pressures were also the second-most of any safety.”
In his first season in Charlotte, Moehrig finished third on the team with 103 tackles . He also totaled three sacks, seven quarterback hits, and one interception. The former Las Vegas Raiders also add three stops in the playoff loss to the Rams.
So what about Moehrig’s counterpart at the other safety spot? Oddly, there was no mention by PFF regarding a fourth member of the starting secondary. This past season, veteran Nick Scott started all 17 regular-season games and finished second on the club with a career-high 109 defensive stops. He also amassed nine tackles in the wild card loss to the Rams. However, he managed only two takeaways and totaled just three passes defensed in 18 total contests.
Zakee Wheatley— continuing to make impacts play in the open field. Unfortunate non-recovery there. pic.twitter.com/OH3wSNVd3p
On the other hand, 2026 fifth-round pick Zakee Wheatley has seen plenty of action in three preseason outings, totaling a combined 18 tackles, along with a forced fumble. He led the team in stops vs. the Panthers (8) and Bills (7), and added three more tackles in the recent victory over the Jaguars. While the rookie defender got the starting nod in the Hall of Fame Game, Scott was in the opening lineup vs. Buffalo and Jacksonville.
Regardless, the Panthers’ defensive backfield is ranked in the upper half of the league. Perhaps a big year from either Scott or Wheatley (or both) could push this group further up the charts.

title: The Good and Not So Good from Panthers' Monday Practice: Jimmy Horn Jr.'s Chances
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers wrapped up practice on Monday, the final week of preparation before the last preseason game this Friday. For many, it's now or never, and stringing together good practices to close out camp as Week 1 inches closer is paramount.
But as usual, there were some good things and some not so good things in the Panthers' practice.
Practice ends with a Corey Thornton pick of Pickett. Thornton had dropped a potential INT a few plays earlier.
Corey Thornton is not only trending towards losing his job, but some have predicted that he won't even make the roster. He's had a rough summer, but today he bounced back. It's now or never for Thornton, and he closed practice with what some have referred to as his best play yet. Putting in good practices and a good preseason finale can change his fate.
Canales says if the starters get enough work in Wednesday’s joint practice, they will likely not play in Friday’s game. #Panthers
Dave Canales has seen his team come out flat to open the season twice in a row, and he hasn't really learned. The head coach has given the Panthers' starters more run thus far, but he may not let them play at all in the finale, though not for health. He said it will depend on how they do in joint practice . Either they need to play for the reps (which is likely), or it's not worth the health risk. Choose one.
Jimmy Horn just scored in seven on seven … and celebrated by doing a front flip.
Jimmy Horn Jr. has found himself in a muddled competition for the final few wide receiver spots. Whether the Panthers take six or seven receivers, Horn isn't guaranteed a spot on the roster. He has put in the work, though he hasn't excelled as a receiver yet. Today, he made a great play and celebrated accordingly because he has likely given himself a boost towards making the final 53.
Chuba Hubbard is expected to be ready by Week One; hit 20mph on Return-to-Play last week. Haynes King will not return for the preseason finale on Friday. #Panthers
Let's all hope the Hall of Fame Game was enough, because Haynes King is unlikely to return to the field this weekend. Not playing will hurt his chances of making the roster, even though Dave Canales might've hinted that he expects him to make the roster. He can do nothing towards that, though, and is fully at the mercy of the staff after one preseason game against the backups of backups . It's not ideal.
“I wouldn’t want to put him in a game setting after practicing for a week,” Canales on Darren Waller. He said they have to lean on his recent history because it’s hard to get an evaluation on a week in practice. He likely won’t play Friday but will be sprinkled in against…
Like Haynes King, let's all hope that Darren Waller's history and his impression in practice is enough, because he is unlikely to play on Friday. The veteran tight end was brought in to revitalize the tight end position, yet he hasn't played. That makes it hard to roster him, though the Panthers would probably be foolish not to.
