title: Play and Players of Day at Practice 15 of Training Camp (Bad News, Haters)
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The first play of Green Bay Packers training camp on Monday was a handoff to Josh Jacobs. Cornerback Brandon Cisse beat his man and was waiting for a tackle for loss.
The last sequence was a goal-line stand.
And so it went for about 2 hours. The 15th practice of Packers training camp was total domination by Jonathan Gannon’s defense. Starters, backups. It didn’t matter. So, naturally, our daily feature is defense-centric.
On third-and-8, impressive first-year quarterback Kyle McCord fired the ball downfield. Safety Kitan Oladapo, who has been playing mostly in the slot the last couple weeks, made a leaping interception.
“Just dropped to the curl-flat and Kyle was looking right at me. I don’t know why he actually threw it,” Oladapo said, unable to stifle a laugh.
The Packers drafted Oladapo in the fifth round in 2024. At the Scouting Combine, he posted a 36-inch vertical jump. That was while wearing shorts and gym shoes. There’s no way of knowing, obviously, but it seemed like a full-pads Oladapo jumped higher than that.
“Yeah, I’m a gamer. I’m not a good test-taker,” he said with a laugh.
The team held a closed practice on Sunday, Oladapo intercepted Tyrod Taylor in that one.
“I dropped down as a hook player and Tyrod play-actioned and tried to throw a dig and I just jumped up and I caught the dig,” Oladapo said.
“I probably got higher yesterday, I’m not going to lie,” he added. “I’m just glad to make the most of my opportunities.”
The starting cornerback tandem for Week 1 at Minnesota might be set. Brandon Cisse almost certainly will be one. Keisean Nixon probably will be the other.
With Benjamin St-Juste out with a hamstring injury, Nixon took all the No. 1 reps and had an excellent day.
First, Jordan Love went deep up the right sideline to Jayden Reed. Nixon had textbook coverage and swatted the pass aside with his left hand. Next, on fourth-and-10 in a 2-minute drill, the play broke down and Love extended the play to his right. With no good options, he threw one up but Nixon made a leaping interception.
Fine, but how about against the speed of Matthew Golden? Love went 0-for-2 on deep passes. On the first, Nixon walled off Golden so he couldn’t get to the ball; from afar, it seemed like Nixon might have been able to make a play on the ball rather than simply forcing an incompletion. A few plays later, Love tried it again but Nixon had excellent coverage and the ball fell harmlessly incomplete.
While Jonathan Gannon might be able to scheme up some pressures, it’s indisputable that the key to the opening stretch of games will be the ability of Lukas Van Ness to help replace some of Micah Parsons’ pass rush.
Van Ness has had some good days and some quiet days. This was a really good day.
It started with Van Ness stuffing a handoff to Josh Jacobs during the opening series of plays. In the passing game, Van Ness provided pressures against both of Green Bay’s tackles.
Against left tackle Jordan Morgan, he ducked underneath Morgan and got to Jordan Love. Love hit Matthew Golden for a big gain near the sideline, but Van Ness might have had a sack.
Later, during a 2-minute drill, Van Ness beat Morgan again to force a throwaway. A couple plays later, on third-and-10, Van Ness tossed premier right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele at the feet of Love, which resulted in an errant checkdown to MarShawn Lloyd.
“It’s been awesome,” he said last week. “I’ve really enjoyed the defense. It’s putting us in a position to win and just a lot of different looks and fronts and schemes. We’re having fun. I’ve been happy with the way they’re utilizing me and I’m excited to see how I can grow.”
The tone-setters of the defense will be the elite linebacker tandem of Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin. They’ve seemingly traded dominant days all summer, with Monday being Cooper’s turn.
During the starters’ second set of plays, Cooper broke up a pass over the middle to tight end Tucker Kraft. Shortly thereafter, he ruined back-to-back plays for MarShawn Lloyd. First, Cooper didn’t buy any of the misdirection stuff in the backfield and tackled Lloyd for a loss. Next, on third-and-4, Jordan Love checked it down to Lloyd but Cooper stopped the play well short of the marker.
Later, Cooper set the edge on a perimeter run by Jacobs and teamed with Barryn Sorrell to make the play near the line of scrimmage.
Finally, during the starters’ last set of plays, Cooper almost intercepted a pass intended for Kraft on third-and-2. A couple plays later, Lloyd tried to bounce a run to the outside but Cooper was there in a blur.
“I just feel like with me and Coop, it’s really just being honest with each other, first and foremost, on what we both can be better at,” Franklin said last week. “And we hold each other accountable, which I think is a great thing.
“I think we both have a great energy. We both love football and we both just really enjoy playing. That always comes out. At the end of the day, whether I’m not really in a mood or he’s not in a mood, at the end of the day, we both love playing. And I think we always connect over our love of ball.”

title: Packers-Cardinals Fight? Matt LaFleur Has Fun Solution
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The final week of Green Bay Packers training camp begins with the second-to-last public practice of training camp on Monday. The main event of the summer will come on Wednesday with a joint practice against the Arizona Cardinals.
It will be a brother battle between longtime Packers coach Matt LaFleur and the Cardinals’ new coach, Mike LaFleur.
“It’s going to be a pretty cool experience,” LaFleur said at Lambeau Field before Monday’s practice. “It’s not the first time but it’s certainly the first time as head coaches. I talked to him last night, just trying to finalize the details and the plan for practice and look forward to seeing him.”
LaFleur tried to downplay coaching against his brother before finally admitting that it will be cool to work with his brother at Wednesday’s practice and against him during Friday’s final preseason game.
“I think it’s going to be pretty special but, at the end of the day, we’re just looking to try to get good work on both sides,” he said. “Certainly, always going to prioritize the Green Bay Packers but if there is another team in the National Football League that I’ll be rooting for, it will be the Arizona Cardinals.”
His parents will be there, of course.
“They’ll probably look like a Christmas tree, green and red,” LaFleur joked.
Mike LaFleur isn’t Matt LaFleur’s brother. He’s Mike LaFleur. Staying true to that has been an important part of his career, Matt LaFleur said.
“I think it’s a byproduct of a lot of things,” Matt said of his brother’s career path. “I’d say certainly, he’s never shied away from the work. He’s earned the opportunity, and then it’s also, we’ve both been fortunate to be around a lot of great people. This doesn’t happen unless you get those experiences and learn from some of the best in football. But it is cool to see him get his shot.”
Before practice, LaFleur discussed a handful of injuries.
Rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse, who has emerged as a likely starter, played only one series against Denver because of a knee injury, “should be good to go” this week, LaFleur said.
Second-year defensive tackle Warren Brinson was a surprise inactive against Denver.
“Yeah, it happened in warmups, he felt a little tweak in his calf. So, he’ll miss a little bit of time,” LaFleur said.
Long snapper Matt Orzech remains on PUP because of a calf injury. In his absence, rookie kicker Trey Smack has found a groove with Cal Adomitis doing the snapping.
“I think he’s getting closer,” LaFleur said. “To say he’ll be back this week, I think it might be too soon to say. But I know he’s getting close.”
Running back Josh Jacobs, who returned to individual drills last week following a calf injury, will take a step this week.
“He’ll be limited in all team periods, but he’ll be out there practicing,” LaFleur said.
Rookie receiver J. Michael Sturdivant remains in the concussion protocol, which will obviously hurt his chances of making a last-minute dash to a roster spot.
“He’s done a lot of good things,” LaFleur said. “What I really like about him is just doing all the little things, because I think it’s true with most young players, especially guys that are trying to carve out a role on this football team, it’s like, the more you can do. I think we’ve seen it in the run game, just how he goes out there and blocks. I think we’ve seen it on special teams, his ability to go out there and contribute.
“There’s going to be a lot of tough decisions though down the stretch.”
LaFleur has done a bunch of joint practices during his tenure. It’s a collaborative effort between the coaches to get the work done in a way that work for everybody.
“He’s quick to criticize everything that I put on the schedule,” LaFleur joked. “So, he’s like, ‘Why are we doing this? Why are we doing that? We never do this.’ And I was like, ‘All right, Mike, you’ve got all the answers.’ Nah, it’s been healthy, it’s been good. There’s been give and take on both sides, for sure.”
Joint practices can get chippy, especially with fewer ramifications in terms of NFL fines and suspensions. After all, it’s a practice and not a game.
LaFleur isn’t sure if the brother-vs.-brother nature of the practice will impact the teams’ behavior. However, in a carrot-and-stick approach, playing time will serve as LaFleur’s stick.
He punctuated his answer with a joke.
“It goes back to what we’ve been saying for years,” LaFleur said. “First of all, if there is an issue in practice – we’re not going to play everybody in the game, but if you don’t get your work in, you’re going to play in the game. And conversely, if you’re somebody that needs that work, to get those snaps so the whole world can see it, you’re going to be limited or not at all playing in the game.
“The second part of that is if there’s an issue, I’m going to tell the guys, ‘Hey, you come tag me in. They can tag in my brother. And we’ll throw down on the 50.’”

title: Ultimate Packers Longshot Anthony Campbell’s Journey Started in Jamaica
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It took about 2.5 seconds for Anthony Campbell to beat his blocker and sack Broncos quarterback Sam Ehlinger on Saturday.
Campbell’s path toward beating some incredible odds and potentially earning a spot on the Green Bay Packers’ 53-man roster has taken about half a lifetime.
Campbell was born in Kingston, Jamaica. Football was definitely not on his radar.
“I played a lot of different sports like soccer, rugby, track and cricket – a lot of sports,” he told Packers On SI recently. “I played more soccer. In middle school, when I moved over here in 2013 (or) ‘14, around there, I started playing soccer. I was a goalie back in Bartow, (Fla.), so that’s where it started off.
“And then in high school, a school resource officer, RIP Officer (Michael) Quinn – he died from cancer – but he seen me in the hallway walking around, he was like, ‘You should come play football for us.’”
Because of his background in soccer, Campbell started out as a kicker. As a sophomore, he started playing as a 215-pound defensive end.
“And my junior year, I started getting looks and offers and all that crazy stuff,” he said. “So, it’s been a big transition to football.”
There were a couple big detours along the way, though. Offers from Florida Athletic, Indiana and other schools dried up when he missed his senior season at Bartow High School because of a leg injury.
So, he spent the 2019 and 2020 seasons at Independence Community College in Kansas, which got him back on recruiters’ radars, and the 2021 and 2022 seasons at Louisiana Monroe, where he had 3.5 tackles for losses during his final season.
That got him his big opportunity at Miami.
“I wanted to go against better competition, get experience, better coaching and stuff, and we was losing and had ups and downs there, so I transferred to Miami and stuff happened.”
Campbell played in one game for the Hurricanes in 2023 and eight games in 2024. In two seasons, he played 56 snaps on defense. He wasn’t hurt. He just didn’t get on the field.
“Not wanting to bash nobody, but it’s just opportunity,” he said. “You know, stuff happens and then opportunity. You just got to be in the right place at the right time.”
Campbell’s confidence could have been crushed. If he wasn’t good enough to play in college, how on earth would he be good enough to play in the NFL?
Campbell, however, wouldn’t take no for an answer. He listened to those close to him and kept chasing what might have seemed like an impossible dream.
“You got people in your background telling you that you can do whatever you want,” he explained. “Because I’m very dedicated. Once I put my mind on something, I’m going to accomplish it. And I’m going to try to push myself to overcome anything, any obstacle that’s coming my way. I like to challenge myself and prove people wrong.”
Not surprisingly, Campbell went undrafted in 2025. He signed with the Seahawks about a month after the draft and competed for a roster spot during training camp but was released. He spent a couple days on their practice squad, and that was that.
Campbell was out of the league until the Packers signed him to their practice squad for the final week of the season and then retained him with a futures contract.
That humble start kicked off one of the more amazing Packers training camp stories in years. Campbell started camp by batting down a pass or two every day. As camp has progressed, he’s made more plays in the backfield, whether tackles for losses on running plays or pressures of the quarterback.
Against Denver, he clobbered Ehlinger. He finished the game with three tackles, according to the official stats, and a team-high four pressures, according to Pro Football Focus.
Anthony Campbell had a big night at Denver. Here’s his sack. pic.twitter.com/yarFNSW6L4
“A.C., man, he’s a guy that’s going to maximize every opportunity you give him,” position coach Vince Oghobaase said last week. “In the spring, every technique, every alignment, every drill, he wants to do it to perfection. When you get out there and tell him to do something to an offensive lineman aligned at this position, do this technique, he’s going to do it.
“He’s maximizing his opportunity. I think he’s batted over 10, 12 balls over the course of training camp, dating back to the spring. He’s been playing lights out, playing fearless, playing confident, playing with a chip on his shoulder. He’s come a long way. He’s done an incredible job. That confidence piece is huge for defensive linemen. When you’re confident, and you play fast, you play free, things can happen for him. He’s going like that (hand angled up).”
How? How did a player with exactly one tackle in two seasons at Miami put himself in position to make the Packers’ roster?
“It’s just something in me,” Campbell said. “My mom, the same way. It’s something in me.”
He shared a tackle for loss with Chris McClellan against Denver and with Warren Brinson against Pittsburgh.
“Just doing my job. Coach J.G. calls the right call, I’m going to do my best to execute it. Just doing my job. Coach V.O. teaches a lot of stuff to do. We got techniques we work on every day. You do it. I’m just going to go out there and do my best. Not think a lot, just go. Do my job. Whatever they tell me to do, I’m going to do it.”
From Kingston to kicking, from out of the league to challenging for a roster spot, it’s been an incredible journey.
“It’s not over yet,” he interjected. “I’m still working but, at the end of the day, I want to look back and I’m saying, damn, I’m strong. I’m going to keep pushing. Whatever happens here or somewhere else, I’m going to keep pushing.”
A huge final week of training camp will kick off on Monday. It will culminate with a joint practice against the Cardinals on Wednesday and a preseason game on Friday. Gutekunst will select his 53-man roster on Sunday.
“I love this transition for me,” Campbell said. “I like the experience I’m getting right now. Everything here is beautiful here. I love everything here. Players, everybody.”

title: A Lot on the Line During Final Week of Packers Training Camp (Pun Intended)
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – This will be a hugely important week for the Green Bay Packers to solidify an offensive line that’s more wet cement than firm concrete.
The Packers will kick off their final week of training camp on Monday. The final practice of camp, a joint practice against the Cardinals, will be held on Wednesday. The preseason will conclude on Friday at Lambeau Field against Arizona. On Sunday, general manager Brian Gutekunst will handle the long, tortuous task of cutting the 91-man roster to the 53-player limit.
The line is filled with questions, with the coaches and standout former Packers lineman Mike Wahle providing answers.
Jordan Morgan has had a quietly good training camp. That, of course, is exactly the type of training camp you want from any offensive lineman. He’s just done his job and kept Jordan Love out of harm’s way.
“He’s done a nice job,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said of Morgan on Saturday, one day after the preseason win at Denver. “He’s just quietly gone in here and anchored down the left side. He’s been good. There’s not a whole lot to talk about because he’s gone in there, done his job and stepped up. I’m happy with him right now, for sure.”
Last year, standout Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat rushed from the defense’s right side and against the offensive left tackle about half the time. He hasn’t practiced during training camp due to chronic knee issues. If he comes off PUP, it would be a great test for Morgan if Sweat, who is coming off a season of a career-high 12 sacks, would be on the field for the joint practice.
“He's very athletic,” Wahle, who helps NFL linemen through his Process2Perform, said of Morgan. “He moves well off the line of scrimmage. I think his first step is really explosive. Obviously, can get into space really well.”
Wahle hopes more of Morgan’s power emerges through experience.
“I don't know if it's the way they're being taught, but they don't necessarily play with the power that is in that body from an athletic standpoint – like the hip pop, the snap extension with your hands. So, there's things like that that you can continue to improve on, both in the run and the pass game, but really good athlete.
“The thing that both those guys do well, talking about Zach (Bako-Bewele) and Jordan in particular, is they get into these spots where they are able to anchor down pretty well despite not maybe winning with their hands or being in a really upright position They're kind of catching those players and they're almost doing it by design.
“Guys like Terron Armstead made a career of doing this, where you're kind of by design catching a guy but you have the ability to sit down on it. For me, it's not the ideal way to play football, but Mark Tauscher made a career out of it and was pretty damn good.”
Because of a knee injury, the Packers’ $77 million man practiced sporadically for the first couple weeks of training camp before finally getting some 11-on-11 reps at practice last week. He has not played in the preseason. The starters probably won’t play in Friday’s game, so Banks will need the joint practice to show that he’s ready for the season.
Arizona’s defense features 2024 first-round pick Darius Robinson at defensive tackle.
“At some point, we’re going to need him to go out there and put it all together for a string of time,” Stenavich said. “Otherwise, you won’t know if you can rely on him as the season goes. I think that’s going to be a big thing for me over these next two weeks is just getting out there on a regular basis, getting through practices and performing at a high level.”
It’s rather incredible to consider that Sean Rhyan, who has made eight career starts (including playoffs) at center, is perhaps the sure thing on the line.
“I like Sean Rhyan's want to finish,” Wahle said. “I don't know if he's ever going to be the most powerful guy in the world, but there's a guy that really is maximizing his athleticism because of his footwork and body position into contact.”
Jacob Monk has gone from battling for a roster spot to perhaps being the Week 1 starter at right guard. He replaced returning starter Anthony Belton before Family Night and hasn’t looked back. With rookie Jager Burton set to focus on center this week, the deck has been cleared.
“Monk, love his play style,” Stenavich said. “He’s a nasty dude. So, watching him play has been really fun.”
Monk has the play style that offensive line coach Luke Butkus prefers.
“I think Jacob Monk was born with a chip on his shoulder. He showed that at Duke and that’s one of the reasons we were attracted to him,” Butkus said. “He is a physical and violent human being when he steps on that football field. I don’t know if you guys have noticed, but when he gets on that field, he flips that switch. Love it, and that’s the play style we talk about.”
Wahle, who talked to Packers On SI before the Denver game, liked what he saw from Monk against the Steelers.
“I've always kind of liked that body type,” Wahle said. “He's a little bit shorter, but I like that as you get to play with great leverage. Looks like he's put some weight on – some good weight. I think he moves really well.
“The thing that stood out in the Pittsburgh game was the lateral run game; he really excelled at it. Obviously, he's got a quick burst out of his stance. He takes good footwork, has that leverage. He was really able to extend that backside hand, particularly on some of those outside-zone-to-the-left plays. You just like the ability to kind of get into those bigger opponents.”
The problem with being a shorter lineman is having shorter arms; Monk needs to avoid lunging out and overextending, which is why he was beaten by Broncos star Zach Allen on Jordan Love’s touchdown pass.
“That’s a huge learning thing for him at guard,” Stenavich said. “You go against really good players, you have to play with great fundamentals. Otherwise, you’ll get exposed.”
The team’s best lineman suffered a knee injury at Denver last season and missed the rest of the season. The Packers are easing him back into things but “he’ll be ready to roll Week 1,” Butkus said.
With Aaron Banks’ on-again, off-again status, rookie Jager Burton has been Plan B at left guard throughout training camp, which has limited his ability to compete at right guard. This week, Stenavich said, Burton will focus more on center, which could make him the universal backup at all three interior spots.
Wahle has been impressed. Burton needs to play with better patience but is advanced in other facets.
“The guy does a really nice job of some real basic parts of playing offensive line and not just for a rookie,” he said. “Really good initial footwork. He's gaining leverage towards his opponent on every play. He comes in with a really great body profile. He stays square to the line of scrimmage in pass pro, for the most part.
“Again, nothing's perfect – it's not going to be as a rookie. My eye goes immediately to how good you are at the precontact basics of the sport, and he's really, really good at them. He's advanced for this group.”
Anthony Belton opened training camp as the presumptive starting right guard after stepping into the lineup for the stretch run of last season. Having lost the job early in training camp, he’s been filling in behind Zach Bako-Bewele at right tackle. Since being replaced, he’s barely played any left tackle and he hasn’t played any right guard.
“There were enough positive traits last year that I certainly thought, OK, this guy should be expected to make a jump at right guard or at least be able to compete for the spot right now,” Wahle said.
“I think Jacob Monk could be a good player in the league. It’s Year 3 for him, so it’s kind of that time where you got to prove it. Maybe they've just seen so much that they like. You know, we never know what's going on in the background, but it is really surprising that he wouldn't get reps at right guard. He didn't do anything last year to dissuade me from thinking he…

title: Predicting the Packers’ 53-Man Roster With Cuts Looming Next Week
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers have made it through the first two preseason games and are heading toward a meaningful final week of training camp with a joint practice and game against the Arizona Cardinals.
There are plenty of battles to be won as the depth of the roster has made for some interesting decisions and even given the Packers some potential trade chips if they choose to go that route.
Other spots are easy to project, and some jobs have been solidified with big-time performances in the preseason from kicker Trey Smack and defensive back Kamal Hadden.
Here is our second crack at a 53-man projection with a big week looming.
On the 53: Jordan Love, Tyrod Taylor.
Not much to see here. Jordan Love is the starter. Tyrod Taylor will be the backup.
Kyle McCord has been excellent in the preseason, and the Packers may have to weigh whether a team would scoop him up if they release him on cutdown day. If he’s released and clears waivers, the Packers would likely be thrilled to have him back on the practice squad.
On the 53: Josh Jacobs, Marshawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks.
MarShawn Lloyd is healthy and proving why the Packers were willing to wait for him to work through his injuries through the first two seasons of his career. Chris Brooks is the team’s best blocking back and a core special-teamer.
One thing that could be interesting is what the Packers do with Pierre Strong Jr. He’s shown an ability to get downhill in the run game and return kickoffs. Strong returned a kickoff 68 yards to set up a Trey Smack field goal in the game Friday against the Denver Broncos. With legal questions surrounding Josh Jacobs, could the Packers look to keep an insurance policy?
On the 53: Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Jayden Reed, Skyy Moore, Bo Melton, Savion Williams.
There are some intriguing practice-squad candidates with Isaiah Neyor, J. Michael Sturdivant and Will Sheppard proving their worth at different points in the preseason and training camp.
As far as the roster goes? There’s just not that much drama here. In order to keep one of the aforementioned players, they’d either have to keep seven receivers or release Bo Melton.
Seven receivers feels like a waste of a roster spot with all of the needs in other places on the roster. The likelihood is the Packers could get some, if not all of the aforementioned receivers, back on the practice squad.
Releasing Melton would be the shock of the century. The organization loves him. He might be the team’s best special teams player, and has made plays for them as a receiver. On Saturday, special teams coordinator Cam Achord said they are working 18 players at gunner but pointed only to Melton. Then, passing-game coordinator Jason Vrable said Melton is one of the receivers’ top blockers.
On the 53: Tucker Kraft, Josh Whyle, Drake Dabney.
The first two choices on this list are easy. Tucker Kraft is back, but they’re going to have to hold him back early in the season while he fully recovers from his torn ACL.
Josh Whyle is firmly entrenched as the backup tight end. After that, Drake Dabney’s name could read Dabney Drake and it may not make a difference. Dabney is making the roster at this point by default, but tight end feels like a position where the Packers are going to have to add someone from the outside.
Jonnu Smith is one possibility as he has played under coach Matt La Fleur. Zach Ertz is a veteran with some big-game chops, but the Packers are likely to lean toward a younger player who could potentially make an impact on special teams.
On the 53: Jordan Morgan, Aaron Banks, Sean Rhyan, Anthony Belton, Zach Bako-Bewele, Darian Kinnard, Jager Burton, John Williams, Jacob Monk.
There may not be a player who has helped himself more in training camp than Jacob Monk. At the beginning of camp, it appeared he would be on the roster bubble. Now, he appears to be the overwhelming favorite to start at right guard against Minnesota in Week 1.
The back end of the offensive line room is starting to take shape. Jager Burton is the plug-and-play guy at all three interior spots if he’s not starting in favor of Aaron Banks. Anthony Belton is the swing tackle. John Williams is a potential super-sub with reps at left tackle, left guard and center during camp.
Darian Kinnard played well for the Packers a season ago if he can get off the injury report. Not only could he provide depth at right guard and right tackle but he played 66 snaps at tight end last season.
On the 53: Javon Hargrave, Devonte Wyatt, Chris McClellan, Karl Brooks, Jonathan Ford, Warren Brinson.
Jonathan Ford is one of the top performers in training camp and may start at nose tackle if the season were to begin tomorrow. He replaces Nazir Stackhouse, who made the cut in our initial projection.
One question that could upset the apple cart here is whether the Packers want to keep training camp stalwart Anthony Campbell. He’s been all over the field during practices and games, including his first sack against the Broncos on Friday. If the Packers don’t want to risk losing Campbell to waivers, they’d either have to keep him in favor of Ford, trade Karl Brooks, who is entering the final year of his deal, or keep seven.
That’s something worth monitoring as the preseason comes to a close.
On the 53: Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox, Dani Dennis-Sutton, Collin Oliver.
This group has had an up-and-down camp and is facing a big week with their joint practice session against the Cardinals. The pass rush was solid against the Steelers in the first week of the preseason, with Lukas Van Ness and Brenton Cox recording sacks.
Friday night against the Broncos, they were dormant against one of the better offensive lines in football. Nobody has really separated themselves in game situations, and that could make for one giant Micah Parsons-sized question mark as the season kicks off in three weeks.
On the 53: Zaire Franklin, Edgerrin Cooper, Isaiah McDuffie, Ty'Ron Hopper, Nick Niemann.
This is another pretty easy group to forecast. The Packers likely hope to sneak local product Kristian Welch onto the practice squad for the depth he provides at linebacker along with his special-teams ability.
Otherwise, Zaire Franklin and Edgerrin Cooper are the starters. The primary backups are Ty’Ron Hopper and Isaiah McDuffie, with Nick Niemann playing the role of special teams ace.
On the 53: Keisean Nixon, Carrington Valentine, Brandon Cisse, Benjamin St-Juste, Domani Jackson, Kamal Hadden.
There has been a lot of drama at this position, but right now it’s hard to forecast any major changes coming. Carrington Valentine and Keisean Nixon could be trade candidates at the end of camp, but can the Packers really afford to sacrifice any depth at the position? As things stand, Brandon Cisse is likely to start Week 1. with Nixon, Valentine and Benjamin St-Juste battling it out for roles as the season goes on.
Kamal Hadden has popped since returning to action and could provide positional versatility as a boundary cornerback and slot. Domani Jackson has missed a good chunk of camp, but is back on the field, and the Packers liked him enough to draft him. He’ll get one of the final spots on the roster.
On the 53: Evan Williams, Xavier McKinney, Javon Bullard, Kitan Oladapo, Mark Perry.
The first three help form what is likely the best safety trio in all of football. Javon Bullard should return to action soon after missing time with a foot injury that has hampered him during training camp. Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams might form the best starting safety tandem in the NFL.
The big addition here is Mark Perry, who popped onto the screen in Friday’s win over the Broncos with an interception that led to a field goal late in the first half. Playmaking and his ability on special teams should give him the nod for one of the final spots on the roster.
On the 53: Daniel Whelan, Trey Smack, Matt Orzech.

title: Texans Sign Former Jaguars DE Derek Parish: What to Know
full_text:
The Houston Texans have gone out to sign a brand-new face from free agency to add onto their defensive line.
According to ESPN 's Adam Schefter, the Texans have agreed to sign former Jacksonville Jaguars seventh-round pick, defensive end Derek Parish.
Former Jaguars 2023 sixth-round pick and UFL edge rusher Derick Parish reached agreement today with the Houston Texans.
Parish, who was a five-year player for the University of Houston from 2017 to 2022, has most recently been a part of the UFL during the most recent 2026 season with the DC Defenders. He also spent a couple of years in the CFL with the Toronto Argonauts.
Now, Parish makes the Texans his next stop. He'll be signed onto the 90-man roster and could have a chance to be seen in uniform by the time Houston plays their third and final preseason game against the Carolina Panthers on Friday .
Parish, who was the 240th pick in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft, is a 6-foot-1, 27-year-old defensive end who's made his way back home to Houston. Parish not only attended the University of Houston for five years, but also comes from Pearland High School in Pearland, TX.
He has yet to appear in an NFL game since being drafted to Jacksonville three years ago. However, he did play pretty significantly last season in the UFL.
Parish played in 10 games with the Defenders, where he logged 23 total tackles, three total sacks, and a forced fumble. He also appeared in two postseason games where he posted three tackles.
The Texans had a clear need to fill within their defensive line when it comes to their defensive end depth. Because in recent days, the position has seen a ton of noteworthy pieces go down pr with various injuries.
Jadeveon Clowney is dealing with a lower leg injury, Dominique Robinson is recovering from a calf injury that was suffered after the Texans' last preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders, and fourth-year edge rusher Dylan Horton has reportedly suffered a torn Achilles that will sideline him for the entire 2026 season.
The Texans needed depth off the edge, even if just to close out their preseason before roster cuts take place this weekend . And Parish is the guy they bring onboard, who has a bit more of a unique path to the league than some other free agents when factoring in his history in both the CFL and UFL.
But Parish could have an interesting opportunity on his hands. For a team which now has a depth chart that's wide open at defensive end past their top three names, it opens the door for a surprise standout in the room to climb up the ranks into a bigger role than expected.
Parish doesn't have much time before the Texans are tasked with slimming their roster to 53 players on Sunday, though with a strong showing in practice and preseason, maybe a practice squad nod could be in reach.

title: What to Expect From Kayshon Boutte's First Week With Texans
full_text:
The Houston Texans made a noteworthy addition to their wide receiver room earlier this week with the trade for wide receiver Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots for second-year safety Jayden Reed and a future seventh-round pick from the New Orleans Saints.
The move from the Texans comes just a few days after their No. 2 wide receiver Jayden Higgins went down with a season-ending ACL tear in their recent joint practice with the Las Vegas Raiders.
Houston had a need at the position, they addressed it with Boutte , and he now joins the roster less than three weeks away from the start of the 2026 regular season.
But before the Texans kick off Week 1 of their regular season, they've got one more game of preseason to go against the Carolina Panthers on Friday night.
Houston will also be facing the Panthers in a joint practice this Wednesday in preparation for their final exhibition game to close out the week.
So what can be expected of the Texans' newest wide receiver addition as the team heads to Charlotte for their next practice? Here's the latest on what we know:
As the Texans are set to practice with the Panthers in Charlotte on Wednesday morning, according to The Houston Chronicle 's Jonathan M. Alexander , Boutte will be making the trip to join the team in what will be his first practice session with Houston's roster since the trade went down on Monday afternoon.
That means Boutte will also be in town for the Texans' preseason game that lands on Friday night, offering the fourth-year wide receiver an opportunity to play alongside his new team within an in-game setting before the regular season kicks off early next month.
It's an extremely quick turnaround for Boutte, who was just catching passes from Drake Maye in training camp practice with the Patriots last week. But after some buzzing rumors turned into real trade talks between New England and Houston, he'll now be getting his fourth year rolling in Houston.
As to whether or not Boutte expects to play in game three of the preseason against the Panthers, or how much time he plays overall, remains to be seen. He was healthy throughout the start of the Patriots’ training camp, so if rested, the Texans would likely be doing so for precautionary reasons.
Throughout the first two games of the Texans' preseason so far, they've remained relatively conservative as it relates to playing their starters or key pieces a large share of snaps.
In game one of the preseason against the Los Angeles Chargers, all of the Texans' starters rested for the entire night, except for their first-unit offensive line, which played the first drive of the night. Game two against the Las Vegas Raiders saw the offensive line, C.J. Stroud, and Woody Marks suit up for one drive, but all defensive starters were out once again.
So maybe Boutte only gets to play a drive or two with his new team on Friday. Based on how they've operated through their showings thus far, Boutte will probably see a select few reps in the first and/or second quarter, rather than playing the entire way.
But at the very least, Boutte seems likely to be with the team and in pads for their second joint practice of camp against the Panthers on Wednesday–– which certainly starts to make his addition to this offense feel a little more real.

title: Texans Injury Tracker: Latest Updates Before Preseason Finale
full_text:
The Houston Texans are a little less than three weeks away from the start of their 2026 regular season, as kickoff for Week 1 is slated for September 13th against the Buffalo Bills .
And in the preparation for the season, through the past few weeks of training camp and a couple of preseason games, the Texans have sustained a few noteworthy injuries.
Some have limited players from practicing, have sidelined them for an extended period of time that puts their availability to start the season in jeopardy, and in a few cases, have ended their 2026 campaigns entirely.
Here's the latest surrounding what we know about the Texans and their injury statuses heading into their joint practice and final preseason game with the Carolina Panthers later this week:
The following players reportedly missed the Texans' latest training camp practice on Monday, according to KRPC2 's Aaron Wilson . The latest information about their injury status will be attached:
WR Tank Dell (knee) - Was held out of Monday's practice. Has been gradually returning to team drills with full pads, but has yet to participate in a preseason game. Head coach DeMeco Ryans previously said he expects Dell to play in a preseason game.
TE Brevin Jordan (knee) - Has been dealing with a lingering knee injury since before the Texans' game against the Chargers. Has yet to play in a preseason game, and timetable for return is unknown.
DE Jadeveon Clowney (calf) - Is dealing with a new lower leg injury as of the Texans' latest camp practice. Head coach DeMeco Ryans says the team "expects him back soon."
DE Dominique Robinson (calf) - Suffered a lower leg injury during the Texans' game vs. the Raiders. Timetable for return expects to be day-to-day.
LB Jake Hansen (calf) - Has remained sidelined since the first week of Texans' training camp after leaving practice via cart with a lower leg injury , therefore having yet to play a preseason game or practiced since July.
RB Jawhar Jordan (hip flexor) - Has been dealing with a hip injury prior to the Texans' first preseason game vs. the Chargers. Has not played in either preseason outing.
CB Collin Wright (soft tissue) - Recovering from a soft tissue injury that was suffered in his first preseason game against the Chargers. Did not play vs. the Raiders.
S Kamari Ramsey (ankle) - Dealing with an ankle injury after the Texans' game vs. the Raiders. Expects to be minor.
RB Noah Whittington (ankle) - Suffered an ankle injury during the Texans' game vs. the Raiders. Timetable for return expects to be day-to-day.
LB Wade Woodaz (thumb) - Suffered broken thumb during the Texans' game vs. the Raiders. Underwent surgery to repare it, and could still be on track to return in time for Week 1.
The Texans have five players who are expected to either start the season on the physically unable to perform list or miss the 2026 year entirely:
LB E.J. Speed (quad) - Suffered quad injury during the 2026 offseason . Has been on the PUP list since the start of training camp, and is expected to miss a majority of, if not all of the 2026 season.
S M.J. Stewart (quad) - Recovering from the quad injury he sustained in 2025 that ended his season entirely. He's been on the PUP list since the start of training camp, with no word on when he might be able to return.
QB Graham Mertz (knee) - Suffered a torn ACL in the Texans' first preseason game of the year vs. the LA Chargers. He is expected to miss the entire 2026 season, and Houston has signed Brett Rypien as their newest QB3 in his place.
WR Jayden Higgins (knee) - Suffered a torn ACL during the Texans' first joint practice of training camp against the Las Vegas Raiders. He is expected to miss the entire 2026 season.
DE Dylan Horton (Achilles) - Reportedly suffered a torn Achilles during Tuesday's team training camp practice, and is expected to miss the entire 2026 season because of it.

title: Biggest Winners and Losers of Texans' Kayshon Boutte Trade
full_text:
The Houston Texans made a much-needed acquisition for their wide receiver room earlier this week with the trade to land New England Patriots pass-catcher Kayshon Boutte in exchange for safety Jayden Reed and a future seventh-round pick.
Trade! The Patriots are sending WR Kayshon Boutte to the Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . pic.twitter.com/NZXCdOX4RT
Houston was due to add another wideout to their offense following the news that their second-year receiver, Jayden Higgins, would be missing the entire 2026 season with a torn ACL .
Boutte was a name on the market linked to a trade for some time, and now, the Texans are the ones to strike with the hopes of answering their questions at receiver.
Time will tell if the Texans were wise in making this deal. But at least as the dust is still settling after the move, there are a few immediate winners and losers to take note of involved in the deal that might just raise–– or lower–– their stock heading into the 2026 season starting next month.
Let's sort through three winners and two losers from the Texans' latest trade to bolster their roster at receiver:
It feels like Kayshon Boutte is someone within this entire equation who now finds himself in a much better position than where he just was.
He's bound to get a whole lot more snaps his way in Houston considering their offensive situation. He has a better chance to build up his value and net a second contract with the Texans, and he moves to another contending-level team in the AFC that can get him right back to the Super Bowl stage he was just on.
The makings truly could be there for Boutte to have a career season in Houston, and win a ton of games while he's at it. So if he were to get dealt anywhere, the Texans aren't a bad result for him by any means.
The one name on the Texans' wide receiver depth chart who now sees immediate competition for reps is fourth-year wideout Xavier Hutchinson–– who felt primed for a lot of opportunities to come his way after Higgins' injury .
Now the Texans always felt bound to add some firepower to their receiver position in some way, so Hutchinson's spot as the WR2 was never exactly secure. But now, the route gets a whole lot harder for him to have a true breakout season for an even better year than he just put up in 2025.
So Houston's wide receiver room gets better as a whole. But for Hutchison individually, his stock might be trending downwards.
In order to get Boutte on the roster, the Texans had to shed some depth in their secondary. Second-year safety Jaylen Reed would be the one shipped out, and that means fifth-round pick  Kamari Ramsey is in for even more work to come his way early in the season.
The Texans have a clear top three in their safety room that'll place ahead of Ramsey on the depth chart: Calen Bullock, Jalen Pitre, and Reed Blankenship; potentially the best three-man group that any team in the NFL has at the position.
However, without Reed, and for as long as M.J. Stewart is sidelined with his long-term quad injury, Ramsey becomes the next man up as the primary backup, and a versatile defensive back that can line up around the field, and get defensive snaps as soon as Week 1.
The Texans' wide receiver room now gets one man deeper. And for those who are fringe roster guys— like third-year pass-catcher Jared Wayne — the move doesn't exactly bode well for their security to land past the 53-man cut.
Wayne has had a strong preseason and training camp that makes him well worth consideration to make it on the roster past this weekend. But with four to five virtual roster locks, depending on Tank Dell's status, Lewis Bond, Justin Watson, Sterling Shepard, and Zay Jones, there's a ton of competition for Wayne to work through in the days ahead.
An obvious winner in this situation is none other than the Texans' starting quarterback: C.J. Stroud, who will now be able to take a deep breath when it comes to what his receiver room is going to look like for the season ahead.
Without a presence like Higgins for the entire year, there was a bit of panic to be had for what was next at the position for the Texans. Yet, Boutte is a reliable set of hands who's been productive for the last two seasons with the New England Patriots, and now offers some much-needed relief for their passing offense.

title: Texans' Rivalries Uniforms Released: What to Know, What They Look Like
full_text:
After a long wait, the Houston Texans' newest uniforms have officially been released––as have the seven other Rivalries edition uniforms that were slated to drop on Tuesday morning .
And for the Texans, they got a completely new look from what the franchise has seen on their uniform throughout 25 years in the league: a white-shelled helmet, a white and bright blue jersey described as an "iced out" uniform that "celebrates H-Town," and another bold take in the NFL's ongoing Rivalries uniform campaign.
The Texans' social media released a promotional video showcasing the new-look uniforms, and a sneak peek of what they look like on players, highlighting the slogan, "By the H. For the H."
Our city. Our colors. Our uniform. pic.twitter.com/5mnX8j7M4b
The Texans were set to get their Rivalries edition uniforms this season following the debut of the series in 2025, which saw eight teams across two divisions add another uniform to their collection to be worn on special, divisional matchups throughout the course of the regular season for the next three years.
This season, after the AFC East and the NFC West got their uniforms last season, the AFC South and the NFC North were due for their own release ahead of the 2026 campaign.
So Houston's surrounding division—the Tennessee Titans, Indianapolis Colts, and Jacksonville Jaguars—all released their respective uniform sets, with themes and concepts unique to their respective franchises. Or, like in the case of the Texans', one that really connects to the home city.
With another uniform now being added to the Texans' wardrobe, they'll head into the 2026 season with five different uniforms to showcase throughout the season: their typical home and away sets that they'll mostly be wearing, as well as three alternates: these new releases, their all-red, "Battle Red," uniforms, and their "Space City" uniforms.
The Texans will have one week in which they roll out their Rivalries edition uniforms on the field: Week 11 against the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday Night Football.
It'll be the second time in the 2026 season where the Texans see a Rivalries edition uniform on the field with them. In Week 3, Houston will be facing off against the Colts on the road in their own newly released kits.
The Texans will be wearing these jerseys twice more across the 2027 and 2028 seasons, as will those around the AFC South. But going up against the Colts deeper in the season at home on a primetime setting could be a perfect way for Houston to debut these new threads in-game.
The Texans are 5-0 against the Colts in their last five meetings, with Indianapolis' last victory coming in 2023.
Time will tell if Houston can continue that trend for both of their contests this coming season, which are bound to have a little more flair than usual with the Rivalries implications.

title: What Dylan Horton’s Season-Ending Injury Means for Texans
full_text:
The Houston Texans will be down a player on their defensive line for the 2026 season following Monday's training camp practice.
According to KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson , Texans defensive end Dylan Horton is feared to have suffered a season-ending Achilles injury.
Horton was set to enter his fourth season with the Texans in 2026 and had been fighting to make it onto Houston's 53-man roster as a depth piece within their defensive end room.
However, in a practice before the Texans' third preseason game of the year against the Carolina Panthers, Horton would go down with a torn Achilles, thus ending his 2026 campaign and changing the outlook on Houston's defensive line along with it.
After three seasons in Houston, Horton was shaping up to have a bit of an increased role for the Texans' defense in 2026.
While he was battling to be the fourth defensive end on the depth chart after Houston signed Jadeveon Clowney earlier in training camp , Horton was only active in 25% of in his games played in 2025.
If he won out to be DE4, he had a chance to see that number, and his individual stats would take a step forward––which comes even more important in a contract year.
Last season with the Texans, Horton played in 16 games to log 26 total tackles and 0.5 sacks.
Now, the 2023 fourth-round pick will have to wait until 2027 to take his next snap, which may or may not be with the Texans, and take on the long road of recovering from a torn Achilles.
With Horton now out of the picture, the Texans' defensive line depth now looks a bit more interesting than it did this time last week. And this has been a group that's already seen a fair share of questions throughout training camp.
Besides Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter, and Jadeveon Clowney at the top, Houston is now down to free agent signings Dominique Robinson––who is currently hurt heading into game three of the preseason, Salomon Byrd, Ali Gaye, and Sebastian Harsh.
It's a group that has some promise, but not a ton of proven production. All four of them have a combined 4.5 sacks throughout their careers, with 3.5 of those coming from Robinson during his four years with the Chicago Bears.
As to who will be the best bet to take that DE4 role from Horton, Robinson feels like the most likely to do so . However, his recent injury could add even more uncertainty to the position creeping closer to the regular season, and perhaps more importantly, this weekend's 53-man cutdown.
With the look of Houston's defensive line depth, it feels likely for the front office to approach the position with an addition via free agency, or a trade if they're very interested in adding another defensive end.
The Texans have proven multiple times leading up to this season that, if they have a certain need on the roster, and there's talent ready to be acquired on the market, they're going to make the move to do just that.
Houston needs another edge rusher? Jadeveon Clowney is signed to a one-year deal. They need another receiver after Jayden Higgins suffers a season-ending injury? The front office goes out to trade for Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots .
The Texans have been continuously proactive in patching up their necessary holes, and doing whatever it takes to best position this roster to be a Super Bowl-caliber group by the time the season ends.

title: Instant Grade: Texans Land WR Kayshon Boutte in Trade With Patriots
full_text:
The Houston Texans are adding a new pass catcher to their wide receiver room.
According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero of NFL Network , the Texans are acquiring wide receiver Kayshon Boutte in a trade from the New England Patriots.
Trade! The Patriots are sending WR Kayshon Boutte to the Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . pic.twitter.com/NZXCdOX4RT
The Texans are reportedly sending over second-year safety Jayden Reed and future seventh-round pick from the New Orleans Saints to the Patriots in exchange for Boutte.
It was a much-needed, and even partly an expected move for the Texans to make after the recent events that have taken place at their wide receiver position. 2025 second-round pick Jayden Higgins went down with a torn ACL earlier last week during practice , and will be sidelined for the entire 2026 season because of it.
And now, the Texans have acted quickly by bringing in Boutte as the latest name to their wide receiver room.
Let's break down the Texans' latest deal for what it means moving forward, along with an instant grade for how Houston fared.
Boutte has been circled as an easy trade target for teams–– and narely, the Texans–– across the league in recent days to weeks.
Boutte's in the final year of his contract, and on a Patriots team that acquired two other targets in A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs earlier this offseason, that makes it far less likely that he's in for a new deal with New England in 2027.
And for the Texans, they made sense as a perfect target . They had a clear need in their wide receiver room, and especially for someone that can effectively line up on the outside of Houston's offense as a starting-caliber pass-catcher opposite of Nico Collins.
Kayshon Boutte fits that mold quite well. He's a little smaller at 5-foot-11, but he's coming off of two quality seasons in New England, where he was a consistent, reliable target for Drake Maye.
In 2025, Boutte put together 33 receptions, 551 yards, and six touchdowns, the second straight year where he had over 30 catches and 500 yards. He was second in the Patriots' offense for total receiving touchdowns, and fifth in total receiving yards.
As a big-play, downfield threat, Boutte can be a noteworthy contributor. And pretty immediately, he could be in for some significant targets in the Texans' wide receiver room as the WR2 or WR3 behind Collins, and maybe Xavier Hutchinson.
As it relates to the Texans' deal to bring in Boutte and how well they fared, you can't imagine a much better outcome. The draft capital they sent out was minimal, and the player they shipped out was at a position they had a nice chunk of depth at anyways.
Jaylen Reed is a nice safety with solid potential to be a starting-level defender, but the Texans already have a lot to work with at the position with Calen Bullock, Reed Blankenship, Jalen Pitre, and fifth-round rookie Kamari Ramsey. Shedding a depth piece from that group and investing in their wide receiver group is a stellar way to manage those assets.
Now, the Texans can take a deep breath for what lies ahead in their receiver room, and have a solid group of weapons behind Collins to rely on to, at the very least, stay afloat without Higgins' presence for this season.
The only reason this move isn't an A+? Because of the uncertainty that lies ahead for Boutte in Houston past this season.
He's on an expiring contract, and in a wide receiver room that also faces pending free agents for Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell, there are no guarantees that this will be a multi-year pairing between the Texans and Boutte.
But for now, the move to bring in a trustworthy receiver like Boutte was necessary and took minimal cost to make happen. With that in mind, an A feels like the right grade.

title: Three Texans WRs Poised for More Targets Without Jayden Higgins
full_text:
The Houston Texans' wide receiver room is set to look a bit different than initially expected this season without second-year wideout Jayden Higgins in the lineup— who will be out for the 2026 campaign due to a torn ACL suffered in practice last week.
Without Higgins, who was overwhelmingly expected to be the Texans' No. 2 wide receiver in the offense, how this position could pan out for the offense this season could change drastically.
Guys are going to trend up the depth chart, get more targets and opportunities on their hands because of it, and might have some of their best seasons ever on the horizon.
Not having Higgins certainly hurts this Texans passing offense as a whole. But for these three wideouts on Houston's roster, they'll be in store for a lot more work without him.
The receiver who feels immediately due to claim the snaps left up for grabs from Higgins is none other than Xavier Hutchinson: someone who's healthy, fits the physical mold the Texans would want lining up as their Z receiver, and comes off a career-best season in 2025 entering a contract year.
The makings of an even better season are there for Hutchinson , who had over 30 receptions and 400 yards in 2025. Last season, he was fourth in the Texans' wide receiver room for target share at a little more than 10%. But now, two of the names that were above him in Higgins and Christian Kirk are no longer in the way for 2026.
Seeing Hutchinson log over 600 receiving yards this season and take that target share jump up to around 13% or higher certainly wouldn't be the most shocking outcome. And it could be what leads him to a nice payday once this next offseason arrives.
Second-year wide receiver Jaylin Noel got a slow start to training camp due to the minor finger and hamstring injury he suffered at the end of July.
But now, he's trending back to full health heading into the final week of preseason. And with a smooth recovery, he could be due for an even bigger jump in opportunities from how things were shaking up in Houston's offseason program in the summer.
Compared to last season, Noel has another year of experience under his belt, won't have to compete for targets with either Kirk and Higgins, and feels like the most likely candidate to claim a majority of the snaps as the Texans' slot receiver throughout the course of the season. That role alone means Noel is due for a big jump in numbers.
Noel had a tiny 6% target share in the Texans' offense last season. If that number weren't in double digits by the time this season ends, it'd be a pretty big surprise.
Some may argue Tank Dell is in store for a significant jump in targets after Higgins' injury. But he hasn't even participated in a preseason game since recovering from his injury. And until he's back to a true 100%, his absence puts a star like Nico Collins in position for even more work than he was already expected to get.
Collins is about as trusted and proven a wide receiver that the Texans could have in their unit. He's already coming off of three straight 1,000-yard seasons, but less depth without Higgins, and maybe Dell to start the season, means those targets get further consolidated into top options like Houston’s WR1.
As long as the Texans don't make any major changes to the position , and Collins remains healthy throughout the year, seeing him post a career-best season might not be out of the range of realistic possibilities for 2026.

title: Texans’ Biggest Surprise Standouts From Preseason So Far
full_text:
Despite the Houston Texans losing both of their preseason games played thus far, there have been a handful of standouts worth nothing around the roster who have boosted their stock in one way or another leading up to the regular season.
Especially for the Texans' rookie class, who have gotten significant reps through Houston's showings against the Los Angeles Chargers and Las Vegas Raiders, things have looked notably positive for a select few.
And with one preseason game––along with a joint practice––to go against the Carolina Panthers, the hope is those who have shined can keep that momentum up and put themselves in position for an ideal start to Week 1, kicking off in less than three weeks.
Let's take a look at five players around the Texans' roster who have emerged as surprise standouts through two weeks of preseason.
The Texans’ wide receiver room has been due for someone down the depth chart to stand out following the injury to Jayden Higgins, and third-year wideout Jared Wayne has stepped up to the occasion to do just that.
In game one of the Texans' preseason action, he hauled in Houston's only touchdown score of the day on an impressive red-zone catch on a ball from Davis Mills. He's totaled five receptions for 30 yards through two games, and is the only receiver on the roster to log multiple receptions in both games.
Jared Wayne and the Texans get out to an early lead Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/WYMFNSLKtj
There's a lot of uncertainty as to what the Texans' receiver room will look like come Week 1 . But Wayne's recent performance could be creating an extremely compelling case that makes him the final name at the position to make it onto the roster past cutdown day.
Klein really needed a big preseason to showcase why the Texans invested in him so highly in April's draft with a second-round pick. And so far, he's done just that.
In Klein's first game, he had a game-high 31-yard reception that really put him on the map. In game two against the Raiders, Klein had an equally strong day with three catches on four targets for 31 yards.
OKAY MARLIN‼️ 📺: @abc13houston pic.twitter.com/tJ7JZBbIZt
Klein had a slow start to the Texans' offseason program earlier this summer, but his recent emergence could shoot him much further up the depth chart entering Week 1 from what anyone initially expected.
Woodaz seems likely to miss some time moving forward, as the rookie linebacker suffered a broken thumb in the Texans' second preseason game against the Raiders. But the sample size he's shown thus far is really promising for what his future will look like in this Houston defense.
Game one resulted in Woodaz putting together a quiet two tackles, but his second game against the Raiders is where he really shined: two total tackles, a pass defended, and an interception returned 80 yards for a touchdown on this year's No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza.
OPEN UP A CAN OF WOODAZZZZZZ 🤯 📺: @nflonespn pic.twitter.com/Ke0lrYupPs
Time will tell how long it'll be until Woodaz is back in the fold, and whether or not he starts the season on injured reserve. But when he is back, there's a pretty solid chance he finds his way to that LB3 role on the depth chart that's been wide open since E.J. Speed's been out with a torn quad.
The Texans selected two linebackers in April's draft. And so far, both of them have been exceeding expectations when factoring in how well seventh-round pick Aiden Fisher has been producing through two showings .
Game one against the Chargers saw Fisher log a game-high seven combined tackles and one tackle for loss. Game two saw him collect a similarly impressive six combined tackles, which tied for second-highest on the Texans' defense in tackles behind Brandon Codrington.
Combining the recent injuries in the room with the performances of Fisher might be the perfect storm for Fisher to be someone who sneaks onto a 53-man roster spot, so long as he keeps the momentum going into this week's game against Carolina.
Fifth-round rookie Kamari Ramsey deserves a shoutout for his interception on Trey Lance against the Chargers in week one of the preseason. But another safety in the room who's also performed well through two games is second-year talent Jaylen Reed, who's done nothing but produce strong numbers.
He has a combined 11 tackles with a pass defended in two games. He's one of three players with double-digit tackles through both games alongside Aiden Fisher and cornerback Stephen Hall.
Reed's chances to make the Week 1 roster were already pretty solidified entering training camp, but production like this certainly does lock that status in even further for what appears to be a deep and versatile safety room.

title: How Wade Woodaz's Latest Injury Changes Texans' LB Room
full_text:
The Houston Texans' linebacker room has been hit with another injury: fourth-round rookie Wade Woodaz .
According to KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson , Woodaz is expected to undergo surgery following the broken thumb injury he sustained in the Texans' preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
His timeline for return reportedly remains undetermined, but placing Woodaz on injured reserve before the season remains a possibility.
It's one of multiple injuries the Texans have seen in their linebacker unit before Week 1 of the regular season.
Woodaz joins both E.J. Speed (quad) and Jake Hansen (ankle) as candidates who could end up missing the start of the year, and thus makes the position group even thinner from what they were working with.
Let's break down what the injury to Woodaz means for the Texans' linebacker room moving forward:
After the Texans' training camp work and two games of preseason, it felt like Woodaz was the primary candidate in the lead to claim Houston's LB3 role before the season .
It's been a spot that's been open on Houston's defense since E.J. Speed first suffered his quad injury earlier this summer, but felt increasingly settled in Woodaz's hands, especially after his 80-yard pick-six on Fernando Mendoza against the Raiders that really made a statement on top of what he had already done through training camp.
But now, the Texans could have that LB3 job back up for grabs, at least to begin the 2026 season while Woodaz is off to the side. Perhaps that comes via someone already on the roster, or maybe Houston goes out to acquire someone via trade to really fill the position.
The two names who stick out with the most likely odds to get work in Houston's linebacker room are veteran Marte Mapu and seventh-round rookie Aiden Fisher .
Both have performed well throughout the past few weeks that the Texans have been back in the building, and will now have even more opportunity on their hands––especially if Woodaz is going to be placed on injured reserve to start the year.
Two other names to keep an eye on: fourth-year linebacker Jamal Hill and offseason free agent signing Jake Hummel. Each might be more geared towards being primarily a special teamer, but as the room continues to get slimmer, they'll have a better chance to lock themselves into a 53-man roster spot, but also into a bigger role defensively.
The Texans have already acted by adding extra depth within their linebacker room since Woodaz's injury, reportedly signing veteran Caleb Johnson. who's entering his sixth season in the NFL.
#Texans set to sign veteran linebacker Caleb Johnson after successful workout, per a league source. Johnson, the first @HouChristianU #NFL player in school history, Has 40 career tackles, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, previously #Bears #Jaguars #Falcons #Dolphins … https://t.co/aqb3QREnEi pic.twitter.com/2OcqJXTAQv
The undrafted product out of Houston Christian has been mostly a special teamer throughout his five years in the pros, having played for the Chicago Bears, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Miami Dolphins. He has 40 career tackles and one forced fumble throughout his career.
Johnson has over 1,100 snaps on special teams throughout his time in the league. With the Dolphins last season, he played just two games and just 22 snaps, suffered a shoulder injury, and saw his 2025 campaign shortened because of it.
He may not have an inside track for the Texans roster with a week to go until cutdown day, but he will be someone to watch getting snaps in preseason later this week, as Houston travels to face the Carolina Panthers for their final preliminary showing on Friday, August 28th.

title: Colts Injury Report Gets Promising Update With Regular Season on the Horizon
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have been without star wide receiver Alec Pierce since the 2025 regular season concluded.
Pierce signed a four-year, $114M contract to stay in Indianapolis earlier this offseason. He's been set to become the Colts' next WR1 option since they traded away longtime starter Michael Pittman Jr. to afford Pierce's services.
However, even though the Colts are betting on Pierce to continue his emergence as a legitimate top option in the NFL, the wide receiver hasn't practiced all offseason, and now we're a little over two weeks away from the 2026 regular season.
Pierce had a clean-up procedure done on his left ankle/heel a few weeks after he signed his aforementioned deal, and his projected rehab slated him for a four-to-six-month return.
The earlier side of said timetable would've brought Pierce back for training camp, but alas, with camp wrapping up late last week, the wait for his activation has intensified as the regular season quickly approaches.
The good news is that Alec Pierce will be back in time for the 2026 regular season.
Colts head coach Shane Steichen revealed before practice on Tuesday that wide receiver Alec Pierce is expected to practice this week, ESPN's Stephen Holder reported.
There's a chance Pierce suffers a setback before making his long-awaited 2026 debut, but as of now, all signs are pointing to his return happening ahead of the Colts' preseason finale against the Detroit Lions on Saturday.
There's not much time left for Pierce to get up to full strength before the regular season arrives on September 13, so getting back in the swing of things sooner rather than later is massive.
Cornerback Charvarius Ward Sr. had a strong training camp performance before he was sidelined for weeks with a back injury.
He was already coming back from a concussion-littered 2025 campaign that nearly caused him to retire, so another setback was tough for Ward to deal with.
Ward returned to practice today for the first time since his back injury popped up mid-camp, and now the Colts have their starting cornerback opposite Sauce Gardner, just in time as the 2026 regular season quickly approaches.
Star tight end Tyler Warren went down with a groin injury in the Colts' second-to-last training camp practice and has been sidelined ever since.
However, the good news was that Warren is dealing with a minor injury that won't keep him out of the regular season, but his absence is still hard to accept.
With just two weeks left until the regular season officially arrives, the Colts are prepared to ease Warren back into the mix instead of rushing him back.
Head coach Shane Steichen said the Colts will be smart with Warren, so his extended absence shouldn't be concerning, but rather reassuring that Indy isn't rushing back the focal point of their offense.
