title: 4 Options After Chargers Reveal Final Tyler Biadasz Injury News
full_text:
It’s officially over for Tyler Biadasz and the Los Angeles Chargers in 2026.
The Chargers were trying to hold out hope that Biadasz might be able to return later in the 2026 season after recovering from a serious knee injury.
In the wake of the Chargers’ second preseason game, though, the team put an end to that with the reveal that Biadasz will move to injured reserve.
The crusher: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport , Biadasz “exhausted all options before the move was made. Likely meaning, no return is possible.
So, where do the Chargers go from here?
The Chargers drafted Slaughter to play guard, despite being a college center. He’s back at center now and will stay there. Barring a shocker, he’s the unquestioned starter. But his reps in preseason Week 2 were up-and-down, as expected.
More concerning, at least for now, is just who might actually emerge at left guard, where at least three names still appear to have a chance at starting there.
Now 32 years old, Daniel Brunskill spent last year with Miami. That wasn’t his only connection to Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, either, given his years in San Francisco from 2019-2022. Right now, he’s currently with Washington, but it’s an option worth exploring as a backup if he doesn’t make it through final cuts or winds up on the trade block.
Graham Glasgow and James Daniels are two veterans with the ability to play multiple spots on the interior of an offensive line.
Glasgow is 34 years old and spent the last few years in Detroit. He’d need to be willing to accept a backup and mentor-type role behind Slaughter, though.
Similar story for Daniels, who happened to spend last year in Miami, but saw his three-year deal become just one after an injury derailed things. He’s still 28 years old, but would need to accept a spot behind Slaughter.
Because of the absolute mess that is left guard, this is an extremely uncomfortable place for the Chargers to be right now. Finding a backup center isn’t that big of a deal. Neither is starting a rookie center, provided the veterans around him are reliable.
But left guard is a question mark, right guard always felt a little unaddressed with Cole Strange and Rashawn Slater has already had a minor injury setback at a tackle spot. Instead of the best-ever line with a flashy new coordinator, the conversation shifts to whether the line can even be better than last year’s unit.

title: One Rams Draft Pick May Be in Danger of Missing the 53-Man Roster
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams selected Tim Keenan III in April’s draft, it appeared he had a clear path to the roster in a developmental role on the defensive line. However, as the Rams get closer to final roster cutdowns, it’s possible Keenan III isn’t included on that final 53 .
It’s no secret that the Rams have one of the more competitive rosters in the NFL. While a draft pick may have a guaranteed roster spot or be provided with additional roster security on most teams, that isn’t the case on the Rams’ roster.
That was proven last year when the Rams cut linebacker Chris Paul Jr., who they had drafted in the fifth round. Paul was the first Rams draft pick to be cut as a rookie since 2019, when the team waived Dakota Allen before signing him to the practice squad.
While the Rams used their final draft pick in the seventh round on Keenan , there was a lot to like about the selection. The term ‘draft steal’ can get overused, but that looked to be the case with Keenan.
Keenan was an excellent run defender at Alabama and as an older prospect, it was thought that he might be able to get into the rotation early. At the very least, he looked like a potential future replacement for Poona Ford. Ford’s contract expires at the end of 2027, but the Rams have an out at the end of the 2026 season.
Los Angeles @RamsNFL Rookie Tim Keenan Is A Monster In The Middle | Film Review pic.twitter.com/eBOAtEEu80
Even if Keenan didn’t take over in 2027, he appeared to be someone the Rams could place on a developmental path at nose tackle similar to those of Greg Gaines, Sebastian Joseph-Day and Tyler Davis.
Given the depth on the defensive line , it was always going to be difficult for Keenan III to make a strong impression early. However, as the Rams get closer to roster cutdowns and the preseason finale,It seems like Keenan is firmly on the roster bubble rather than safely inside the final 53.
Pro Football Focus isn’t the end-all, be-all, but it is worth noting that among defensive linemen with at least 40 snaps, Keenan’s overall grade of 30.0 ranks 108th out of 110 players. Keenan is supposed to excel against the run and he currently has a run defense grade of 29.7. That ranks 102nd. He does have a run stop rate of 11.1 percent, but that’s still only average.
Again, the Rams have a lot of depth on the defensive line and Ty Hamilton didn’t play in the second preseason game, signaling he might be a lock for the roster. Additionally, if Aaron Donald opts to return to the team , it’s going to be difficult to keep seven defensive linemen.
At this point, it might be easier for the Rams to cut Keenan and then re-sign him to the practice squad if he clears waivers. It’s the approach that they took with Allen in 2019 and it’s one that could make the most sense with Keenan.
The Rams haven’t gotten strong production from the undrafted free agents that they signed on the defensive line. Jaxson Moi hasn’t stood out and may be someone the Rams opt not to bring back
It’s certainly possible that Keenan’s draft status earns him the benefit of the doubt during roster cutdowns. However, the Rams haven’t been afraid to move on from draft picks early if they aren’t meeting expectations. If Keenan doesn’t perform well against the Chargers, his best chance of remaining on the team may be on the practice squad.

title: Rams Film Review: Wesley Bailey Is Proving He Belongs on the 53-Man Roster
full_text:
Throughout the preseason, few players have improved their spot on the Los Angeles Rams’ roster more than edge rusher Wesley Bailey. As an undrafted free agent, a roster spot was always going to be difficult to come by, and that was especially the case on the edge. However, after recording 10 pressures against the New Orleans Saints, a roster spot seems much more likely. It’s no longer a question of whether Bailey deserves a spot on the final 53, but how the Rams could possibly leave him off.
Following the conclusion of the 2026 NFL Draft, the Los Angeles Rams signed 16 undrafted free agents to compete for roster spots, with Bailey being one of them. While those undrafted free agents would be competing for roster spots, making the roster wasn’t going to be easy. A more realistic goal for this undrafted free agent class would be the practice squad.
The Rams’ roster has improved significantly since the 2023 season when the Rams brought in 26 undrafted free agents. At most, there were only a handful of roster spots even available. That was even more difficult on the edge, where the Rams already had established players like Myles Garrett, Byron Young, Josaiah Stewart, and Desjuan Johnson.
When the Rams signed Bailey, he was one of their better undrafted free agents . Bailey had an elite athletic profile with a Relative Athletic Score of 9.83. He had a similar athletic profile to top edge rushers like Boye Mafe and Brian Burns. However, making the roster at the edge rusher spot seemed like an uphill battle. A best-case scenario looked like it would be the practice squad for his rookie season.
Coming out of Louisville, Bailey was an older prospect at 25 and had middling production. He only had six sacks in his final season at Louisville. It was his only season with more than five sacks. Those two factors are largely why Bailey went undrafted. However, the Rams bet on his elite athletic traits and have coached him up.
Following the first two preseason games, Bailey may not make it to the practice squad if the Rams cut him during roster cutdowns. He’s gone from an undrafted free agent to potentially a hot commodity if he hits the waiver wire. While he was credited with no pressures in the preseason opener against the Kansas City Chiefs, he certainly made his presence felt. Against the Saints on Saturday, Bailey had 10 pressures.
Wesley Bailey just made his presence felt all afternoon on the Rams defense. Creates pressure on the backside here to force Rattler to throw off balance and dirt the ball in the red zone. Next play was the INT pic.twitter.com/WRKAIZjBkg
Bailey became the fifth player since 2023 to have 10 pressures in a single preseason game. The other four were Trey Hendrickson, Aidan Hutchinson, Micah Parsons, and Jonathan Cooper. His 10 pressures were twice as many as any other player in Week 2 of the preseason. According to Tru Media, Bailey is just the third player since at least 2017 with at least one sack, one forced fumble, and four quarterback hits in a preseason game.
“I thought you felt his presence all day,” said head coach Sean McVay after the game. “His body of work today compared to last week was an improvement, and he did some really good things last week. Being able to force the fumble, but I've mentioned it before, there are certain guys you feel on defense where you know they're making their presence felt, and that was how I felt about ‘Wes’ Bailey all day today.”
That’s not to say that Bailey is the same caliber of player or pass rusher as Hutchinson, Parsons, or Hendrickson. However, good players are supposed to dominate in the preseason, and that’s exactly what Bailey has done.
Nothing to see here...just Wesley Bailey taking the Saints' RT for a ride into Zach Wilson. Bailey power jumps off the tape on the bull rush. It's like watching a preseason version of Jared Verse. pic.twitter.com/aZE6ule1Yy
Bailey’s power immediately pops on tape. Not to compare him to Jared Verse, but his bull rush and ability to carry offensive tackles into the quarterback’s lap are similar. It’s like watching a preseason version of Verse.
With that said, Bailey has more than just the bull rush in his toolbox. There’s some finesse to his game as well, and that was evident when he sacked Zach Wilson on Saturday. Bailey attacked the right tackle’s chest before ripping underneath and getting to the quarterback. Earlier in the game, he gave a hard inside step and then crossed the offensive tackle’s face to win outside and flush Wilson out of the pocket.
The first career sack for Rams UDFA EDGE Wesley Bailey. Engages with the RT and then rips underneath to get to the QB. I really don't know how you keep him off the roster. pic.twitter.com/BMjJ90315L
Watching Bailey, it’s obvious how badly he wants it. Due to Myles Garrett and Byron Young missing time with knee issues , Bailey has gotten more reps than he might’ve had if they had been healthy. He hasn’t allowed those additional opportunities to go to waste.
This is a player giving everything he has to make the roster. Every play, he’s giving 100 percent, and his motor runs extremely hot. Whether that’s chasing down the quarterback or punching at the ball at the goal line to force a fumble, he doesn’t give up on a play.
The motor on Wesley Bailey is just absolutely relentless. Bailey crashes inside, finds the ball, and then gets the hit on Wilson. pic.twitter.com/XV5gAI8mt8
Over the past several years, the Rams have had a knack for finding players late in the draft or as undrafted free agents. Alaric Jackson was an undrafted free agent and has been the guy to take over for Andrew Whitworth. The Rams have also gotten contributions from undrafted free agents such as Jaylen McCollough and Josh Wallace.
If the Rams are going to trade away young, promising talent such as Verse along with premier draft capital, they have to be able to hit on the occasional late-round draft pick and undrafted free agent. For as much as the Rams relied on Matthew Stafford, Von Miller, and Jalen Ramsey to win the Super Bowl in 2021, players like Nick Scott, Travin Howard, and David Edwards also played key roles as Day 3 draft picks.
Through two preseason games, Bailey has defied the odds and put himself in a position to make the roster . There may not have appeared to be room for another edge rusher at the beginning of training camp, but he’s made the Rams reconsider. Back in 2022, Lance McCutcheon’s preseason performance forced the team to keep seven wide receivers.
Bailey will still have another preseason game to solidify his place, but he may not need it. The Rams will face several difficult decisions during roster cutdowns, but keeping Bailey should be easy.

title: Sean McVay Not Ready to Name Winner of Rams’ Backup Quarterback Battle
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams practiced on Monday for the first time since their preseason game against the Saints. Heading into the Saints’ game, there was a lot of discussion and focus around the battle for the backup quarterback position. Stetson Bennett seemed to answer that call with his performance, but it’s certainly something that will be a focal point as the Rams get closer to the regular season.
Throughout much of the offseason, Bennett had taken most, if not all, of the backup quarterback reps behind Matthew Stafford over Ty Simpson. However, that changed last week following Simpson’s standout performance against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Simpson split reps during the joint practice with the Saints on Thursday. After Bennett only played two drives in the preseason opener, the two quarterbacks each played one full half against the Saints. On Monday, Bennett took nine of the 15 reps while Simpson took six. It’s been a much more even split recently.
While Bennett performed well against the Saints , throwing for 181 yards and rushing for two touchdowns, it doesn’t appear as if the coaching staff is ready to make a decision on the backup quarterback spot. The longer the Rams wait, the more the pressure will build to make a decision.
Head coach Sean McVay was asked whether a decision had been made and if that had been communicated to either quarterback.
“No, absolutely not,” said McVay. “We haven't talked about that or decided that yet. We can talk about it, but we haven't decided that yet.”
It’s possible that the Rams are waiting to see if Simpson will overtake Bennett by the end of the preseason. The rookie has certainly closed the gap, and their numbers are extremely close. At this point, the only edge Bennett seems to have is his experience in the offense.
Rams QB preseason stats... Stetson Bennett: 23/37 (62.2%), 219 yds, 5.9 YPA, 2 total TDs, 78.5 passer rating, 69.2 PFF Grade Ty Simpson: 29/37 (78.4%), 263 yds, 7.1 YPA, 2 TDs, 114. 3 passer rating, 65.8 PFF Grade Through two games, it is VERY close.
The second preseason game against the Saints was an even 50-50 split between Bennett and Simpson. It truly felt like an open competition. However, that may not be the case against the Los Angeles Chargers in the finale.
McVay confirmed on Monday that Simpson would play against the Chargers, but did not say the same about Bennett. The uncertainty surrounding the rotation was similar to the situation before the Chiefs game.
“I don't know exactly how I'm going to allocate those reps,” said McVay. “We’ve got two guys who have played really good football throughout the course of camp and stuff like that. And I'll tell you what, Matthew Caldwell has got some stuff to him too. But the point I'm making is I have not decided on what that approach is.”
As much as many want the Rams to have a quarterback competition , it’s very likely not going to be won over a single preseason game. The Rams have seen Simpson and Bennett grow over the course of training camp and practices during the week.
At this point, it’s about which quarterback benefits most from the live-game reps during the preseason. Right now, that is undoubtedly Simpson. Simpson had limited playing experience at Alabama, with just one season as the starter. He has more to gain from live-game reps, especially given that he’s the team’s future at the position. As McVay mentioned, Matthew Caldwell can be thrown in that conversation as well.
We’ll see what McVay decides, but it wouldn’t be surprising to see Simpson play the entire first half or first three quarters, with Caldwell closing out the game. The Rams generally know what they have in Bennett. Against the Saints, he showed he can operate the offense efficiently with a more extended look.
There doesn’t seem to be anything more for Bennett to prove . Following a middling performance against the Chiefs, he bounced back in a big way on Saturday. That could factor into McVay’s decision on whether or not he plays against the Chargers.
“I thought he made good decisions, had some good opportunities and was pleased with the two-minute,” said McVay. “The fourth-down conversion was an unbelievable play, and two rushes for two touchdowns, being able to use his legs. I thought there was a lot of good stuff there.”
The Rams have not yet decided on their quarterback rotation for Saturday’s game or who will be the backup quarterback. If Bennett sits while Simpson gets another extended opportunity, it could indicate that the Rams already feel comfortable entering the season with Bennett as Stafford’s backup and want to maximize Simpson’s reps.

title: Stock Report: Which Rams Helped or Hurt Themselves in Preseason Rout of Saints
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams took down the New Orleans Saints in dominant fashion on Saturday, 34-0. With roster spots on the line, several players helped their cases while others potentially slipped. Let’s take a look at this week’s stock report.
It’s going to be very difficult for the Rams to keep Wesley Bailey off the roster . Bailey had 10 pressures against the Saints, which was twice as many as any other player. The last four players to have 10 pressures in a preseason game were Aidan Hutchinson, Trey Hendrickson, Micah Parsons, and Jonathan Cooper. All four of those guys are premier pass rushers in the NFL, and two of them are elite. Bailey did what good players are supposed to do in the preseason, and that’s dominate.
Nothing to see here...just Wesley Bailey taking the Saints' RT for a ride into Zach Wilson. Bailey power jumps off the tape on the bull rush. It's like watching a preseason version of Jared Verse. pic.twitter.com/aZE6ule1Yy
It’s unclear if Dean Connors was dealing with an injury of some sort, but after scoring two touchdowns against the Chiefs, he only played six snaps on Saturday. Following an impressive performance, many were excited to see Connors in action against the Saints. However, it’s possible the Rams are trying to hide him and sneak him onto the practice squad. Last year, they lost Cody Schrader after a good preseason. They may be trying to avoid that.
Heading into the weekend, it was worth wondering if Bennett had started to fall behind Ty Simpson a little bit. Those questions were quickly put to rest as Bennett went 19-for-31 for 181 yards and rushed for two touchdowns. B ennett quickly reminded everyone that he’s the player with three previous years of experience in the preseason. He’s more experienced in the offense, and that was very obvious against the Saints as he got a more extended look.
Probably the best throw from Bennett. Still have no idea how he completed this. Rams offense facing 4th down. Changes is arm angle to sidearm the ball around the rusher, goes over two Saints DBs...and drops it in the bucket. Stafford possessed on that one. pic.twitter.com/f1l2148IXM
It might be within the realm of possibility that Tim Keenan gets cut and then stashed on the practice squad despite him being a seventh-round pick. Keenan was a pick at nose tackle made for the future, but he hasn’t been good in the preseason. He had a 32.3 overall defense grade via PFF against the Saints. Among players with at least 40 snaps in the preseason, Keenan ranks 108th out of 110 defensive linemen.
Throughout much of training camp, Hunter has arguably been on the roster bubble. The Rams have three locks at running back, and there’s no guarantee they’ll keep a fourth. Hunter ran hard against the Saints and has proven to be difficult to take down at the next level. He has seven missed tackles forced in the preseason, which is the third-most among running backs. His three runs of 10 or more yards also lead all running backs. However, his strongest case for the roster will be his impact in pass protection. Hunter is the highest-grade running back in pass blocking via PFF.
If Jarquez Hunter has a case to make the Rams' roster, it's this. Hunter is the top-graded RB in pass protection during the preseason. This play stood out live...had to grab it. pic.twitter.com/NxQ08SHDER

title: Rams Get Key Offensive Lineman Back Ahead of Preseason Finale
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are getting some much-needed depth to their offensive line. Throughout the entirety of training camp, the Rams have been without their top interior depth piece in Justin Dedich . Dedich passed a physical on Monday and has been activated by the team.
Dedich had missed the entirety of training camp with a non-fireworks related hand injury that he suffered on the Fourth of July. The Rams placed Dedich on the Non-Football Injury list last month and were waiting for his return to the field.
Last week, head coach Sean McVay seemed optimistic that Dedich could be close to returning.
“He is actually able to start doing some different things where he'll put a cast on that will allow him to be able to participate," said McVay. "We're going to see how he feels doing some different things."
While Dedich may need to play with a cast to start the season, it appears that he reacted well to some of the different things that the Rams put him through now that he passed his physical. Dedich won’t be expected to start the season as Steve Avila and Kevin Dotson are healthy, but he has shown himself to be a quality depth option.
Last season, Dedich started six games for the Rams, including the playoff win against the Carolina Panthers in place of Dotson. He also played at left guard in place of Avila early in the season Dedich performed well enough in that stint to make Avila earn his place back.
That ability for Dedich to play on both sides of the offensive line in a pinch is important. Dedich has only played at left and right guard for the Rams, but he has center experience from college.
The Rams have remained healthy on the offensive line for much of the offseason, but have suffered some injuries among their depth players. Keagen Trost is out with a hamstring injury and will be pushing for a return ahead of Week 1.
Trost is a player who provides guard-tackle flexibility. Getting Dedich back will provide a boost to that depth. With Alaric Jackson potentially facing a suspension , the Rams could be relying on their offensive line depth much earlier in the season than they would like.
With uncertainty around Jackson and Trost’s availability, getting Dedich back before the preseason finale so that he can start preparing for Week 1 is ideal. Dedich may only be a depth player, but simply having him available strengthens a depth group that was starting to look thin.

title: Rams Sign CB Steven Gilmore in Latest Wave of Roster Moves
full_text:
Following their second preseason game , the Los Angeles Rams made two additional signings on Monday. The Rams signed edge rusher Devean Deal and cornerback Steven Gilmore to the roster. They placed cornerback Zech McPhearson and edge rusher Keir Thomas on injured reserve in corresponding moves.
Deal was an undrafted free agent out of TCU who was signed by the Seattle Seahawks after the draft. However, he was cut on May 14 to make room on the roster for wide receivers Rashad Rochelle and Trayvon Rudolph.
Throughout his collegiate career at Tulane and TCU, Deal appeared in 58 games, making 35 starts. He recorded 182 tackles, 112 pressures, 14 sacks and five forced fumbles. During the New Mexico Bowl in 2024, Deal earned defensive MVP honors for the game.
The cameras panned to Bill Belichick after Devean Deal picked up the Gio Lopez fumble and took it for a touchdown 😂 This game is way out of hand now, it’s one of the biggest blowouts of the week. DAMN BILL. pic.twitter.com/ECUOm1xGyS
As the Rams head into their third preseason game, the goal will be to simply fill out the roster with players who can take snaps. It’s highly unlikely that Deal makes the roster or even the practice squad. However, Saturday’s game against the Chargers will be an opportunity to put out tape for other teams. With Keir Thomas going to injured reserve, the move could also increase Wesley Bailey’s chances of making the roster .
There was some confusion when cornerback Zech McPhearson didn’t play on Saturday . However, it’s clear he was dealing with an injury now that he’s been placed on injured reserve. With McPhearson going on injured reserve, the Rams signed Gilmore to provide depth at cornerback for the preseason finale.
Gilmore was an undrafted free agent in 2023 for the Detroit Lions and played in three games. Over the last two years, he’s spent time in the UFL with the Birmingham Stallions. In 2025, Gilmore had the 10th-highest coverage grade in the UFL, according to PFF. However, he ranked 34th out of 40 cornerbacks in 2025. Gilmore also had a blocked field goal returned for a touchdown last season. He is also the brother of the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year Stephon Gilmore.
Steven Gilmore blocks the field goal. Scoops and scores by Gilmore as well!!! #ufl #stallions pic.twitter.com/J2itiZlRbF
Much like Deal, it’s highly unlikely that Gilmore makes the roster or even the practice squad. Saturday’s preseason finale will be an opportunity to put out tape that he can potentially send to other teams.
In another move, the Rams waived linebacker Daniel Rickert with an injury designation. Rickert was signed right before the preseason. While the signings of Deal and Gilmore shouldn’t impact the final roster, both players will have a chance to make an impression before roster cuts. The Rams will begin preparing for the final preseason game on Saturday against the Los Angeles Chargers.

title: What Rams’ Preseason Snap Counts Tell Us About the 53-Man Roster
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams wrapped up their second preseason game on Saturday , beating the New Orleans Saints 34-0. When it comes to the preseason, the Rams typically don’t play their starters or those they see as key depth. If a player doesn’t play, it tends to mean that they are a lock for the final 53-man roster heading into the season.
Following the second preseason game, here’s a list of players who haven’t played in the preseason as well as players who have missed one game.
It does seem notable that the Rams signed Alex Bachman after the first preseason game to return punts and take Xavier Smith’s spot at wide receiver. An argument can be made that Smith was on the roster bubble heading into the preseason. However, following his 40-yard return that changed the game, it seems he’s locked up his roster spot. The same can be said for Beaux Limmer.
When AJ Arcuri didn’t play at all in the first preseason game, some took that as an indication that he made the roster. If Alaric Jackson is suspended,it’s possible that Arcuri is on the final 53-man roster. With that said, the Rams seem to be rotating guys on the offensive line. Arcuri was back on the field for Week 2.
There shouldn’t be any real surprises here. All of these players are starters or key depth. If there is one surprise, it might be Ronnie Rivers. Rivers has become the Troy Reeder of the offensive side of the ball. Given that he’s missed both games, Rivers’ roster spot seems like a lock.
It also seems notable that neither Konata Mumpfield nor David Quessenberry has played in the preseason. Both players are likely seen as key depth on offense. If the Rams are without Jackson, it looks like Quessenberry might be the guy to take his spot.
* Does Not Include Snaps on Special Teams
Desjuan Johnson not playing against the Saints seems notable . Given that he is important depth on the edge, it was somewhat surprising to see him play in the opener. Johnson didn’t play against the Saints, seemingly locking up his roster spot.
However, the decision not to play Hamilton is confusing. It was thought that Hamilton was on the roster bubble and now it’s possible Hamilton has made the roster. Elias Neal didn’t play the first game, but that may be more about the Rams wanting to rotate players at linebacker.
Much like the offensive side of the ball, there aren’t really any surprises here. All of these players are seen as starters or key depth going into the regular season. You could argue that a few of these players should be playing, but it’s better for the Rams not to risk injury.
* Does Not Include Snaps on Special Teams

title: Rams Film Review: Grading Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson in QB Battle
full_text:
Heading into Saturday’s preseason game against the New Orleans Saints, all eyes were on the Los Angeles Rams’ quarterback battle between Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson . After Simpson’s strong performance against the Kansas City Chiefs, the Rams’ coaching staff opened up the quarterback battle and gave each quarterback one half in the Saints’ game.
While some may have hoped for Simpson to start pulling away, that didn’t necessarily happen. There’s no doubt that the gap has been closed, but with a more extended look, Bennett’s experience in the system showed.
The Rams have played two preseason games, and each quarterback’s performance has almost mirrored the other. In the first game, it was Bennett with a middling performance while Simpson impressed. On Saturday, Bennett impressed while Simpson had a middling performance.
Given Bennett’s experience, the Rams likely saw enough against the Saints. It would be somewhat surprising if the Rams played Bennett at all against the Los Angeles Chargers in the finale.
The Rams had Bennett as the starter against the Saints, and after punting on the opening drive, the offense would go on to score four straight times. Bennett settled in, and his experience and knowledge of the offense were evident .
Easy to see that Stetson Bennett has experience in the Rams offense. Knows exactly where everybody is gonna be. Eyes start left, he comes back right, ball is out by the time his foot hits the top of his drop. pic.twitter.com/CyC5iMRx4a
Bennett knows exactly where each receiver running a route is going to be and trusts that they’ll be there. In the play above, Bennett starts looking to his left, and by the time he reaches the top of his drop, he’s come back to his right, and the ball is out to Brennan Presley on the short hitch.
While it may have only been the preseason, Bennett looked like a seasoned veteran . This is someone playing in his fourth preseason, and that experience showed on the field. He looked like a seasoned veteran on the field.
Probably the best throw from Bennett. Still have no idea how he completed this. Rams offense facing 4th down. Changes is arm angle to sidearm the ball around the rusher, goes over two Saints DBs...and drops it in the bucket. Stafford possessed on that one. pic.twitter.com/f1l2148IXM
On arguably his best throw of the day, you would have thought Bennett had been possessed by Matthew Stafford. With the Rams’ offense facing fourth down, Bennett adjusted his arm angle to throw around the incoming pass rushers. He somehow managed to loft the ball over two Saints’ defensive backs and drop it right in the bucket of Tyler Scott coming across. Scott is covered by two Saints’ defenders, and Bennett manages to throw him open.
Last year, Bennett had his best preseason to date. During his first two years, Bennett had a tendency to put the ball into harm’s way and was prone to turning the ball over. However, last year things started to click for Bennett, and he began to gain confidence, especially when throwing outside the numbers. Bennett went to that throw multiple times on Saturday.
You saw Bennett throw this pass a few times last year. Far hash to far sideline outside the numbers is not as easy throw by any means. The Rams QB with a really nice ball to Alex Bachman on 2nd-and-20. pic.twitter.com/8qXGxnSkgf
That throw from the far hash to the far sideline is a positive sign of an NFL-caliber quarterback . It’s a throw that requires good arm strength and velocity, as the ball has to travel 40+ yards and cover a lot of grass. This isn’t to call Bennett elite, but it’s impressive nonetheless, and he completed that throw multiple times.
Where Bennett may have been most impressive when using his legs. That’s part of Bennett’s game that head coach Sean McVay appreciates. When the pocket breaks down, what can you do? Both of Bennett’s touchdowns came on scrambles. The second one was especially notable and shows his understanding of what's going on down the field.
These plays out of structure are what McVay absolutely loves about Bennett. When the pocket crashes, what do you do? Bennett makes something happen with his legs and it results in a Rams TD. pic.twitter.com/NHa7OPnSzv
With the edge breaking contain and crashing inside, Bennett escapes the pocket to the right, knowing there’s going to be open space because his receiver downfield is coming across on a slant inside. Bennett is able to use his speed to beat the Saints’ defenders to the corner for the score.
There’s little doubt that Bennett played well, but that’s also not to say that he was perfect. Bennett can sometimes make the easy look hard and the hard look easy. On the first red zone possession, Bennett floats a ball over Jordan Waters running in the flat, and the ball is almost intercepted. He also threw behind CJ Daniels on a slant, which is something that he did last week as well.
A few balls got away from Bennett, but overall the performance was an improvement from last week. Overall Grade: A-
The narrative coming out of the game on Saturday is that Simpson was outplayed by Bennett following his strong debut , and that isn’t necessarily wrong. However, it does lack a lot of context. When Simpson took over last week, it was a tie game at 3-3. On Saturday, Simpson didn’t touch the ball until 7:34 left in the third quarter with the Rams leading 27-0.
It may only be the preseason, but the Rams also aren’t trying to run the score up on the Saints. At that point, the goal is simply to get out of the game healthy and go home. However, there were still some positives to take away from Simpson’s performance.
Was nice to see Ty Simpson use his legs a little bit yesterday. Thought he showed good pocket movement here to avoid the rush and then take off to pick up the first down for the Rams offense. Turns nothing into something. pic.twitter.com/JjCdpwo5Q1
One thing that we didn’t see last week was Simpson using his legs. He may not be a mobile quarterback, but he does have the ability to take off and run. On his second possession, Simpson navigates the pocket and then takes off with his legs. Simpson turned nothing into something and did the smart thing by sliding at the end of the play.
The Rams did take some of the training wheels off Simpson in his second game. Against the Chiefs, Simpson had eight dropbacks out of play action, accounting for 32 percent of his dropbacks. He only had three against the Saints, accounting for 20 percent of his dropbacks.
Part of that was the game script, but Saturday’s offense was much more of a dropback passing game than it had been the week prior. One thing that you do have to appreciate with Simpson is his internal clock on those dropbacks.
One thing that you do have to appreciate with Simpson is his internal clock. It is very consistently 1...2...ball is out. He's not sitting in the pocket and patting the ball. Little high to Villari, but places it outside, which allows the Rams TE to turn upfield for the 1st. pic.twitter.com/npVFrG94YN
It was something that was evident last week, and that was the case again on Saturday. Very rarely does Simpson sit in the pocket and pat the ball. He goes through his progressions quickly, and the ball is out at the top of his drop.
You still would like to see Simpson push the ball downfield more. His average depth of target was just 4.8 yards compared to Bennett’s 9.9. Last week, it was just 5.3. The thing is, he can do it. When Simpson went down the field last week, he was accurate. That was the case again against the Saints’ secondary.
Here you see Simpson hit the same throw that Bennett did in the first half. The Rams rookie throws an accurate ball to Tru Edwards along the sideline. pic.twitter.com/fuhhLfFmJt
On the same throw that Bennett was hitting outside the numbers along the sideline, Simpson was able to complete a similar pass to Tru Edwards. It’s hard to know if Simpson would have pushed the ball downfield more had the game script not been out of hand, but…

title: Rams 53-Man Roster Prediction: Did Wesley Bailey Force His Way Into the Mix?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have wrapped up their second preseason game , which means it’s time for another 53-man roster prediction. Following the game against the New Orleans Saints, the 53-man roster got a lot more complicated. Wesley Bailey made a strong case at edge rusher with 10 pressures. Players like Jarquez Hunter, Cam Lampkin, and Al’Zillion Hamilton have made strong cases as well. Let’s take an updated look at the 53-man roster following Week 2 of the preseason.
The quarterback position remains straight forward when it comes to the 53-man roster for the Rams. With both Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson on the roster, the Rams are keeping three quarterbacks. The question that remains is who enters the season as the backup . Following Saturday’s performance, it’s looking like that player might be Bennett.
It wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams keep four running backs. Jarquez Hunter has certainly done enough to show that he belongs on the roster. The same can be said about Dean Connors and Jordan Waters. However, the Rams should be able to go into the season with three and then keep one or two guys on the practice squad.
While Xavier Smith has arguably been on the roster bubble , it appears he may have locked up his spot. Smith didn’t play against the Saints and the Rams signed a punt returner for the preseason. It seems increasingly likely that the Rams keep six wide receivers.
These have been the five tight ends since the start of the offseason and that will remain the case.
I could see the Rams keeping 10 offensive lineman. This also gets very interesting if Jackson is suspended at the beginning of the season. In that case, Bill Murray, Austin Blaske, or AJ Arcuri could make the roster. However, right now the practice squad remains the most likely option for those three players.
The Rams could certainly use an upgrade at linebacker, but given who they have on the roster, these are the likely four that will make the 53.
Given how well Wesley Bailey has played in the preseason, it might be impossible for the Rams to keep him off the roster. Bailey had 10 pressures against the Saints and is one of only a handful of players to do that in a single game in the last four preseasons. The others are all premier edge rushers around the NFL. It’s going to be difficult to find room, but the Rams will find a way to make it happen.
If Aaron Donald comes back, it’s going to shake things up on the defensive line. The Rams could also sacrifice here to make room for Bailey. However, depth on the defensive line is important. It makes sense for the Rams to keep six here.
With the emergence of Bailey on the edge, Lampkin’s spot is teetering on the bubble. However, the Rams played Lampkin quite a bit in the slot against the Saints to test his versatility. Lampkin has done well enough to earn a roster spot.
My big change here is leaving off Tanner Ingle. Given Ingle’s special teams value, the Rams could certainly opt to keep him. With that said, the Rams have to make a cut somewhere with the emergence of Bailey, and safety makes sense. Josh Wallace has shown versatility and Lampkin did so on Saturday. The Rams should be able to get by with four.
Harrison Mevis is a perfect 4-for-4 in the preseason and Ethan Evans has punted well. The Rams haven’t brought in any serious competition on special teams. These three are set in stone.

title: Discussing Raiders' Laube’s Increased Role in Jeanty’s Absence
full_text:
Ashton Jeanty is one of the most important players on the Las Vegas Raiders' roster for the 2026 season. Unfortunately, the team could be without its star running back in the short term.
Jeanty suffered an injury during practice on Sunday, giving the organization a scare after he couldn't put weight on the injured leg. Head coach Klint Kubiak didn't give any further details about Jeanty's length of absence, but it is safe to assume that with a few weeks to go until the Raiders' home opener against the Miami Dolphins, there's a chance the 2025 No. 6 overall draft selection may not be ready.
This opens the door for the rest of the running back room to step up and shine in Jeanty's absence. Of course, rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. has received the most praise and excitement considering his preseason performances over the past two weeks, where he has broken off big, powerful runs. Kubiak seems confident in the running back room, crediting position coach Omar Young for their preparation.
"Yeah, I think [Mike Washington] had a good camp, and we have to go see him play really good football on Thursday," Kubiak said in the final training press conference on Tuesday. "But like you said, we've got a lot of other guys that have to step up, Dylan [Laube], we've got [Roman] Hemby, we've got Dare [Ogunbowale]. Omar [Young] is doing a great job coaching those guys and getting them ready."
Dylan Laube is the player who stands out to me the most in this running back room, not Washington. The former sixth-round pick in 2024 has many fans in the online draft community, but he has contributed to the Raiders' offense and special teams as both a change-of-pace running back and a return specialist.
I don't fully trust Washington in the passing game just yet. The Raiders have an opportunity to get a look at their young halfbacks in a committee approach. Laube is a player I think could be productive on the ground and as a receiver.
Laube is no Christian McCaffrey, but he is a good runner and pass-catcher. He can fulfill Jeanty's duties on third down with his increased role for the early slate of regular-season games.
Laube is one of the most versatile playmakers on the roster and is the No. 3 running back on the depth chart. His value to the program is already immense, but it grows even more in Jeanty's absence. This is a wonderful opportunity for the third-year running back out of New Hampshire.

title: Raiders Final Training Camp Practice: Winners & Losers
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders, moments ago, concluded their final practice for the 2026 NFL training camp, and to call this camp consequential could be one of the biggest understatements ever.
Last December, when the powers that be decided to move on from Pete Carroll, they also knew the time had come to rebuild the Raiders.
Gone were the shortcuts and quick fixes; now it was time for a disciplined plan to stay the course and get this once-storied and feared franchise back on track after over two decades of futility.
For a fan base that doesn’t wear the Silver and Black for fun, but sees it as a way of life , they have given them tangible reasons for hope.
Unlike the past several years, the franchise has stuck to the plan. GM John Spytek and his amazing staff of Brian Stark, Brandon Hunt, and Brandon Yeargan, along with each of their respective teams, have put together a roster full of young talent ready to get the Raiders' rebuild underway, with the goal of 2028 being the year they make the NFL Playoffs and then every year after that.
I asked Raider Nation to sound off now that training camp is over on what you came away with from camp, and as always, you were terrific.
Who's going to step up at WR and DT?
Great question. Both of those position groups, coming into and now out of camp, are the weakest links on their respective sides of the ball.
With the Raiders owning the first-round waiver claim, I would not be shocked if both of those groups (especially WR) add a player either by the waiver claim or trade before the season, as long as the said players fit the long-term plan.
That said, Tonka Hemingway would be my first bet at the defensive tackle position, and rookie Malik Benson from the wide receiver group.
Will there be hope for the future or will they pull the rug out from under our feet again? pic.twitter.com/l6DrclcVpg
I wish I had a way to like this Tweet more than just a simple heart and to share it in this article.
Todd, I have seen this franchise repeatedly self-sabotage over my seven years, and each time I've been dumbfounded.
That said, this time they have shown nine months of discipline. With a very small sample size, they have never gone this long staying on course during my time covering the team.
Tom Brady, while still the dominant voice in the organization, has entrusted Spytek more, based on people in the building privately talking, and all of them are letting Kubiak cook.
Kubiak, in turn, has an uncanny trust with management, and certainly a lot will be told throughout the season, but up to this point, I am optimistic, not as a Raiders’ fan, but as a football fan, that the Raiders are getting it right this time for now.
Where are we realistically in terms of what is achievable this season? What does a good season look like?
Ian, this is a great question.
I can tell you with 100% certainty that this is already a better and more talented team than last year. That said, with youth everywhere, there's a learning curve. Not only is your head coach a first-time head man, but so are your offensive and defensive coordinators, a projected eight to 12 rookies, multiple young players, and, oh, by the way, your No. 1 overall pick, QB Fernando Mendoza.
As I reported before, 2026 is a rebuild, and every loss this year ensures more and better players next year, laying the foundation for a 2027 get-right campaign, and finally 2028 as the goal of making, and perennially staying, in the NFL Playoffs.
Last May, I projected seven wins in 2026. I stand by that today, but I will give my final prediction in the first week of the season.

title: Raiders Showing Progress Across Roster Ahead of Preseason Finale
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' Tuesday practice was their last one before Thursday night's preseason matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. The Raiders have gradually improved with each practice, while working through the ups and downs that come with significant change.
Through all of the changes Las Vegas is implementing, everything about them has been different. Klint Kubiak's coaching staff has made the most of their practices, as each has witnessed them take a step forward in some aspect. Tuesday was no different.
On Tuesday, Las Vegas practiced without pads, but was still productive. The Raiders' defense consistently pressured their teammates on offense throughout team drills. Still, Las Vegas' offense had its moments, with multiple chunk plays through the air but little success on the ground.
Tuesday's practice was proof that the Raiders' offense is headed in the right direction. The unit will benefit greatly from a few additional weeks of practice leading up to their Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, but so far, Las Vegas' offense is taking tangible steps forward.
Las Vegas' offense was vocal on Tuesday, but respectfully celebrated their wins as a unit. Tuesday was the most polished the Raiders' offense has looked through training camp, which is to be expected. Las Vegas' offense is where it needs to be at this point in the preseason.
The true test will be the regular season, but the growth the Raiders' offense has shown since their game against the Houston Texans less than a week ago has been noticeable. Offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko recently shared his thoughts on the offense's progress so far.
“I think we're progressing as a team, we're progressing as an organization. We're trying to grow in all phases of our offense, every player, every position group,” Janocko said after practice.
“Ultimately, Coach [Klint Kubiak] has the final say on how and when we're going to play this person, that person, and not just quarterback, but any position group, and how players develop over time. We like to see the guys develop in practice; we like to see what they're doing in these preseason games and then basing decisions on that."
Similar growth has been equally noticeable on the defensive side of the ball, as they work through the process of working as one. On Tuesday, Las Vegas' defense defended a high number of passes throughout the team period, giving their defensive backfield and linebackers a chance to improve.
The Raiders' defensive backfield is its most significant vulnerability on that side of the ball. However, they aim to use a solid rotation along the defensive line and the significantly improved group of starting linebackers to help compensate. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard explained.
“The [defensive backfield has] responded really well. I think that's a collective effort from their teammates, from the position coach. Feeling the love and support as if any human being isn't having success with something of uplifting them within those moments,” Leonard said.
“I think it's been really good. That starts with your culture. It reflects of when a teammate's down, how do you react? Is he sitting there by himself? Genuine care and love for that person based on how they're working. And it's been fun to see. I certainly don't feel alone doing that and picking up these guys.”
More notably, all three units showed signs of progress on Tuesday. Although this is the case every day, Tuesday witnessed the Raiders coaching staff set aside an excessive amount of time to focus heavily on special teams. This was one of the most intriguing aspects of practice.
Tuesday confirmed Las Vegas' plans to be versatile on special teams just as much as they aim to be on offense and defense. After how badly their special teams unit played last season, especially in the first half of the season, Tuesday was a refreshing sight to behold.
The Raiders are another step closer to the regular season, but neither the players nor the coaching staff are looking much further ahead than Thursday night. After that, Kubiak and his staff will begin making roster cuts ahead of Sunday's deadline to do so.
As Las Vegas enters its first regular season under Kubiak, the upcoming roster decisions will be the most critical of his early tenure in the desert.

title: Every Raiders Player Who Helped Their Roster Chances in Preseason
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have been hard at work sorting through installations and much more. Soon, another wave of roster decisions will be made.
Below are several Raiders who have helped their roster and depth chart chances throughout the offseason and the team's first two preseason games.
Las Vegas moved on from Charles Snowden in a surprising offseason move. The additions of Kwity Paye and Keyron Crawford afforded them the flexibility to do so. However, so did the addition of Johnson, who has paired a solid training camp with two impressive preseason performances.
Johnson could very easily be a player who buys Rob Leonard and the Raiders' defensive ends higher on the depth chart a few plays off. Five or 10 plays a game for Johnson could take some of the load off Maxx Crosby, Paye, and others.
The Raiders need all the help they can get at cornerback. Vance has continued to show improvement this offseason. The talented corner has intercepted Fernando Mendoza twice in practice; both would have been returned for touchdowns in live action.
As the Raiders look to deploy many different looks this season, Vance has earned more opportunities.
Masses is a player the Raiders will depend on heavily this season. He has already worked his way up from a mid-round draft pick to a potential starter in a defense desperately in need of what he does well. Still, the rookie must continue to develop.
As the Raiders look for wide receivers who can consistently do their job, Benson has shot up the depth chart. The sixth-round pick has gone from potentially not making the roster to having a chance to earn plenty of playing time for the Raiders on Sundays.
Benson has further development to show, as his two drops against the Texans proved. However, if he stays focused and continues to produce, he may be the steal of the draft.
Some believed the Raiders might look to trade O'Connell this offseason. However, that always seemed unlikely, with the uncertainty surrounding Kirk Cousins' health and performance this season. Still, if there was any doubt the Raiders would keep him this season, it is now gone.
Las Vegas could need a backup quarterback in the blink of an eye. Should that happen, they will be prepared. O'Connell, as he has for most of his professional career, will be there to keep them afloat as long as necessary. His preseason performance against the Texans spoke volumes.
"I think Aidan [O’Connell], like all of those guys, to play quarterback in this league, you have to be very intelligent, and you have to be functionally intelligent," Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko said about O'Connell following the team's win over the Texans.
"The things that Aidan sees, based off of his experience, and things he's seen, whether he's played the game or some of the other quarterbacks he's been around, he just brings a wealth of knowledge to the position that's really beneficial to everybody else and myself especially.”
“He sees things in a manner where he can see it from playing the game, and he can see it from a perspective of how a receiver may see it or how a running back may see it, how the overall offense sees it. So, I think his just overall awareness of game and position is really valuable to us."
Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean handle the starting linebacker duties for Las Vegas. Both are dependable, but the Raiders need their reserve linebackers to continue developing throughout the regular season. Las Vegas must keep Walker and Dean fresh; turning to their reserves will help.
Many believed Olubi would be largely a special-teams player when the Raiders signed him during the offseason. Although that will still be the case, Olubi has shown value in Las Vegas' defense. He needs more repetitions and playing time on Sundays, but the potential is there.
During training camp and, most recently, Las Vegas' preseason win over the Texans, Olubi showed flashes of what is possible as he gains experience in Leonard's defense and with his teammates. Leonard should sprinkle in defensive reps for Olubi and other reserves as soon as possible during the season.
As the Raiders continue their search for a solid starting and reserve offensive line, Mafi has quietly taken a step forward from where he was last season. Mafi's body looks more like that of an offensive lineman than it did last season. Physically, he looks like he is ready to fill in on the interior line.
Mafi is not a starter, but if he continues at his current pace, it is fair to believe he will not only quietly earn himself a roster spot but also thrive in a reserve role, should the Raiders need him. Entering the offseason with a new coaching staff made Mafi a player the Raiders could potentially move on from.
There is a lot going on at any given practice. Of the nearly 90 players Las Vegas has on the roster, many more helped their roster chances who are not listed here. Overall, the Raiders' roster has improved through both additions and subtractions.
Moving forward, Las Vegas aims to turn things around. However, that will take several seasons under Kubiak and several more offseasons of solid additions via free agency and the NFL Draft. So far, they have a roster full of players who have performed well. Far too many to name here.

title: How Raiders Will Handle the Absence of Ashton Jeanty
full_text:
There is no way around it: the Las Vegas Raiders sustained a significant blow Sunday morning when running back Ashton Jeanty suffered an injury in practice. Las Vegas' offense is versatile, but Jeanty's presence on the field adds a constant, game-changing potential to the unit.
Every team has players they cannot afford to lose to injury. As they rebuild and move forward under Klint Kubiak, Jeanty is undoubtedly one of those players. Luckily, along with all of the more notable roster moves the Raiders made this offseason, they quietly added multiple running backs.
Kubiak's offense is predicated on versatility and being able to use multiple running backs in various ways. Las Vegas' front office has supplied him with a handful of running backs the Raiders have spent training camp preparing alongside Jeanty. Now, they must compensate for the loss of the star back.
The Raiders played most of their starters against the Arizona Cardinals but decided against doing so in their second preseason game against the Houston Texans. Las Vegas' depth chart ahead of the 49ers game is the biggest indicator of how the Raiders will handle Jeanty's absence.
Las Vegas dodged a major bullet, finding out shortly after Jeanty's injury that it was not as severe as it looked on the practice field. Leaving practice on Sunday, no one would have been surprised if Jeanty's injury was season-ending. Luckily, it is not, as it seems Jeanty sprained his ankle.
The Raiders have not announced how long Jeanty will be out. However, with it being the first year of a full rebuild and only Jeanty's second in the league, there is no need to rush him back. Furthermore, Las Vegas has spent the offseason and training camp building their offense around multiple backs.
As they enter the 2026 season, the Raiders' group of running backs is as deep as it has been in recent seasons. At its core, Las Vegas' group of running backs, like its group of receivers, has gone from one primary back to a position group filled with multiple capable options.
There is no way to fully replace Jeanty, and it is certainly not possible to do so with one player. That uniqueness is why the Raiders used such a high pick on him. They will need the group of running backs as a whole to pick up the slack until Jeanty returns.
Below are the players Las Vegas will depend on out of the backfield until Jeanty returns.
Washington was one of the backs the Raiders quietly added this offseason. Selecting Washington in the fourth round one season after using the No. 6 overall pick on Jeanty raised a few eyebrows. However, so did Washington's play in Las Vegas' first two preseason games.
Washington registered a 53-yard run against the Cardinals and a 33-yard run against the Texans. His preseason performances and Jeanty's injury have presented an intriguing opportunity for Washington and the Raiders as a whole.
“Yeah, guys are earning roles. We're gathering information. He's a young guy, [RB] Mike [Washington Jr.] is, so we're learning more about him. If guys are having success, then they carve out roles. That's where he's headed, but I'll say it again. Mike's doing a great job running the ball. We got to keep getting him better in all facets of his game," Kubiak said after Thursday night's win over the Texans.
Laube, a late-round pick for the Raiders two offseasons ago, has etched out a spot on special teams each of the past two seasons and will do so again this season. Yet this offseason, during training camp and the preseason, Laube has shown growth as a runner. He averaged 6.2 yards per run against Houston.
Laube matched Washington's per-run average and registered a 13-yard long run as well. The Raiders will have to use all of the backs at their disposal while Jeanty recovers. Laube has the potential to help them on the ground or through the air.
Hemby is another rookie back the Raiders added this offseason who has seen action this preseason. Hemby gives the Raiders a strong runner who can get tough yards. He also gives the Raiders' play-callers flexibility, as defenses will not know whether to expect a run or a pass when he is in the game.
Ogunbowale may be far down the depth chart, but Jeanty's injury shows just how quickly depth can be needed. He may not see the field much, but he gives the Raiders a fourth option at running back.
Time will tell how long Jeanty is out, but the Raiders are much more equipped to deal with his injury this season than they were last season.

title: Raiders Snap Counts vs. Texans: Who Played the Most?
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' coaching staff decided to sit their starters against the Houston Texans in their second preseason game under head coach Klint Kubiak. With the deadline to trim their roster down to 53 players quickly approaching, the Raiders' coaching staff got a quality look at their roster.
Although the Raiders have a few positions solidified on both sides of the ball, depth is a major question facing Kubiak's staff as they head into the regular season. Their comeback preseason win over the Texans allowed several players a legitimate chance to earn a roster spot or more playing time.
Below are the snap counts from the Raiders' win over the Texans last Thursday. They have one preseason game remaining against the San Francisco 49ers this Thursday at Allegiant Stadium. Kubiak has not confirmed whether or not starters will play in that game.
Yet, after the injury to running back Ashton Jeanty , it may not be worth the risk to do so. Las Vegas may take the same approach to their final preseason game as they did against the Texans . Rightfully so. Still, based on their win over the Texans, their final preseason game provides value.
The Raiders' snap counts against the Texans offered clues about which position groups and players Las Vegas' coaching staff has its eye on most ahead of their upcoming preseason game. How the Raiders' coaching staff allotted the snaps against the Texans was interesting, to say the least.
After an offseason filled with offensive changes, the Raiders have worked tirelessly to iron out most aspects of their offense. There is still competition at offensive guard, among Las Vegas' wide receivers, and among their offensive linemen.
The Raiders' win over the Texans allowed their reserve offensive line to get ample work. The game also gave Kubiak's coaching staff an even closer look at the talent available to them.
Aidan O'Connell : 43 snaps
Most of the Raiders' defensive snaps went to players at positions where they still have significant depth questions. This includes their defensive backfield and reserve linebackers. Players in each position group got a thorough opportunity to earn a roster spot or more playing time.
The type of opportunity these players got against the Texans and may get against the 49ers is not always guaranteed in the National Football League for players further down the depth chart. Kubiak is truly letting the players make the roster decisions for themselves more than the coaching staff.
Tristin McCollum: 43 snaps
Las Vegas' week in Texas should have answered most of the questions the Raiders' coaching staff may have had about the core of their roster. Their starters will lead the way, but Las Vegas will undoubtedly turn to their reserves, and likely do so sooner rather than later.
With just under a week remaining until Las Vegas makes roster cuts, their win over the Texans and upcoming preseason match against the 49ers should help Las Vegas solidify the roster. Kubiak explained how valuable the team's work against the Texans was for their overall growth.
“I'm so glad we got the practice against them. That was really important for our team to spend that time in Houston and get some really good work against a different scheme and a really good coaching staff," Kubiak said following Las Vegas’ practice in Houston.
Following the preseason win over the Texans, Kubiak noted that the exhibition matchup "Helps a lot. These game reps are the most valuable ones that we can use. It's not just the defensive tape, but how they're performing on special teams, because so many guys in those positions have to prove their worth on teams. Guys that we can trust. So, it was very helpful for many guys.”

title: How Raiders Can 'Earn' Ability To Run Football
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have a clear identity this season under head coach Klint Kubiak, and that's to run the football.
Through two weeks of preseason action , we have seen the Raiders operate predominantly from under center and prioritize the rushing attack. While speaking with the media on Monday, center Tyler Linderbaum spoke about the importance of establishing the run .
Kubiak has proven to be one of the best offensive minds in the NFL, and his system highlights the run game. The Raiders experienced a scary moment on Sunday when running back Ashton Jeanty suffered a leg injury in practice.
The level of concern was high, as the second-year running back was unable to put weight on his leg as he was helped off the field.
Nevertheless, Las Vegas' offense will be built around the rushing attack. With Kirk Cousins presumably starting the season as QB1, the Raiders want to take as much pressure off the 38-year-old signal-caller with a strong backfield and offensive line. The offense's success will depend on those two departments' ability to work together.
Linderbaum was the premier offensive lineman in free agency this offseason, and he has been one of the best run-blocking centers since he entered the league. The Raiders' offense has promise, and the running game will be the key to unlocking the rest of the passing game. For that to happen, the offensive line must hold up its end of the bargain.

title: Raiders Training Camp Report 26: Pressure Rises As Regular Season Looms
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders wrapped up their second of three practices this week moments ago, ahead of the final preseason game on Thursday against the San Francisco 49ers and the NFL 53-man roster cut-down on Sunday.
With so much on the line as the regular season looms, we have the details and developments surrounding your Silver and Black in our 26th training camp report.
The Raiders, as individuals, rookies, and veterans, have shown a lot and did so again today. Still, they continue to give glimpses to their amazing fan base, who see their fandom as part of their identity and what they are becoming.
1. Very few jobs are settled on this roster. With only one preseason game left and one practice before Sunday’s cut-down day, DC Rob Leonard says players are still competing, a regular theme for Kubiak.
“Not as much ones and twos, but the players are aware and we're aware of where the competition is at, regardless of who's starting or who is not. There's some competitive position groups, without declaring. I mean, until we take the field, that’s still never ending. But they’re well aware of who’s competing and how important special teams is. It’s everything with these guys.”
2. 13 personnel is now in fashion with the Silver and Black. We know that Kubiak is an offensive genius, and TE Ian Thomas bragged about his coach’s play-designing and calling acumen.
"Oh, it's fun. It's fun when you can get three tight ends out there, obviously, and we try to pick each other up and encourage guys to keep going so we can keep three tight ends in the game. You can build that trust in us in the offense and the team build the trust in that tight end room. So, we've been trying to make it happen every day so we can keep getting chances."
3. The Raiders' special teams were terrible last year. I lay that at the feet of Pete Carroll, but Kubiak has prioritized that part of the game. I asked special teams savant Thomas about this team’s commitment to the previously under-prioritized part of the game.
"You're talking about the 25-minute period yesterday? It's good. Time on task. They say, ‘To be great at something, you need a lot of time on task.’ That’s what he's doing, and I love it. The more you can see all of these different looks, the better and more confident you feel. You don't feel rushed, you don't feel a lot of pressure.”
Thomas added, “So, Joe D [Joe DeCamillis] is putting a lot of guys in crazy positions. He's seen a bunch of different stuff from around the league, and he's coached a while. He's seen a lot of stuff, and you never doubt when someone like that tells you what to do, and you're like, 'Well, he knows something.' It's good to get the younger guys to actually acknowledge that part of it."
With a team that I project will carry as many as 12 and as few as eight rookies on that final 53-man squad, combined with multiple second- and third-year players, the future is very bright. Here are some rookie reports after today’s practice.
The Raiders' No. 1 overall pick, who had NFL executives raving about him during the 2026 NFL Draft process, had his worst day as a Raider on Monday. But today he rebounded like the champion he is, and the young man looked sharp and poised. TE Ian Thomas broke down what he saw from his fellow Indiana Hoosier.
"His confidence is through the roof, and I love it. The guys are always right behind him, pushing him to go forward. He's a number one overall, so you expect a lot out of him. But it's not easy going into a pro team, a pro level and making a splash right away. So, the more we can do to encourage him to do better, is better for us. He's been coming along real good, and everyone loves it. So yeah, like I said, he's an IU guy, and I love that too."
I prognosticated that the Raiders would keep ten defensive backs, six cornerbacks, and four safeties in my latest 53-man roster prediction. They could even keep 11, but the reality is that if they stick with ten, six of those will be young players.
If they keep 11, it would be a stunning seven considered young. Something that clearly spells out that the Raiders are going to take their lumps in 2026, but the future is bright. Leonard discussed his young defensive backfield.
“They’ve grown a lot. The highs and the lows. We’re just talking about steady performance. And like any rookie, the emotional highs and lows. Like when they complete a pass, it can’t be the end of the world. Let’s not make it stack two plays in a row of that. And they’ve had a lot of production, but it’s the consistency. We talked about that as a defensive unit."
"I told them a week ago, when we’re at practice and we’re making plays, they come in bunches. And then when adversity strikes, who’s going to step up to respond within the flow of a practice? I tell them, I can’t help you. Who’s going to rally the troops? They get two first downs in a row, and we got to get a stop and get off the field. And it’s the same challenge I ask of those guys.”
It would be unfair, even after just talking about the young defensive backfield, not to mention Stukes individually. He looked terrific today taking multiple reps with the first team, and he keeps producing, pushing for a starting job. He has Leonard’s attention.
“Yeah, he’s been consistent. My job is to push him outside of his comfort zone and challenge him in every way possible. Safeties are a big part of this defense, and he’s done a great job with that. I’m just not going to stop pushing him. He’s done a very good job. I think he played a lot faster last game, and I think again the instincts are self-explanatory.”
Spytek has accumulated a terrific group of young players, but he has also strategically added and retained some interesting veterans who are getting attention during this Raiders' rebuild.
The battle for the starting RG spot with Jackson Powers-Johnson changes daily. If the season started today, after this practice, I give the edge to Powers-Johnson, but Caleb Rogers is not slacking off at all. He has not taken a step back, and if not at the beginning, he will get starts before the season is over.
I asked the NFL’s best IOL and Raiders superstar Tyler Linderbaum what he likes about Rogers.
“The thing about Caleb is he's always trying to find things to improve on, things to work on. If you saw his notebook, you'd see the amount of notes that that dude takes. No, that's the kind of guys you want in the room. He plays the game the right way, has the right attitude, wants to get better, wants to work hard, and we all need to strive to be like that and have that mentality."
Tommy “Freaking” Eichenberg and Cody Lindenberg are shining as camp comes to an end. Eichenberg has added some terrific passing defensive skills (not just rushing anymore) and is playing ferociously. Perhaps no player has had a better camp than Lindenberg, and Leonard is pleased with how their camp has gone and their future.
“Yeah, the Bergs. We got the Bergs. I mean, Tommy [Eichenberg] is a killer. He takes it very seriously. He's very focused. I love Tommy for a million reasons. I could go on and on. I think Cody [Lindenberg] is one of the most improved players just in terms of movement and efficiency from where he was last year, and I think it really stood out in the spring."
"I'm really proud of Cody and all the work he's put in. It means the world to those guys. Those guys do everything they could possibly do. So, just very proud of those guys and want to see them have success as much as they want it.”
The defensive line is the biggest question mark on the defense. Yes, the defensive backfield is going to have its struggles, but they have so much talent; they are just young. The defensive line has legitimate issues. One rising player is veteran Patrick Johnson, who I project will make the roster and who is playing well.
Rob Leonard likes what he sees from his new pass-rushing weapon. “Very instinctive player, tough. Very smart. I think his play speaks for itself.”
When you turn…

title: Mark Davis, Raiders Strike Historic Agreement Ahead of 2026 Season
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are one of the most storied franchises in National Football League history. The Raiders have long been known for their impact off the field just as much as for their successful history on it. Monday morning, Mark Davis and the Raiders furthered that legacy.
While the 2026 Raiders continue their preparations on the field during Monday's practice, Davis announced that he and several others in the Raiders' ownership group will make one of the most significant decisions in franchise history.
Monday morning, Davis and others announced a $25 million donation towards the creation of Nevada's first standalone children's hospital. It is the largest philanthropic commitment the Raiders have made in franchise history, speaking volumes about the project's importance.
“The Las Vegas Raiders are making our largest philanthropic commitment in franchise history because we are dedicated to building a healthier future for kids in Nevada. We want this gift to remind children and families that they have our team backing them and that the support of the entire Raider Nation is in their corner," Davis said.
The Raiders have already built a legacy through decades of hard work by front office members, players, and everyone in between. The Raiders' $25 million gift will help change the landscape of healthcare in the state of Nevada.
Currently, child-specific healthcare is not available, and the nearest options require long-distance travel, often out of state. Raiders owners Davis, Egon Durban, and Michael Meldman each donated $5 million. The Raiders added another $10 million.
The Raiders continue to connect with the community they relocated to after decades in California. The community continues to welcome them with open arms. This move is yet another move by Davis and the Raiders to forever connect with the city of Las Vegas.
Intermountain Health's region president, Mitch Cloward, noted that "The Raiders are committed to excellence, and this gift is a generational investment that will keep families closer, strengthen our community, and give every kid every chance to thrive."
According to the Raiders, "The hospital, located at the UNLV Harry Reid Research and Technology Park, will be the first of its kind in Nevada, anchoring a new future for kids and families across the state and delivering comprehensive, high-acuity pediatric care."
"The 828,000-square-foot standalone children’s hospital will be located on a 33-acre campus and feature 180 patient beds, with room to grow. It will provide advanced emergency services designed specifically for children and a full-spectrum outpatient center alongside inpatient and specialty care."

title: Ranking Potential Breakout Wide Receivers for the Raiders
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders offense is set for a huge boost in 2026, thanks to their offseason additions as well as improved health from last season. They also have a much more offensively savvy head coach.
I don't think Klint Kubiak will turn a Raiders player into the Offensive Player of the Year as he did with the Seattle Seahawks , but he can definitely elevate the production of many of their star weapons. Which of their young wide receivers are most primed for a breakout under their new head coach?
Kirk Cousins and Jack Bech fine-tuning their connection ‼️ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7HmrW03EZO
Jack Bech was selected in the second round of the 2025 draft by the Raiders, and he wasn't overly productive in his first year in Las Vegas. However, I think he's primed for the biggest breakout among their young receivers because of what he can do in the blocking game.
Kubiak invested heavily in their offensive line this offseason because he's going to want to run the ball. Bech is a phenomenal blocker for a receiver, and if he and Kirk Cousins can continue to fine-tune their connection and he can become a reliable target on third downs, it's going to be impossible to keep him off the field.
Jalen Nailor was one of the Raiders' biggest signings this offseason. He was a consistent piece of the potent passing attack of the Minnesota Vikings, but the Silver and Black will truly be a place for him to shine. Kubiak wanted him on his team, so I expect big things out of him in 2026.
Nailor and Tre Tucker are similar archetypes of receivers, so there could be some serious target competition between the two of them. I'd give Nailor the edge because they gave him a three-year, $35 million deal in free agency, while Tucker is in the last year of his rookie contract.
That rookie connection 😮‍💨 #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/SUhXI6sTtW
Finally, I'm extremely intrigued by what Malik Benson can do in his rookie season. He was one of the fastest receivers in his draft class and looks to be developing a genuine connection with Fernando Mendoza.
Dont'e Thornton Jr. is another speedster who could provide some value for the Raiders, but he's been dealing with an injury that's kept him out of practices and both preseason games the Raiders have played. That lays down the perfect foundation for Benson to take the tops off of defenses in his rookie season and be a surprise breakout receiver for them in 2026.
