title: 3 Potential Vikings Trade Candidates 6 Days Before 53-Man Roster Deadline: Zavier Scott Among Possible Bait
full_text:
The deadline for NFL teams to trim rosters to 53 players means the regular season is right around the corner, taking place on Sunday, Aug. 30. While it's an exciting time for fans, this is a terrifying period for Vikings players who don't know if they will have a job or if they will be forced to find employment elsewhere before the regular season begins.
It is estimated that around 1,100 players from across the league will be cut by this coming Sunday's deadline at 6:00 pm ET/5 p.m. CT. For many of those players, their dreams of playing in the NFL could come to an end. Meanwhile, others will search for their next opportunity to prove themselves .
A talented player might be traded instead of being cut. Other teams around the league could be looking for the type of player who isn't a great fit for another franchise. And if a team like the Vikings can get an asset in exchange for a player they were going to let go or didn't see a future with, that is a smart move rather than losing them for nothing.
Here are three players the Vikings may be able to trade before the deadline to get rosters under the 53-man limit.
The Vikings probably wouldn't want to part ways with Zavier Scott, but it will all come down to whether Minnesota keeps three or four halfbacks on its roster for the 2026 NFL season. If the team only keeps three, it would come down to Scott or explosive rookie Demond Claiborne for the final spot after Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason.
The 27-year-old running back played in 16 games for the Vikings last season and saw 254 combined snaps between offense and special teams. A team with uncertainty in its depth and a need to improve its special teams unit might be willing to give up a late-round pick for Scott.
With one-year remaining on his contract, all of Scott's $1,005,000 cap hit would come off the books if he's traded, per Spotrac .
The Vikings selected J.J. McCarthy with the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft and hoped he could be the quarterback of the future for Minnesota. So far, he hasn't lived up to expectations, as he has been inconsistent. His grim outlook worsened with a forgettable preseason effort against the Ravens on Saturday, highlighted by missing a wide-open pass to wideout Myles Price (h/t VikingzFanPage).
JJ McCarthy misses Myles Price WIDE OPEN in the end zone. pic.twitter.com/Ix8VJrEPTe
However, McCarthy has shown flashes of brilliance with his legs and his arms. He has also struggled through injuries and abysmal offensive line play in front of him. A team could see him as a project that could be acquired rather inexpensively if the Vikings throw in the towel on developing the former Michigan standout, as he'll carry a cap hit just over $3.1 million in 2026 and 2027.
It sounds weird to say that the Vikings might be able to trade Jeshaun Jones, but he has had a solid training camp and is only 26 years old. Minnesota has a ton of talent at wide receiver heading into roster cuts and will have to part ways with at least one player who has looked great heading into the season.
Jones was a bright spot in Saturday's 13-3 loss to the Ravens, catching five of his six targets for 63 receiving yards— including a beautiful 36-yard grab off a pass from Carson Wentz right before halftime.
Carson Wentz throws it up to Jeshaun Jones who hauls in the tough 36-yard reception 👀 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GdocS8a5jq
Jones has been a fringe player since joining the team in 2024. He has bounced around the practice squad and was even given a reserve/future contract. For a player to be that close to the 53-man roster and then look good leading up to cuts , some teams likely already have their eye on him if he is let go as part of the team's final transactions to trim the roster to 53 players.

title: 3 Vikings on Thin Ice After Preseason Week 2: Michael Jurgens Is Running Out of Time
full_text:
There wasn't much to love about the Vikings' performance in their Week 2 preseason game against the Ravens. The 3-13 defeat on Saturday afternoon only shone a brighter spotlight on the problems facing the franchise heading into the 2026 NFL season.
The good news for the Vikings is that they still have time to improve. Minnesota has one more preseason game , along with several practices, to get the team up to speed and prepare them for the regular-season opener against the Packers.
Minnesota needs to identify problem areas and devise a plan to address those issues. Saturday's preseason game made it clear that three Vikings desperately need help if they want to save their jobs and should be considered on thin ice until they prove otherwise.
Minnesota used a seventh-round draft pick on Michael Jurgens in the 2024 NFL Draft, and the team hoped the former Wake Forest blocker could turn into a solid contributor. Given that he has played 18 games for the Vikings, Jurgens should look like he knows what he's doing on the field.
Instead, he struggled mightily against the Ravens on Saturday, finishing with a 46.6 overall grade on Pro Football Focus after allowing two pressures on 37 snaps.
If not for disgustingly shallow competition at center, Jurgens likely wouldn't have as much responsibility for the Vikings. He is still above Gavin Gerhardt and Delby Lemieux on Minnesota's depth chart, but that still shouldn't make him feel comfortable.
To add even more to Jurgens' situation, starter Blake Brandel has struggled mightily in practices, yet there is no credible threat to compete with him on the Vikings' roster. It wouldn't be surprising if Minnesota watches cuts around the league for a center or looks to trade for someone who could push Minnesota's offensive linemen.
If not for the focus on J.J. McCarthy these days , there would be a lot more disappointment for Max Brosmer. The Vikings signed him as a priority free-agent quarterback after the 2025 NFL Draft and had high expectations for the former University of Minnesota standout.
Brosmer has not yet demonstrated the potential the Vikings hoped he could bring to the team. He has thrown a pass in six NFL games in his career, attempting a total of 71 throws, and has yet to toss his first touchdown as a pro, but has thrown four interceptions.
Saturday's preseason game against the Ravens was a reminder of the frustration Brosmer can cause. Even though he wasn't getting much help from his offensive line, the young passer looked uncomfortable under center and couldn't execute against Baltimore's third- and fourth-string defenses, even throwing an interception near the end of the game.
Silas Walters picks off Max Brosmer for the @Ravens INT Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8WXVwIDnER
As it stands, Brosmer should be among the Vikings' roster cuts, and the team should evaluate whether to put him on the practice squad.
When the Vikings selected Caleb Banks in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft, it surprised a lot of people. Analysts were quick to call him a reach at No. 18 overall and point to concerns about a foot injury that could linger for the big defender.
Through two preseason games, Banks does not look ready for the regular season . His disappointing performances against the Giants and Ravens only amplify existing concerns. It's a small sample size and "only" the preseason, but a 33.7 overall PFF grade and a 29.7 run defense grade are valid reasons to worry.
Banks is saying all the right things and seems to know what he needs to do to improve, but until he proves he is ready for the NFL, it may be in the Vikings' best interest to plan for someone else to start in defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit.

title: Patriots' Christian Gonzalez is Frustrated With How Extension Talks Have Gone
full_text:
FOXBORO --- A deal is still not done for Christian Gonzalez. The New England Patriots cornerback remains without a lucrative contract extension , one that would make him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history.
And yet, when he's not dealing with an ankle injury, Gonzalez remains a full participant in practice. But it's clearly weighing on the 24-year-old Gonzalez as Week 1 rapidly approaches.
"It's frustrating," the cornerback said following Tuesday's training camp practice. "I'm focused on the season. I'm focused on here now and doing what I got to do, and I'm out here to compete and get better."
Frustrating. That's the first we've heard him say that all offseason. It's alright to be frustrated, especially for a player who's been as important to this team's growth as he as. Is he optimistic that a deal gets done?
"I mean, I'm focused on Week 1 at this point," Gonzalez said. "I mean, it's been all offseason, so like I said, I feel like the line of today is it is what it is. So, focused on Week 1 and doing what I gotta do."
Not much has changed on that front. The Patriots remain committed to getting a deal done , or at least they say they are. Gonzalez has said he wants to remain here . Since owner Robert Kraft publicly shared that the team wants to make him the highest-paid Patriots player of all time, that tune has yet to be deterred from.
"We want him here. He’s an elite player," Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf said . "I’ve been on record saying that before, and we’re continuing to work with his representation to find a resolution that works for everyone."
So what's holding this up? What's going on? Could this bleed into the regular season? Could you imagine that?
"I’m confident we’re continuing to work on it," Wolf said, "And we’re positive that we’re making momentum."
"I think we're continuing to work on the negotiation side of Christian, and I think that's where that stays," vice president of player personnel Ryan Cowden said when asked about the possibility of trading Gonzalez.
It doesn't seem like Gonzalez won't be suiting up in a different uniform this season, considering the team's willingness to express their want for him. Scratch that off your potential bingo sheet for this year.
But Gonzalez clearly miffed, and rightfully so. The All-Pro has been involved in these talks all offseason, saw his fellow 2023 draft pick Devon Witherspoon ink a lucrative deal and can't go one press conference without fielding a question about it.
Gonzalez wasn't out on the field for either of the joint practices between the Indianapolis Colts or the Philadelphia Eagles. He declined to get into his absence was related to that ankle injury or his contract dispute. When asked if he feels like the team has held up their end of the bargain when it comes to talking about the contract to the media, Gonzalez gave a long pause.
"I don't know," he ended up saying. He's been vocal about this, since the spring, about trying to keep most of this information private, and between the Patriots and his representatives.
"The (front) office knows how I feel," Gonzalez said. "My team has made it known what I feel I'm worth, so the right people know what I'm worth."
During Gonzalez's media availability, Kraft's helicopter landed on the helipad right next to the Patriots ' practice field. The cornerback paused to let the noise die down, but not before saying tongue in cheek that he "called him in."
There's a funny metaphor in that scene.
And on that same note, despite what might being shared publicly, these negotiations are starting to feel like they're getting choppy.

title: Eliot Wolf's Explanation Behind Patriots Trading Kayshon Boutte Makes Plenty of Sense
full_text:
FOXBORO --- It worked out almost perfectly. The New England Patriots traded away wide receiver Kayshon Boutte just one day before reporters were set to speak to de facto general manage Eliot Wolf.
Let's rewind: The Patriots shipped off Boutte, the fan favorite in the final year of his rookie contract, to the Houston Texans for young safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh round pick. On paper, not the greatest of returns for a player that scored seven total touchdowns last year between the regular season and postseason.
I'm sure there are fans upset online, partially at the return, but more so at the fact that they traded away Boutte -- Drake Maye's favorite target in the deep game -- for pennies on the dollar. The 24-year-old was the NFL's top receiver when it came to scoring on passes that traveled more than 25 yards in the air (he had four). His talent, and his growth as both a player and person, are both reasons to keep him in New England.
But let Wolf explain the reasoning behind what went into the trade, and it does have some sense caked into it.
"When a talent like A.J. Brown becomes available ... it was just an elite player that we were excited to be able to acquire. It's always about improving the roster," the Patriots executive vice president of player personnel told reporters Tuesday, confirming that sending Boutte to a potential AFC contender didn't impact the deal.
"We have guys that are good enough to be on the 53, but we're going to be looking to upgrade. It's all about improving the roster."
That point is spot on. The Patriots had a crowded wide receiver room for months , mostly because of the additions of Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown. The team went out and acquired both of those guys, who are expected to have larger roles in the passing attack than Boutte.
It's part of the reason why Boutte ended up requesting a trade back in April. He could see the writing on the wall. Add in Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams, DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism III and it was obvious that another shoe was about to drop ahead of Week 1.
This summer, Boutte looked great in practice. Solely based on reps and his pure talent, he could have easily made the 53-man roster. It just wasn't that easy for the Patriots to roll into the season with seven wide receivers.
"We feel really good about our receiver group," Wolf said. "We have guys that can play in multiple positions, they all really compliment each other really well."
And then Wolf followed that up by saying that when the Patriots brought in both Doubs and Brown, "something had to give." Clearly that was Boutte, and upgrading from last year's duo (Stefon Diggs and Boutte) with those two players is a move that makes the Patriots better, both in 2026 and the seasons following that.
When you add in the fact that the Patriots tried to draft Reed coming out of Penn State last year , it makes you feel a bit better about how the team views this deal.
"Jaylen was a guy that we identified in the draft process as somebody that we'd might pick," Wolf said, praising his abilities in Houston's playoff games last winter. "When we determined that he might be available, he was someone we wanted to acquire."
Reed's a player that can play as both a reserve in the secondary and as a potential core special teamer. If you consider the fact that the Patriots don't really have a true nickel/dime defensive back, it gives some clear path for how Reed can impact this squad . With a deep receiver room, you couldn't say the same for Boutte.
Wolf had tremendous praise for Boutte's talents and his growth since being drafted in 2023, but it was clear that the receiver wasn't going to get as big a role on the field that some might have hoped.
"This was about the Patriots and doing what's best for our organization," Wolf said.
You can't argue with that mindset.
At the end of the day, it didn't seem like Boutte was going to be in New England's long term plans. And for them to get anything (a player they liked coming out of college, plus a pick) out of what looked like a dead end is a win.

title: Resetting Patriots Secondary: Where Does Jaylen Reed Fit In?
full_text:
The dust has settled on the New England Patriots trading wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans. In return, they were able to get safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh round pick .
On paper, no bueno in terms of the return. Boutte was Drake Maye’s top deep ball target a year ago and was easily talented enough to remain on the roster as a sixth/seventh receiver (depending on how that room shook out). But the team now cleared up the drama that had surrounded Boutte for months and traded him after he reportedly requested a trade earlier in the offseason.
Now it’s time to roll with Reed, a second-year defensive back who had a minimal role with the Texans last season. A 23 year old out of Penn State, Reed was more of a backup on a Houston defense that looked poised to run the postseason table.
And yet this year, the Texans had a pretty stuffed safety room (Caleb Bullock, Reed Blankenship, Jalen Pitre, Kamari Ramsey) that allowed Reed to be expendable. It gave the Patriots the chance to add some more depth to the room in return for a player that is in the final year of his rookie contract .
Could the Patriots have gotten someone at a position of greater importance, like offensive guard or linebacker? Maybe, maybe not. But they got a depth player anyway.
“Depth – depth has to be built,” the head coach said. “That is something that has to be built through experience and making sure that the guys are in place to be the first backup in. Those are critical. Those are almost starters. We know how many people are going to have to play for you throughout the season and there cannot be a drop-off.
“So, that is why we're building it, and that is what you have preseason for. It is what you have training camp for. That is what you have practices and joint practices for is to be able to identify those players that you think are in a position to provide that. And that is what we're trying to do.”
Looking at resetting the Patriots’ secondary, the safety room now feels like it’s overflowing. At the top, you have Kevin Byard and Craig Woodson – the pairing that can easily become one of the best duos in the entire NFL.
Behind them is a tight competition for who turns into the third (or fourth) safety. Dell Pettus, Mike Brown and John Saunders Jr. have all had shining moments since the spring and are nearly neck-and-neck for a roster spot.
Undrafted free agents Eric Butler and Peter Manuma follow them, and special teams captain Brenden Schooler remains sidelined on the non-football injury list.
So when you add Reed into that equation, it feels like it’s putting more pressure on that trio of Pettus, Brown and Saunders. You wouldn’t have traded for Reed if he wasn’t going to stick around, and his abilities as a tackler and run defender could easily work into a nickel/dime role on this defense.
This trade, while headlined as a receiver move, could have some ramifications to how the safety group ends up. Brown ended the spring as the clear-cut favorite to win the third job, but he’s started to fade since training camp began. Pettus has come into his own on both defense and special teams, while Saunders leads the Patriots with five interceptions this summer.
If I had to stamp my claim on it ahead of the team’s final preseason game this week, I’d go with Byard, Woodson, Reed, Pettus and Saunders making the roster, while Schooler opens up the season on the Reserve/NFI list.
Something has to give, and it’s not going to be Reed.

title: What You Need to Know About Newly-Acquired Patriots Safety Jaylen Reed
full_text:
The biggest news of the day for the New England Patriots was that they traded away fan-favorite wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans .
The fourth-year receiver, who reportedly requested a trade earlier in the offseason after the team went out and added Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown , is heading into a contract season this fall.
In return, the Patriots didn't get the greatest of returns. They were able to get safety Jaylen Reed, a second-year player out of Penn State, and a 2028 seventh round draft pick. Ultimately? Not the best they could have done for a receiver that helped elevate New England's deep game a year ago.
But maybe this was just what Boutte's market was after a year where he recorded 551 yards and a career-high six touchdowns.
At the end of the day, this move helps clear up a muddy wide receiver picture for the Patriots, gives Boutte a chance to earn more snaps and helps New England add some depth in the secondary.
Here's what you need to know about Reed, the player who'll now be tasked with becoming a solid rotational player in this Patriots defense.
The 23-year-old Reed played in seven regular season games and two postseason games for the Texans as a rookie last year, racking up 19 total tackles and a fumble recovery. 12 of those tackles game in a single game against the Buffalo Bills on Thursday Night Football.
Reed was an All-Big Ten Honorable Mention in his junior season (2023) at Penn State, and would then record 98 tackles one season later. While he put up solid numbers for Nittany Lions, he fell into the sixth round (187th overall).
When he did get a chance to play last year, he spent a lot of time in the slot or in the box. He's versatile in different defensive schemes and can run quick from his normal safety position. He was poised for a larger role in a Houston defense with Super Bowl aspirations.
"Going into year two, after having a year under my belt, definitely helped," Reed told Texans.com earlier in the offseason . "The coaches I have and the staff, they're helping me develop into a young man that's going to take on bigger roles this season. I'm excited for it. I'm prepared for it. I'm up for the challenge."
Right now, it feels like Reed could become a nickel/dime player in this Patriots defense. If you take a look at the *expected* defensive backs to earn a roster spot, it looks like Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis, Marcus Jones, Charles Woods, Kevin Byard, Craig Woodson and then a few names out of Kindle Vildor, Karon Prunty, John Saunders Jr, Dell Pettus and Mike Brown.
Bringing in Reed feels like he's guaranteed a spot in that secondary, potentially making things difficult for players playing deep into the preseason games ( Saunders and Brown come to mind). Reed played just 73 defensive snaps last year and might not be an every down player for New England, but there is clearly a skillset that he can bring to the roster.
He's a competitive player, especially when it comes to playing the run. For the Patriots who struggled against the run late last year, that's always a plus. He won't be asked to line up 1-on-1 against some wide receivers, but has looked solid when tasked to do so in stints.
Reed ended his college career with five interceptions, something the Patriots secondary continues to stress this summer as a key point of emphasis. If Reed can start to make some plays in the slot on third downs and start to take the ball away, the Patriots will be more than pleased with those results.
At face value, the Patriots didn't come away winning this trade in my judgement. They got rid of a player with an established rapport with Drake Maye in the passing game for not that much bang for your buck.
Reed is a fine player, and one that brings a sound tackling technique and athleticism to the field. But safety wasn't the biggest need on the defensive side of the ball for the Patriots to address.
This past week, both Chad Muma and Khalil Jacobs went down in the preseason win against the Philadelphia Eagles. Those two linebackers have left a pretty sizeable hole in the middle of the defense behind the starting duo of Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss.
If I was focused on upgrading one position of need via trade, it likely would have been linebacker.
At the end of the day, this move gives some serious clarity to the Patriots' wide receiver corps and will allow them to focus in on the current players in that room (Brown, Doubs, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III).
Reporters will get to speak with Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf Tuesday afternoon, and will be able to get a better assessment into what led to this trade. Stay tuned.

title: Patriots Roster Moves: What Releasing WR Kobe Prentice, CB Kenneth Harris Means Going Forward
full_text:
Heading into their final week of preseason games, the New England Patriots have made several moves to their roster.
The team announced that they've released rookies wide receiver Kobe Prentice and cornerback Kenneth Harris. Both of these moves were to open up roster spots for offensive guard Jack Conley -- first reported by Patriots On SI -- and punter Matt Haack.
Both Prentice and Harris weren't spotted at the team's training camp practice Monday morning.
Prentice, 22, spent this summer with the Patriots after originally signing with the Carolina Panthers. He was claimed off of waivers before training camp and played in both of the Patriots' preseason games as a reserve.
He caught four passes for 47 yards in the Patriots' games against the Indianapolis Colts and Philadelphia Eagles. Prentice didn't factor into the team's future plans as an undrafted free agent, especially when others at his position (Nick DeGennaro, Cameron Dorner) burst onto the scene a lot quicker.
Harris, 24, signed with the Patriots out of Oklahoma State folllowing the NFL Draft. He didn't record any stats against the Eagles, but did have two total tackles in his NFL debut against the Colts.
Both of these positions are pretty dense, making it a tough spot for any young, undrafted player to crack through. Prentice got a few chances during the summer in the return game, but ultimately was caught up in a numbers game that was a stacked receiving room.
His speed helped put him on the map, but he wasn't really able to differentiate himself on a roster that felt like the cards were heavily stacked against him from the start.
Prentice was the second Patriots receiver to depart the team Monday. It was reported earlier that the team is trading Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a future seventh round draft choice .
As for Harris, he was stuck at the bottom of another deep room. If it wasn't Christian Gonzalez, Marcus Jones, Carlton Davis or Kindle Vildor on the field, it was other defensive backs (Karon Prunty, Charles Woods, Channing Canada, Marcellas Dial, Kobee Minor, Brandon Crossley) who got larger opportunities in both the practice and game settings.
The Patriots did suffer injuries to both their offensive line and punter positions in their 24-21 win over the Eagles this weekend, leading to the signings of Conley and Haack.
Conley, who spent time last year on the Patriots practice squad as a rookie, comes in to help shore up a line that's lost Ben Brown, Andrew Rupcich and Marcus Bryant to injury. Haack, a longtime NFL veteran, is now in the fold after regular punter Bryce Baringer wasn't able to complete Saturday's game with an undisclosed injury.
Both Conley and Haack were present at Monday's practice, sporting No. 67 and No 19, respectively.

title: Patriots Trade WR Kayshon Boutte to Texans for Young DB, Future Draft Pick
full_text:
After plenty of offseason rumors about if this move would eventually happen or not, the New England Patriots are going to trade away wide receiver Kayshon Bou tte after three seasons.
According to Tom Pelissero, the Patriots have agreed to trade Boutte to the Houston Texans for second-year safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh round draft pick. Boutte, set to enter a contract season in New England, was coming off his best season as a pro.
The Patriots went out and brought in A.J. Brown (trade) and Romeo Doubs (free agency) this past offseason, part of the reason why Boutte's departure felt like it was imminent .
Boutte, 24, was drafted by the Patriots in the sixth round (187th overall) back in 2023, and has been a part of three different head coaching regimes in New England.
As a rookie under Bill Belichick, he struggled to find the field, catching just two passes in what was essentially a redshirt season.
One year later, under Jerod Mayo, the former LSU star broke out of his shell. He caught 43 passes for 589 yards and three touchdowns. His first career touchdown catch -- a 40-yard grab over Houston Texans star cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. -- was also the first passing touchdown of Drake Maye's career.
There were signs that Boutte, who once had the possibility of going in the first round out of college, was meshing with Maye in the deep game. In 2025, that became true. He had 33 receptions and 551 receiving yards, and set a career high with six touchdowns.
In the postseason, Boutte was very hot and cold. He beat Stingley Jr. (again) for an impressive one-handed touchdown in the Patriots' 28-16 win against the Texans in the AFC Divisional Round. Three weeks later, he caught just one pass in the team's loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Super Bowl LX.
Boutte now joins a Texans receiving corps that already has Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel. After finishing second in the AFC South, Houston wanted to add to their depth at the position. Bringing in Boutte, who can threaten any team down the sideline, is a worthwhile move -- especially at the price tag that they gave up.
For the Patriots, it was an offseason filled with question marks surrounding Boutte . As he entered a contract season, Boutte did not report to the team's voluntary offseason workouts. There had been reporting that Boutte would have welcomed a trade out of New England because he felt like his role had been reduced.
Vrabel had been asked if he gotten a sense that his absence was about wanting a trade.
"Kayshon has communicated, and which I which I texted him and told him that I respected him for doing so," Vrabel said during OTAs. "There's different reasons why guys aren't here or will miss a day or - that's their prerogative. It's voluntary. We have a few days that are mandatory. We just want to make it a product that they feel like is worthwhile being here. That's important."
Once mandatory minicamp rolled around and players were required to show, Boutte was present, even working in with the top offense. On the final day of the three-day session, he did not participate, making some eyebrows raise about what that could have meant.
Before the first day of minincamp, Vrabel talked about the process to reacclimate players who were absent at OTAs (Boutte, cornerback Christian Gonzalez, edge rusher Harold Landry) and what their usage rates may look like.
"I do not know if he will participate fully, just because I do not think that is fair to him to just say, 'Hey, go run 20 reps,'" Vrabel commented. "Again, I think that part of this is about evaluating where guys are, getting them reacclimated to what the new stuff is that we are putting in in the red zone.
After spending part of the offseason in Florida working out, Boutte made headlines as he hosted pickup basketball games in Franklin, Mass. for any Patriots fans that wanted to show out. At one of these games, he mentioned how he wanted to remain in a Patriots uniform for good.
"I want to be in New England for the rest of my career," Boutte said to WBZ’s Dan Roche . "I’ve enjoyed it out here. Been here three years. Every day I’m here. I call this home. This is my new home. Grew up in Louisiana, stayed there 20 years, but now Boston is my life."
The Patriots leaned on Boutte a lot last year , especially when they wanted to air the ball out. Early in the season, in games against the New Orleans Saints and Tennessee Titans, Maye connected with Boutte for a few long touchdown passes. Boutte became a really valuable part of the offense after two years of off-and-on production.
But because the team sent away a 2028 first round pick and a 2027 fifth round pick to the Philadephia Eagles to acquire Brown, the writing felt like it was on the wall for Boutte. With the Eagles, Brown worked inside and outside of the formation, and is the real-deal "X" wideout for this offense.
Even though Boutte shined as the Patriots' "X" last season, there really isn't much he brings to the table that differs from Brown's skillset. He was open and honest about wanting a chance to compete this spring/summer, telling reporters at minicamp that he welcomed whatever opportunity the team gave him in the offense . But the Patriots decided to move on from Boutte with one year left on his rookie deal.
Stefon Diggs was New England's top wideout last year, and now those snaps are going to get gobbled up by both Brown and Doubs. When you add in Hollins and the growth potential for Williams as a downfield threat, it felt harder and harder for Boutte to get the snaps he would have deserved in a contract season.
So the Patriots add some extra depth at a position with plenty of players already shining. Reed, in his second season after getting drafted by Houston in the sixth round (187th overall), joins a safety room that already has Kevin Byard, Craig Woodson, Mike Brown, Dell Pettus, Eric Butler, John Saunders Jr. and Peter Manuma.
Coming out of Penn State, Reed was a solid tackler for the Nittany Lions. He had 46 tackles and two picks in his junior season. He was a starter the next year before declaring for the 2025 NFL Draft.
Last year, Reed played in seven games as a rookie and recorded 14 tackles and a fumble recovery. The 23-year-old started one game for Houston, who's defense was among the best in the entire NFL.
It felt like Houston would be a plausible landing spot for Boutte via trade after their wide receiver, Jayden Higgins, went down with a season-ending ACL tear. Considering the Patriots' connection with Texans general manager Nick Caserio and their now-need at the wideout position, it felt like Boutte was destined to land in Houston.
Ultimately, for a player who reportedly requested a trade earlier in the offseason, the Patriots were able to grab a future draft pick and a depth player in their secondary ... marking this deal as a productive one for both sides. With seven receivers set to possibly make the Patriots roster, the current group now feels more set in stone.

title: The Good and Not So Good From Patriots Practice: TreVeyon Henderson Leaves Early
full_text:
FOXBORO --- In the N ew England Patriots ' first practice since their 24-21 preseason win over the Philadelphia Eagles, they got some developments on both side of the spectrum. Both Christian Gonzalez and TreVeyon Henderson made headlines with injury updates.
The Patriots were able to get Gonzalez back onto the field for the first time in two weeks , while Henderson left to go inside the team's facility halfway through the session. Here's why those were important, and what it could mean for the Patriots going forward:
The Patriots' best defensive player was back out on the field for the first time since Aug. 10. Gonzalez, who dealt with a minor ankle injury this month and missed out on both joint practices, was a full participant today and worked with the top defense. He got a PBU against A.J. Brown in 1-on-1s and beat DeMario Douglas in 2-on-2s.
"I think we’re hopeful that he will be able to do some stuff," head coach Mike Vrabel said before the practice. "He was working before the game and trying to work through the return to play, so we’ll see how he feels this morning."
While Gonzalez remains in the middle of potential contract extension negotiations , the Patriots secondary has drastically missed their best player. They're happy that he's healthy and ready to return.
"The most important thing is health and everything," fellow cornerback Marcus Jones said after practice, where he didn't know that Gonzalez would participate until the session began. "So, happy that he’s feeling better and everything, and happy to have him back too."
But even with Gonzalez returning to the field with his teammates , his head coach didn't want to address any concerns he may have for Gonzalez's availability when the regular season opens up on Sept. 9.
"I’m going to focus on today. I’m not ready to talk about Week 1," Vrabel said. "I hope that we have to do everything we can to get the guys ready. Each guy has to be ready individually, and then I have to find a way to make sure that the football team is ready and that we’re conditioned and ready to go."
This was the first time since the spring that the Patriots practiced on the lower field next to their brand-new facility. It was evident that something was up, as a slick playing surface led to several players falling down during practice.
"Everybody was slipping," running back Rhamondre Stevenson said. "It's just something we gotta get used to. If that's the field conditions, we have to get used to it."
While some players, like newly-signed offensive guard Jack Conley, were able to get back up and continue practicing, Henderson wasn't able to. The second-year running back slipped while trying to make a cut and then met with several members of the training staff as they looked at his right foot/ankle.
After a few minutes sitting on a trainer's table, Henderson would eventually depart inside the New Balance Athletics Center. Losing another running back to injury at this point in the summer could turn into a bigger story, as the Patriots didn't have Lan Larison and Jam Miller active in practice Monday.

title: Preseason Injury to Bryce Baringer Forces Patriots to Sign Matt Haack
full_text:
FOXBORO --- The New England Patriots have signed free agent punter Matt Haack, after incumbent starter Bryce Baringer suffered an injury in the team's preseason matchup on Saturday against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Baringer started against the Eagles, punting twice for 91 yards. He was then replaced by third-string quarterback Behren Morton for the remainder of the game.
"Bryce wasn't feeling great after the first two punts," head coach Mike Vrabel said Saturday after New England's win over Philadelphia. "So, I figured instead of risking anything there with Bryce or with Andy (Borregales), that Behren was able to get us out of there."
Vrabel kept it clear on Monday when asked the severity of Baringer's injury.
"Serious enough that we'll probably have to sign a new punter," he said. "It was something that occurred during the game, which is why the quarterback had to punt."
Baringer, heading into a contract year, had been New England's only rostered punter throughout training camp. While the team had brought in tryout players during rookie minicamp and mandatory minicamp, the Patriots opted to roll solely with Baringer in camp.
Last Thursday against the Indianapolis Colts, the 27-year-old had six punts for 309 yards (51.5 yard average).
New England also loses a key part of the field goal operation, with Baringer working as the team's holder. Kicker Andy Borregales made all four of his kicks on Saturday (one field goal, three extra-points) working with the full unit. The week prior, with long snapper Julian Ashby injured, Borregales missed three of his six total kicks.
With the severity of Baringer's injury currently unknown, there is a chance Haack only sticks around for the remainder of the preseason. However, if Baringer's injury lingers into the regular season, having a backup punter on Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks and dynamic return man Rashid Shaheed could get messy.
The Patriots will be Haack's 10th NFL team he has spent time with, including multiple stints with the Buffalo Bills and Arizona Cardinals. The 32-year-old was most recently with the Washington Commanders, spending training camp with them before being waived last Tuesday.
He was present in Monday's practice, wearing No. 19.
Haack appeared in seven games last season with the Arizona Cardinals, where he averaged a boom 51.3 yards per punt, good for third-most in the NFL.
Now in New England, Haack could be a pivotal part of the Patriots' special teams unit early in the regular season if Baringer is unable to play.

title: Source: Patriots Add Offensive Line Depth, Reunite With Jack Conley
full_text:
FOXBORO --- The New England Patriots have lost three offensive linemen in their last two preseason games , and have now made a move to help bolster the trenches.
According to a source, the Patriots have agreed to a contract with free agent guard Jack Conley. The former Boston College Eagle was originally signed to the Patriots as an undrafted free agent last summer.
Conley, 25, spent six years at BC, playing in 60 games and was named an All-ACC Honorable Mention for starting 12 games in his final graduate season. He inked his deal with the Patriots for training camp before getting released during roster cutdowns. During the preseason, he played 76 total snaps.
The Patriots have signed OG Jack Conley, per source. He spent two separate stints with the team last year as a rookie.
He would later re-sign with the team's practice squad for a brief, 20-day stint in early September. He would be cut at the end of the month.
His rookie year ended with stints on the Detroit Lions and Cleveland Browns, where he remained on their practice squad for the rest of the season. Conley was released earlier this month by Cleveland after inking a futures deal to close 2025.
His size (6-foot-7, 333 pounds) helps add some much-needed depth to an offensive line depleted by injurie s. The Patriots lost backups Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich to injuries in their first preseason game against the Indianapolis Colts, and then lost backup offensive tackle Marcus Bryant this weekend against the Eagles.
"I do not think we have a very deep team," head coach Mike Vrabel said over the weekend about playing starters during the preseason, "so I think we have to make sure that we are preparing our football team and that we are doing everything that we can to keep our best players available."
During his college career, Conley spent time at right guard, left guard and right tackle. He also got reps as an eligible tight end, and could certainly play a large role in the team's final preseason game against the Browns this week.
Conley joins an interior offensive line room that already has Mike Onwenu, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Greg Van Roten, James Hudson, Mehki Butler, Jacob Rizy, Darrian Dalcourt, Joe Michalski and JonDarius Morgan. They'll need to make a corresponding move to make room for Conley.

title: Patriots Found Ideal Backup QB in Behren Morton
full_text:
FOXBORO --- There isn't a quarterback competition by any stretch of the imagination for the New England Patriots.
We know that Drake Maye has the starting job locked up for the longterm future and Tommy DeVito has played his way into the QB2 job. But Behren Morton, the seventh-string rookie who's gotten limited snaps in practice , has done more than enough to stick around this year.
With the NFL allowing teams to roster an emergency third quarterback, it gives the Patriots some roster flexibility when it comes to keeping Morton on the roster. In other years, the team might be compelled to part ways with Morton, considering his path to the starting lineup is virtually impossible.
Now that quarterbacks like Morton can be in uniform, it could give him a spot on the 53-man roster. And now that he also showed his prowess as a backup punter in Saturday's preseason win over the Philadelphia Eagles, he could become a real backup swiss army knife.
Morton looked good in the 24-21 win, throwing for 129 yards and the game-winning touchdown to undrafted wideout Nick DeGennaro. The final drive showed off Morton's accuracy, as he hit six passes to lead the Patriots to their first win of the 2026 season.
"I think playing quarterback, especially playing in the NFL, you dream of this moment, of leading your team down to have a game-winning drive," Morton said postgame. "It goes back to all the hard work that we've put in through the spring when we got here, summer, and then obviously training camp. To go out there and do it, being well-prepared from coach (Josh) McDaniels, for the offense, that was big for us tonight."
At Texas Tech, Morton was a great quarterback when it came to moving in and out of the pocket to extend plays. He's been able to show that during his extended preseason reps, and while he might not be able to show off those skills in the regular season, he already has the look of a McDaniels quarterback prototype.
He's also got the coach speak drilled into him, knowing there's plenty to correct from Saturday.
"There's a lot to correct from today that we can get a lot better from," he said. "So maybe we don't put ourselves in a situation where we need a game-winning drive, and we don't have to be in that position."
If the Patriots decide to keep Morton as their emergency third quarterback, if anything happened to regular punter Bryce Baringer, he wouldn't be allowed to punt in a game. That could lead to some funky gametime decisions from the coaching staff, should Baringer ever go down.
But for now, the Patriots seem perfectly set with the trio of quarterbacks they have right now. If Morton can go into each week and play Sam Darnold, Trevor Lawrence or any of the other quarterbacks on New England's roster, that draft pick can already be written off as a win .

title: Saints Stock Watch: 5 Players Trending Up Before Final Roster Cuts
full_text:
Just as we did last week, we will go through the New Orleans Saints players whose stocks have risen throughout training camp .
There are new players to add to the list, so there is no need to discuss those we listed last week because they have remained in good standing for the most part.
We have a veteran player who may have finally shown what he can do when healthy, two offensive linemen, a journeyman wide receiver and a fast-rising linebacker who highlights the depth of that position group.
Here are five players trending in the right direction.
While Kendre Miller missed a solid portion of training camp with a back injury, he returned last week and has been one of the sharpest in the running back room. Although he only had six carries for 22 yards in the preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams , he showed great burst and a nice catch-and-run off a screen play that went 12 yards for a first down before it was called back due to a penalty.
When Miller is healthy, he is one of the most talented weapons on the offense. However, the key words are “when healthy.”
We expect him to make the final 53-man roster.
The two highest-rated offensive players are offensive linemen Easton Kilty and Asim Richards .
Kilty has a grade of 87.3 according to Pro Football Focus (PFF) , the highest on the offense. He also has a 91.3 run block grade, which is the highest among the offensive line. He became a starter on the second team offense last week against the Rams, picking up an offense grade of 80.2 and a run block grade of 86.2 .
Richards has an 82.3 offensive grade and an 83.5 run block grade but has a slightly lower pass block grade of 77.2 .
While it is unknown how they will perform during the regular season, it is a good sign they are playing well now.
A former undrafted free agent out of Fresno State, Jalen Cropper is entering his fourth year in the league but has bounced from team to team and is just coming off a stint with the Houston Gamblers of the UFL.
However, he has moved up the depth chart thanks to the plethora of injuries affecting the receiving corps, and he has done well enough throughout the preseason to stay there. Through two games, he has five catches for 97 yards, an average of 19.4 per reception.
According to PFF , he has the third-highest offensive grade on the Saints behind Kilty and Richards with an 80.1 and a 79.2 receiving grade.
Of his five catches, four occurred 10 or more yards downfield, three resulted in first downs and two were contested catches.
Jaylan Ford was one of the players whose stock rose last week; now his partner-in-crime Isaiah Stalbird is on the rise as well.
The South Dakota State product has 11 tackles so far and is the highest-rated defensive player with at least 30 snaps, earning an 85.2 overall defense grade. He has also been an effective run stopper with an 86.4 grade.

title: Saints vs. Cowboys: 3 Things to Know Before Friday’s Preseason Finale
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will travel to the Dallas-Fort Worth area to take on America’s Team , the Dallas Cowboys .
The Cowboys have been 2-0 so far throughout the postseason and have looked good doing it, winning both of their games by two or more scores. In their last game, Dallas defeated the Arizona Cardinals 34-13 in Glendale last week.
One would expect the Cowboys to play some of their starters, but their backups have done mighty fine, especially Joe Milton who has thrown for 286 yards and three touchdowns over the last two games.
Regardless, we think playing against the Cowboys as the ramp-up game before the season is good because it allows everyone to see where they stand against one another and their chances of making the team.
While it’s not certain we will get to see the starters, it’s a possibility given that neither the Cowboys or the Saints have played them yet.
If they do, it’s another good measuring stick for the Saints, especially on defense given that the Cowboys had the No. 1 offense in the league last season. A chance to see Dak Prescott trying to throw it to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens against the Saints’ defense would be interesting to see.
Also, the Cowboys have one of the best running backs in the league with Javonte Williams .
Saints fans will have the chance to get a good look at safety Caleb Downs , someone who many draft analysts considered a generational safety prospect coming into the draft.
Playing at both Alabama and Ohio State, he helped lead both teams to the playoff and was on a playoff team in all three seasons. While he was with the Buckeyes, he was a two-time All-American and the Big 10 Defensive Player of the Year and helped guide Ohio State to the national championship in 2024.
Undrafted free agent Camden Brown has been a revelation throughout the preseason . He has had five catches for 139 yards (27.8 yards per catch) and two touchdowns
While in college, Brown had a hard time trying to get on the field at Auburn but he became a standout receiver at Georgia Southern in his senior season, catching 65 passes for 1,079 yards and led the Sun Belt in touchdown catches with 14. For his efforts, he was named First Team All-Sun Belt.

title: Saints Training Camp Notebook: New Kicker, New RB and More Injuries
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints opened the last week of the preseason slate coming off a 34-0 shutout loss to the Los Angeles Rams with practice at their Metairie facility this afternoon.
It will also be the last week for the Saints to cut the 91-man roster to 53 players, with the leaguewide deadline going into effect Sunday at 5 p.m. CT. It is a critical week not only for the organization but also its players as they seek to prove they belong on the full roster.
The Saints participated in a light practice two days after a game to start the new week.
Here is a notebook of observations from throughout the day.
Other than that, everything else remains the same.
Spencer Rattler and Zach Wilson both shared responsibilities with the combined second and third team, similar to last week.
At running back, Kendre Miller was the first running back to go after Travis Etienne in the rotation. Audric Estime returned to the practice field and he followed Miller.
The big news to start off the day was free agent kicker Daniel Carlson signing with New Orleans .
Moore mentioned that he brought him because he was a veteran kicker who had a lot of success.
“Daniel's really a talented kicker," he shared. "He's had a lot of success in this league, and I feel like there's worthy opportunities there for a competition to get him involved here. We'll kick here in, two days on Wednesday."
Tanner Brown and Charlie Smyth have been battling it out for the starting job, but both have been inconsistent throughout training camp and both have missed at lest one field goal in two preseason games.
With all of the injuries in the running back room, the Saints made the movie to trade veteran linebacker Deion Jones to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for running back Zamir White on Sunday night.
White, who spent the previous four seasons with the Las Vegas Raider s , will be a key depth piece while New Orleans navigates Alvin Kamara ’s knee injury that will cause him to miss the start of the regular season.
“Yeah, I think he's done a nice job in this league,” Moore said about White. "Going back to college as well, and just watching his preseason, I think this will be a smooth transition. This is really hard for a guy like him to hop in here, mid-week, and trying to give yourself as much of an opportunity from Friday.  I feel like the transition will be pretty smooth as far as what he was being asked to do in the last few weeks."

title: Saints Add Daniel Carlson After Kicking Competition Fails to Produce Clear Winner
full_text:
Per Mike Garofalo and Ian Rapaport of the NFL Network, the New Orleans Saints are going to sign veteran kicker Daniel Carlson to their roster on Monday.
The Saints decided to add a wrinkle into the kicking battle between challenger Tanner Brown and the incumbent Charlie Smyth . It’s a good move for New Orleans as one of the biggest holes on the team right now is the kicker position.
Carlson spent the last eight seasons with the Raiders. He was 224-of-255 on field goals and 238-of-249 on extra points during his time with the Raiders.
Carlson earned second-team All-Pro honors in 2021 and was named a first-team All-Pro in 2022. That 2022 season was the best of his career, when he converted 34 of 37 field-goal attempts and connected on 11 field goals from at least 50 yards.
The 31-year-old Carlson brings considerably more experience to New Orleans. He has been a mainstay in the league since 2018 after initially being drafted by the Minnesota Vikings before being released by the club after two games and then signing with the Oakland/Las Vegas Raiders where he stayed until the end of last season.
Carlson's numbers dipped last season, making 22 of 27 field-goal attempts at an 81.5% rate. He was 5-of-8 from 50 yards or farther and made 21 of his 22 extra-point attempts.
The primary reason New Orleans brass signed the veteran kicker was the faltering competition between the team's current options, which has failed to produce a reliable starter.
Smyth, the incumbent who replaced a struggling Blake Grupe after Week 11 last season, converted 12 of 16 field-goal attempts, including a 57-yarder. However, he has struggled throughout training camp as he has made just under 80% of his field goal attempts throughout camp.
In the preseason opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, he made both extra-point attempts but missed a 52-yard field goal late in the third quarter. Had he made the kick, the Saints would have held a two-possession lead, potentially changing the game's closing dynamics.
Smyth did not attempt a kick in last week's preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams .
Brown had shown more promise during camp, particularly with long-range accuracy. He converted attempts from 49 and 29 yards against the Jaguars on Aug. 15, but missed a 39-yarder last week. Including practice sessions, that marked his fourth missed field goal from inside 40 yards during the preseason.
This mounting lack of confidence in the current roster led the Saints to turn to Carlson, hoping the veteran can stabilize the position before the regular season begins.

title: Saints Make Clever Trade to Address Their Suddenly Depleted Backfield
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints traded veteran linebacker Deion Jones to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for running back Zamir White, as reported by ESPN's Adam Schefter on Sunday night.
The swap comes just weeks after New Orleans signed Jones to a one-year deal. The New Orleans native spent the previous season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , recording 29 tackles in 17 games.
Jones, 31, spent the first six seasons of his career with the Atlanta Falcons after being selected in the second round of the 2016 NFL draft. He has also played for the Cleveland Browns , Carolina Panthers and Buccaneers.
However, Jones was a long shot to make the team as the Saints have considerable depth at linebacker and he joined the franchise too late to make a push for the final 53-man roster.
Trade: the Saints are sending veteran LB Deion Jones to San Francisco in exchange for RB Zamir White, per sources. pic.twitter.com/VvIDfI38YH
White has experience as he enters his fifth year in the NFL. A fourth-round draft pick, he spent his first four years with the Las Vegas Raiders before joining the 49ers during the offseason.
His best season came in 2022 when he had 104 carries for 451 yards and a touchdown as the No. 2 tailback behind Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs .
White, who signed with the 49ers in early August, had faced long odds to make the team after running backs Christian McCaffrey , Kaelon Black and Jordan James returned from injury in the past week.
While it is unclear if he will make the final 53-man roster at this time, the running back room is depleted due to injuries, and White will fill a short-term need for the Saints.
Veteran Alvin Kamara sustained an MCL injury last week that is expected to keep him sidelined for multiple weeks , likely ruling him out for the first two games of the regular season.
Meanwhile, Audric Estime suffered an ankle injury during New Orleans' preseason opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars and was unable to travel to California for Saturday's matchup with the Los Angeles Rams . Additionally, Devin Neal reinjured his lingering hamstring against the Rams on Saturday, forcing an early exit shortly after returning to action.
The Saints recently got back running back Kendre Miller (back) and offseason acquisition Travis Etienne Jr. , Ty Chandler and CJ Donaldson are all healthy.

title: 3 Things Saints Learned the Hard Way in Ugly 34-0 Loss to Rams
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints fell to 0-2 in the preseason after a 34-0 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, tied for the fourth-worst exhibition loss in franchise history.
Virtually nothing went right, leaving a string of bad and downright ugly moments. From poor discipline and struggling quarterback play to missed opportunities in the red zone, it was simply bad football—and about as low as it gets.
Saints head coach Kellen Moore did not make any excuses after the game.
"Regular season, preseason, does not matter. Those are not the ones you want," Moore said.
Here are our three biggest takeaways.
Just when you thought it would be wrapped up this week, it wasn’t.
After a strong performance against Jacksonville, Zach Wilson seemed poised to secure the role if he could sustain that momentum on Saturday against Los Angeles. However, he fell short. Wilson struggled in his start, completing only 6 of 12 passes for 55 yards, an interception, and a modest 50% completion rate.
Spencer Rattler recorded higher stat totals than Wilson, finishing 14-of-23 for 141 yards. Even so, his turnover proved costlier when Rams safety Alex Cook intercepted a pass and returned it 100 yards for a touchdown.
Neither Wilson nor Rattler has yet demonstrated the consistency needed to solidify the primary backup spot.
"Obviously, we're going to have to watch the film really closely because, you know, your gut reaction is obviously that we want to accomplish more as an offense," Moore said when asked about the two quarterbacks. "We had the unfortunate interception in the first half. We had one in the red zone in the second half where we're driving, and so, yeah, we're just going to have to watch this film and get better. I thought those guys had some really good work throughout this entire week, and obviously, as a team collectively, we didn't take advantage of this opportunity today."
Red zone struggles re-emerged as a major concern for the Saints, who failed to score on three separate opportunities.
On the second-half opening drive, New Orleans reached the Rams' 6-yard line, but Alex Cook intercepted Spencer Rattler's pass to Treyton Welch and returned it 100 yards for a touchdown.
Later in the third quarter, the Saints advanced inside the Rams' 10-yard line, but Ty Chandler fumbled after a 3-yard run, with Los Angeles recovering at their own 3-yard line.
New Orleans had one final chance, but Tanner Brown missed a 39-yard field goal attempt with 37 seconds remaining.
Drawing twelve penalties for 96 yards is a terrible look. The Saints seemed to draw flags for almost everything imaginable, at one point accumulating more penalty yardage than rushing yards.
The disciplinary issues surfaced immediately: within the game's opening 10 plays, New Orleans was flagged for unnecessary roughness, holding, and offensive pass interference. Getting called for a false start in front of a quiet preseason crowd at SoFi Stadium was bad enough.
"Just a lack—lack of discipline, lack of detail," Moore said in regard to the Saints being flagged so much throughout the game. "A lot of them are under our control. You know, 12 penalties in a football game is—you're not going to win football games. And I feel like we've talked a lot about that, and it was obviously a step back from the progress that we felt like we've made. So it's going to be a lesson."
While this initial road trip took place before a sparse crowd, the environment will shift dramatically in a couple of weeks when they face hostile, packed houses in Detroit and Baltimore to open the regular season.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly: Saints Deliver a Preseason Performance They’ll Want to Forget Immediately
full_text:
Few expected such a dismal performance from the New Orleans Saints .
The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Saints 34-0 in a game that tied for the fourth-worst exhibition loss in franchise history . Since leading 20-6 at halftime against the Jacksonville Jaguars last week, the Saints have been outscored 52-0.
The performance in Southern California offered little to like and much to improve upon.
Bright spots were scarce, but tight end Moliki Matavao and running back Kendre Miller offered positive performances.
Matavao, who flashed potential during training camp, hauled in a first-down catch through tight coverage against the Cowboys. While he struggled as a blocker and failed to record significant plays in the preseason opener against the Jaguars, his pass-catching ability on Saturday validated the preseason optimism surrounding him. A closer review of the film will provide more clarity on his blocking progression. He limped off the field in the 2nd quarter with a knee injury that is still to be determined.
What a sideline grab by Moliki Matavao! #Saints | 📺: FOX-8 pic.twitter.com/cv5aa1WQJI
Miller demonstrated his capabilities during his limited snaps. He logged two strong runs and an early long-gain reception, though the latter was negated by a penalty. Assuming he maintains health, Miller remains a viable depth option behind T ravis Etienne until Alvin Kamara returns. Devin Neal ’s pre-game injury further bolsters Miller's roster outlook.
The competition remains far from over.
Following a dominant showing against Jacksonville, Zach Wilson appeared to have the inside track if he could maintain that momentum against Los Angeles on Saturday. That was not the case.
Wilson struggled in his start, finishing with a meager 50% completion rate by connecting on just six of 12 attempts for 55 yards and a pick.
Spencer Rattler posted better numbers than Wilson, going 14-of-23 for 141 yards. However, his interception was even more damaging, as Rams safety Alex Cook snagged the pass and returned it 100 yards for a score.
Does anyone want to win the Saints backup QB job? Spencer Rattler throws into triple coverage, 100-yard pick-six. pic.twitter.com/O8Ae2kRmBg
It might be a tired narrative, but an injury to Tyler Shough would leave New Orleans in a precarious position. The team experienced a similar slide last season, starting 1-7 before Shough replaced Rattler. The rookie eventually guided the Saints to a 4-5 finish over the final stretch.
As of now, neither Wilson nor Rattler has proven capable of providing the stability required from a primary backup.
One of the biggest concerns for the Saints was its red zone offense, one that was last in the NFL last season. That concern came up again as the Saints were in the red zone three times and failed to score a single point.
New Orleans moved to the Rams' 6-yard line on the opening drive of the second half, but Los Angeles safety Alex Cook intercepted Rattler's pass intended for Treyton Welch and returned it 100 yards for a touchdown.
The Saints got inside the Rams' 10-yard line again later in the half, but running back Ty Chandler fumbled after a 3-yard run. The Rams recovered at their own 3-yard line to end the threat.
The Saints had one last chance to put points on the board, but Tanner Brown missed a 39-yard field goal with 37 seconds left on the clock.

title: 4 Quotes: Kellen Moore Has Blunt Assessment of Saints After Ugly Rams Shutout
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints fell to 0-2 in the preseason after its shutout 34-0 against the Los Angeles Rams .
Head coach Kellen Moore was just as bewildered as the people back on the Gulf Coast watching the game as the New Orleans Saints lost to the Los Angeles Rams . Read our game story here .
While it was a preseason game, the Saints did not want that embarrassing result at all as they committed three turnovers, two of which happened inside the 10-yard line in the Rams' territory, and were the preseason returned for a 100-yard touchdown. There's also the fact that the Saints went 0-for-3 in the redzone and committed 12-penalties that resulted in 96 yards.
Here are four notable quotes from his postgame presser.
Regular season, pre-season, does not matter. You know, those ones aren't the ones you want. You know, that was a big-time missed opportunity for us. It starts with me: we didn't respond the right way. I thought we had a really good week out here. As far as the workload that we got, we just missed an opportunity at the end of this week, and obviously it's really frustrating. At the end of the day, film is your resume in this league—coaches, players. We didn't coach well enough to prepare ourselves to take advantage of this opportunity, and so, obviously, hopefully it's going to be a really valuable lesson for our team, a response opportunity for our team moving forward with one more week of essentially pre-season football, preparation week, and a game in Dallas.
Yeah. Just a lack—lack of discipline, lack of detail. A lot of them are under our control. You know, 12 penalties in a football game is—you're not going to win football games. And I feel like we've talked a lot about that, and it was obviously a step back from the progress that we felt like we've made. So it's going to be a lesson.
Obviously, we're going to have to watch the film really closely because, you know, your gut reaction is obviously that we want to accomplish more, you know, as an offense. We had the unfortunate interception in the first half. We had one in the red zone in the second half where we're driving. We're just going to have to watch this film and get better. I thought those guys had some really good work throughout this entire week, and obviously, as a team collectively, we didn't take advantage of this opportunity today.
We're going to get to learn some great lessons from this game, I think, at the end of the day. There's going to be some challenging lessons coming out of this game, but I think it's going to be lessons nevertheless. And I think that just shows you the discipline, the details of football. You know, they didn't have the penalties. They didn't turn the ball over. They ran the ball well. They took advantage of opportunities in the red zone. You know, it's a game of execution, and I think at the end of the day we didn't prepare ourselves well enough from a coaching perspective. Our guys weren't there, and so we got to reset together. And, hey, we're going to go back to Metairie. We're going to have a great week of practice out there, get ourselves ready

title: Saints Make Mistake After Mistake in Embarrassing Shutout Loss to Rams
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints fell to 0-2 in the preseason after its shutout 34-0 against the Los Angeles Rams .
It was truly as ugly as the score indicates as the Saints were outgained 405-293, had 13 first downs compared to the Rams’ 28, three turnovers including a pick six and 12 penalties that resulted in 96 yards.
Spencer Rattler had the better day than Zach Wilson , completing 14 of his 23 passes for 141 yards, but he was the one who threw the pick six. Wilson, who started the game, completed six of the 12 passes for 55 yards and also threw an interception.
Meanwhile, Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson combined to throw 254 yards for the Rams with Bennett tossing for 181 yards and scoring two downs on the ground.
Rams running back Jarquez Hunter led both teams with 68 yards on 12 carries with a touchdown.
Saints head coach Kellen Moore took full blame for today’s performance.
"Regular season, preseason, does not matter. Those are not the ones you want," Moore said.
Unlike the last game where the Saints got off to a hot start, this week was the exact opposite as the Saints were manhandled from the get-go with the Rams building a 17-0 lead.
Los Angeles outgained the Saints 272 to 107 in half number one. The biggest difference was the passing game as Bennett torched the Saints defense, finishing off both of the Rams’ touchdown drives in the first half with rushing touchdowns.
CJ Daniels led the Rams with eight catches for 68 yards in the first half.
Possession played a huge factor in Los Angeles' favor as they held onto the ball seven minutes longer than New Orleans did in the first half and ran 47 plays compared to the 26 plays run by the Saints.
Wilson was ineffective at leading the offense as the Saints failed to gain more than 30 yards on the four drives they had in the first half. And each of them ran seven plays or fewer. He also threw a critical interception that led to Los Angeles' first touchdown of the game.
The Saints finally put together a drive of more than 30 yards in the second half as Rattler led an efficient opening series, highlighted by a 25-yard pass to Jalen Moreno-Cropper . Despite heavy contact on the play, Moreno-Cropper made the catch while drawing a defensive pass interference penalty that New Orleans declined.
New Orleans moved to the Rams' 6-yard line, but Los Angeles safety Alex Cook intercepted Rattler's pass intended for Treyton Welch and returned it 100 yards for a touchdown.
The Saints reached Rams' territory again later in the half, but running back Ty Chandler fumbled after a 3-yard run. The Rams recovered at their own 3-yard line to end the threat.
Hunter would score the final touchdown of the game when he scored from 12 yards out for the final margin to finish off a dominant performance by Los Angeles and an embarrassing permance by New Orleans.
The Saints had one last chance to score points again with a 39-yard field goal, but Tanner Brown missed it.
A reminder: it’s only a preseason game. But it doesn’t excuse the silly mistakes and lackluster performance.

title: 3 Things to Watch When Saints Face Rams in Preseason Week 2
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints face the Los Angeles Rams in their second preseason game at 3 p.m. Saturday at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.
New Orleans is coming off a 24-20 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in its preseason opener, while the Rams won their first preseason game 20-12 over the Kansas City Chiefs.
Key storylines for the Saints include the ongoing backup quarterback competition and the emergence of potential roster locks. Saturday's matchup offers a critical look at the following three areas as training camp continues.
That is question No. 1 for a lot of people, and for good reason.
Spencer Rattler was the backup quarterback to Tyler Shough heading into the first preseason game against the Jacksonville Jaguars . However, Zach Wilson outplayed Rattler in that game, which ultimately led to a change in the rotation, with Wilson taking the first snaps with the second-team offense.
After that, Wilson took the first reps with the combined second- and third-team offense. Is that a sign that a rotation has taken place? Well, Wilson may be expected to go on the field first, but he still has to outplay Rattler if he wants to win the backup quarterback job and make the final 53-man roster.
In a crowded receiving corps, standing out by any means necessary is essential — a challenge wide receiver Bub Means is actively meeting.
During last week's preseason matchup against the Jaguars, Means paced the offense with four receptions for a team-leading 77 yards. His performance featured a 28-yard reception that initially appeared to be a touchdown before being overturned on video replay.
Pro Football Focus (PFF) named Means the Saints’ highest-graded wide receiver against Jacksonville last Saturday, with an 81.0 grade. Beyond his receiving numbers, he impressed the coaching staff with the finer details of his game. He also earned a standout 84.7 run-blocking score from PFF, trailing only left tackle Asim Richards .
Last week, Means and Wilson were the breakout stars offensively, as their connection in the passing game drew extra attention to them for the rest of training camp.
Defensive end Michael Heldman has been a training camp darling, but his two sacks against the Jaguars last week have made some predict him as a lock for the 53-man roster.
Linebacker Jaylan Ford and defensive back Jayden Price also locked in their place among the second team.
With the injuries in the running back room, could Kendre Miller and Devin Neal remind people they are still here? Can Ty Chandler show the Saints that the 86-yard kickoff return to open the game last week was no fluke?
Could we have a breakout performance from wide receivers Kevin Austin or Trey Palmer ?
We will find out on Saturday.

title: Giants Trade Joshua Ezeudu to Chiefs for Draft Capital
full_text:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh mentioned that he wouldn’t object if the team could swing a few more trades involving some of their extra talent, and sure enough, that’s what happened.
The Giants sent offensive lineman Joshua Ezeudu to the Kansas City Chiefs for a 2028 seventh round draft pick .
Ezeudu was originally a third-round draft pick (No. 67 overall) out of North Carolina in 2022, where he had earned third-team All-ACC honors in the 2020 season.
Ezeudu, who played offensive tackle in college, initially came to the Giants projected to move inside, playing 10 games as a rookie, with 2 starts at left guard.
Unfortunately, injuries have hampered his development.
In 2023, he stepped in as the starting left tackle for Andrew Thomas in Week 2 of the season after Thomas suffered a hamstring strain in the Week 1 opener against Dallas. Ezeudu had his struggles over the next five games, before his season ended thanks to a toe injury.
He spent all of last season on IR due to a calf injury. And just last week, he was kicked in the back of his leg at the joint practice against Miami, which caused him to miss a couple of practices.
Ezeudu finished his Giants career having appeared in 738 snaps over 33 games, with 10 total starts.
Ezeudu had been competing with the second team offensive line at right guard and right tackle.
He played 27 snaps in the preseason opener at right tackle, 30 at right guard, and 17 at right tackle in last week’s game against Miami, and has posted a perfect pass-blocking efficiency rating .
Ezeudu had been working with the second team offense this summer, but with him now moving on, the depth behind the five starters appears to be Aaron Stinnie, one of Lucas Patrick or Bryan Hudson (both of whom can play guard or center), and rookie JC Davis.
Evan Neal, who has been working at guard this summer, still remains in the mix and could be the final man kept if the Giants decide to keep nine offensive linemen.

title: Giants' Training Camp Surprises: Nabers, Fields Fuel Growing Optimism
full_text:
Running back Devin Singletary took the handoff from Jameis Winston, made a wide turn around the right corner, and scampered 13 yards into the end zone without much difficulty.
His dash against the Dolphins pretty much summed up the New York Giants ' four-day trip to Miami, one filled with increased optimism as the team winds down training camp with one preseason game remaining.
Head coach John Harbaugh has seen plenty of good things from his starters on both sides of the ball. And he's been able to hold them out of the preseason more so because of his confidence in them rather than concern over potential injuries.
There are the obvious veteran starters who look as though they haven't missed a beat - headlined by outside linebacker Brian Burns, who clearly has emerged as one of the team leaders, and left tackle Andrew Thomas. Harbaugh knew what to expect from them, and they have shown him to be exactly what was visible on tape.
However, Harbaugh may be even more pleased by the surprises he's received this August—and you could start with the wide receivers, given the rapid development of third-round pick Malachi Fields and the remarkable progress made by injured star Malik Nabers.
Nabers has been very impressive during his ramp-up following reconstructive knee surgery last October. He rid himself of the "no contact" red jersey this week and appears to have given himself a chance to return to the lineup sooner rather than later with opening day against Dallas less than three weeks away.
"I thought he looked good ... was moving well, probably moving the best we've seen him look," Harbaugh said Monday. "Got the red shirt off; that was a good step."
Health never was a concern for Fields, although nobody knew how quickly he would adapt to the pro game after a strong career at Virginia and Notre Dame. But his high-level work ethic has allowed him to ascend quickly.
"He's going to be even more determined to continue to improve. That's just who he is," Harbaugh explained.
"There's no way he's going to get the big head. That's not what he's about, so I expect him to keep improving. I know he will. And if you ask him, he'll probably tell you the three, four, five things he didn't do well. That's what he'll be thinking about."
There's also been a surge in the veteran secondary, starting with cornerback Deonte Banks and safety Jevon Holland and the return of reserve inside linebacker Micah McFadden coming off a broken foot.
And one cannot say enough about how far the offensive line has come since the end of the 2024 season. No, this area is no longer considered a serious weakness on the roster.
Reserves such as centers Lucas Patrick and Bryan Hudson, tackles Marcus Mbow and J.C. Davis, guard Aaron Stinnie, and swingman Joshua Ezeudu have given the Giants plenty of good vibes.
