title: Giants' Calvin Austin III Carted Off With Possible Significant Knee Injury
full_text:
New York Giants wide receiver Calvin Austin III, who appeared well on his way to earning a roster spot after having signed with the team in the offseason, suffered what could be a significant knee injury during the team’s practice on Tuesday.
Austin was injured in a one-on-one matchup against cornerback Deonte Banks when the injury struck him in what appears to have happened during a non-contact situation .
His injury brought the practice to a halt as concerned teammates and coaches came over to console the distraught receiver, who was then carted off the field for further evaluation.
Head coach John Harbaugh was not scheduled to speak to the media on Tuesday, so no update was immediately available regarding Austin’s status.
All indications are this is exactly as bad as it looked for those on site at #Giants practice today. Tough one for Austin, who was set for a key role. https://t.co/qbLn2nGf3j
Regardless, it’s a potentially devastating blow for the young receiver and one that potentially resets the depth chart at the position with less than a week to go before the initial 53-man roster needs to be set.
The 5-foot-8, 162-pound Austin, who signed a one-year deal with the Giants in free agency earlier this year, was having a solid summer and preseason.
In two games (38 snaps), he caught both of his pass targets for 24 yards and had one rushing attempt this past weekend on a jet sweep that went for 21 yards.
Austin also appeared well on his way to locking down the team’s punt return role after averaging 14.5 yards on two returns, those coming last weekend in the win over Miami.
Austin’s injury shakes up the Giants’ depth chart at receiver and potentially puts Odell Beckham Jr., who can flex inside and out, and Braxton Berrios, who can return punts and kickoffs, on firmer ground in their respective quests for a roster spot.
It could also mean that any plans for trading one of their extra receivers such as Darnell Mooney, is now off the table as the Giants look to assess Austin's injury and determine where to go from here.

title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Slips on Giants' Unofficial Depth Chart
full_text:
While many of the roster decisions for the New York Giants are falling into place, a new conundrum has apparently opened up at running back.
On the team’s unofficial depth chart–unofficial because the coaches don’t sanction it–the picture at running back has changed.
Cam Skattebo, who last week got the day off against the Dolphins, is listed as the starter, and behind him, the chart lists Tyrone Tracy Jr., Najee Harris, or Devin Singletary as RB2.
On the two prior versions of the unofficial depth chart, Skattebo and Tracy had been listed as the RB1.
Tracy has had a rough two weeks. In the preseason opener, he whiffed on a blitz pickup against Vikings defender Jay Ward, the safety crashing into quarterback Jaxson Dart with a hit that sent the quarterback to the medical tent for the sixth time in his short career.
Then last week in rainy conditions, Tracy lost the handle on the ball while inside the Dolphins’ 10-yard line, the ball coming loose despite the running back not having been touched.
Despite Tracy’s in-game struggles, head coach John Harbaugh wasn’t willing to give up on the third-year back who is seeking his third straight season with 1,000 all-purpose yards.
“I don’t think you say, hey, a bad play or even two bad plays nullifies a whole career body of work,” Harbaugh said.
“In the last two games, he’s had two things you don’t want to have. So, nobody feels worse about it than he does. He’s a very conscientious, very determined guy. It matters a lot to him, so he’s beating himself up.
“But the rest of the plays were all good. They were all pluses. So, you don’t hold it against him. At the same time, you understand how valuable and important those things are to your football team, and he knows as well.”
Tracy has eight carries for 31 yards, a 3.9 yards per carry average, the per carry average the same as Singletary’s, who has 11 carries for 43 yards.
Skattebo, who has half of Tracy’s carries total, has 19 yards, giving him a team-best 4.8 yards per carry average.
Tracy, according to PFF, has the lowest grades out of six Giants running backs in terms of overall grade and rushing grade.
The 2024 fifth-round pick, who converted from wide receiver to running back when he got to Purdue, has 1,579 career rushing yards on 368 attempts and seven touchdowns, plus five career fumbles.

title: Giants Rookie J.C. Davis Seized His Shot in First Extensive Preseason Action
full_text:
Those might be the most important three words the New York Giants' coaching staff can preach inside the locker room. And among those who can keep the quarterback upright is rookie offensive lineman J.C. Davis, who showed he’s definitely up to the challenge, having done so for Jameis Winston in the team’s 26-3 preseason win over the Miami Dolphins last weekend.
Davis made the most of his opportunities in his most extensive NFL playing time, having gone the distance in the game . The sixth-round draft pick was unflappable, refusing to yield against a defensive line brimming with desperation and hunger. He allowed no pressure in 81 snaps, and he consistently graded out in the high 80s overall in run and pass blocking, per Pro Football Focus .
“I think the last time I played a game that hot had to be when I was in New Mexico; we played A&M,” the former First-Team All-Big Ten and First-Team All-Mountain West selection said.
"So, it’s been a minute since I played in something like that, but we were prepared. We were hydrating all week, so we knew it was going to be hot. We had practice out there Thursday, so we were well prepared for it."
The Giants wanted to test Davis, and he aced the exam. The Oakland, California, native eventually found his way in the trenches. He thrived in his sophomore year with the New Mexico Lobos and then helped Illinois post a 19-7 record across the 2024 and 2025 campaigns. What will he do in the Meadowlands?
Initially regarded as a raw prospect in need of at least a year of seasoning, Davis is playing himself onto the 53-man roster, and his performance against the Dolphins has made it a risk to even contemplate exposing him to waivers next week when training camp rosters must be trimmed.
The 22-year-old is confident in his abilities—his accolades speak for themselves— but he is grateful for the chance to study under one of the best protectors in the NFL : left tackle Andrew Thomas.
"He does way different stuff than me, but I'm trying to pick up and learn from him and pick off stuff that he does," Davis said. "Some stuff you can't do what he does. That's him."
The Giants do not need this young lineman to be the next Thomas. They want him to work hard and slide in when necessary, and he earned a decent amount of trust in Miami.
"I think it was a great opportunity for the coaches to see my ability, what I could do at left tackle, and I think it went pretty well," Davis remarked.
"Of course, I’ve got things to improve on, but overall, it was a good game. We got the win. That was the most important thing."
John Harbaugh surely loved that sentiment. Davis waited three days to hear his name called at the NFL Draft, but New York handpicked him to join its remodeling project. After starting on the ground floor, the 6-foot-2, 322-pounder is rising rather quickly.
Davis should enter the Giants' final preseason matchup with reinforced confidence and plenty of momentum.

title: Giants 53-Man Roster Projection 4.0: Does Odell Beckham Jr. Make the Cut?
full_text:
This week is the final act for a lot of the New York Giants ’ 90-man roster.
Make or break. Sink or swim. By this time next week, the initial 53-man roster’s identity will be known, the winners of the summer’s marquee roster battles determined, and the preparations for the start of the regular season underway in full swing.
“We're certainly not certain about what we want to do yet, yet I wouldn't say it's all up in the air either,” head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday. “There's probably some key points, some clutch areas where we just have to make decisions still, with three, four, five decisions that have to be made.”
Some will end up returning to the Giants’ practice squad, and others will land with other teams. In this, our fourth iteration of the Giants’ initial 53-man roster, we not only look at projections for each unit but also at the biggest questions for the position groups.
We’ve been projecting the 53-man roster since the end of the mandatory minicamp in June; our last version is found here .
As we get ready to do another–and yes, there will be one after the preseason finale on Friday against the Jets–we’re focused more on this installment being about the biggest questions at each position unit and how they could sway the outcome of the final projection.
The Giants are keeping Jaxson Dart and Jameis Winston, but the question to which the answer isn’t as clear is whether they intend to keep a third quarterback on the practice squad and, if so, who.
The third quarterback would serve as a fallback plan should Dart, who has already had one trip to the blue medical tent, draw future trips from which it’s determined he’s not fit to return to action.
One would think that given the newness of the system, that Brandon Allen, who has not exactly set the league on fire this summer, would be the logical choice to retain given his familiarity with the offense at this point, but the Giants did add Jake Haener to the mix, though presumably that was to give them three quarterbacks for the preseason game against Miami in which Dart and the starters didn’t play.
The arrival of Najee Harris has thrown the projected order at this position into flux, but does it really matter?
First, Harris is still working his way back into football shape after missing most of last year with an Achilles injury. Everyone seems to be rushing to assume that Harris is now RB1, followed by Cam Skattebo as RB2, Devin Singletary as RB3, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. as RB4.
While that still might end up being the case, a more likely scenario is that Harris, who has the potential to be a “Derrick Henry light” for the Giants, and Skattebo switch back and forth in doing the pounding part of the run game; Tracy does the finesse stuff, and the nondescript but still very valuable Singletary gives them a little bit of everything.
In other words, the exact pecking order might not matter as much as some think it will, as whoever gets his number called will be determined by the opponent, match-up, and situation.
Patrick Ricard is technically a fullback, but he’s been running with the tight ends. This poses an interesting decision.
First, Isaiah Likely and Theo Johnson are locks. Ricard is also a lock. And considering how Chris Manhertz was voted as part of the team’s leadership council by his teammates, it’s hard to fathom him not being a lock as well.
So what about Thomas Fidone II? Fidone did well to get in the way of defenders in pass-blocking situations, but when it came to run blocking, he wasn’t as effective.
To be fair, injuries have plagued him in his first year-plus with the Giants, so perhaps further development on the practice squad would be just what the doctor ordered.
Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields, Darius Slayton, and Calvin Austin III are the locks at this position. That leaves, potentially, two spots for Braxton Berrios, Darnell Mooney, Dalen Cambre, Isaiah Hodgins, Xavier Gipson, Jalin Hyatt, and Odell Beckham Jr., assuming the Giants only keep six at this spot.
Mooney has been linked to early trade rumors, given the overlap between him and Darius Slayton in their skill sets.
While Berrios can give the Giants one guy for three different roles–receiver, punt returner, and kickoff returner–the Giants have other guys who can fill those roles and then some, Austin being one such guy.
If Cambre, who has been one of the better special teams performers for the Giants, makes the roster, and Jalin Hyatt, who is languishing away in the trainer’s room with a leg/ankle injury that almost certainly will have him landing on IR, that should leave a spot open for Beckham, the fan favorite who is trying to end his career where it all began.
The Giants, believe it or not, are stocked at tackle thanks to the solid showing by sixth-round draft pick J.C. Davis, who is on the upswing, giving Big Blue starters Andrew Thomas, Jermaine Eluemunor, Davis, and Marcus Mbow at the position.
The interior is the bigger question mark, however. Francis Mauigoa, the first-round draft pick this year, is a lock for the future. Jon Runyan, the incumbent at left guard, is not, as he is not signed beyond this year. Behind Runyan and Mauigoa are Aaron Stinnie, Lucas Patrick, Evan Neal, Josh Ezeudu, and Jake Kubas.
Stinnie should be a lock to make it as he’s not only durable; he’s reliable and has quietly had a strong summer in both run blocking and pass protection in the 56 snaps he’s played.
The coaches seem to like what they have seen from Ezeudu, who, believe it or not, has also had a strong showing this summer in 74 snaps played.
Ezeudu, whose 74 snaps are the second most behind Davis’s 102, has not allowed a quarterback pressure thus far in preseason action. The only concern with Ezeudu, to be frank, is that he seems to be snake-bit as far as injuries go.
That said, Stinnie and Ezeudu appear to be the leading contenders as far as backup depth at guard goes.
And speaking of backup depth, we have to address the center position. John Michael Schmitz is the starter, but he, too, has been snakebit by injuries.
Bryan Hudson saw extensive work at center when Schmitz missed the preseason opener, and on par, he has been solid in run blocking, posting the highest PFF grade (69.0) of the three Giants centers (Schmitz and Brenden Jaimes are the other two). Hudson can also be an emergency guard if needed.
With Lucas Patrick having dealt with knee issues, Hudson makes more sense for the coming season.
Yes, yes, and yes. But first, DJ Reader, Shelby Harris, Darius Alexander, and Chauncey Golston are all locks. Bobby Jamison-Travis hasn’t been a disaster, but he’s still on the raw side. That said, it would be surprising if the Giants try to slide him through to the practice squad.
Now to the original question. Who is the backup to Reader at nose tackle? If Jamison-Travis is still raw, it probably won’t be him. Leki Fotu, who could give them snaps at nose tackle, has been a disappointment, ranking as PFF’s lowest of the Giants’ eight defensive linemen (out of eight) overall and in run defense grades.
Whether it’s a trade or a waiver wire claim, don’t be surprised if the Giants prioritize this position group at cut-down. We have five projected here, but we strongly believe there will be a sixth lineman added.
When putting together a roster projection, it’s important not to ignore special teams. And when one thinks of special teams, usually it’s a receiver, defensive back, or linebacker who finds himself specifically with that role.
That’s why I have added an extra linebacker to the foursome I originally had: Arvell Reese, Tremaine Edmunds, Micah McFadden, and Jack Kelly.
The fifth spot will come down to Zaire Barnes or Darius Muasau, two linebackers who can give a little on the defensive side of things, but whose roles will be more special teams than anything else.
Based on PFF grades, Muasau, in 209 snaps, is the second-highest-graded Giant in the special teams category, with a 79.2 mark. Muasau has played seven more special teams…

title: Giants Aren't Done Exploring Making Trades
full_text:
A week after trading offensive lineman Daniel Faalele to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a sixth-round pick, the New York Giants might not be done yet trying to make deals.
“Yeah, I mean, if we could, we'd do it as much as we possibly could,” head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday. “We'd like to take advantage of the opportunities, if they'll come up, as much as we can.”
The Faalele deal came as a surprise to many, largely because he was trending toward not making the roster to begin with, plus the Giants were able to get a concrete sixth-round pick with zero conditions attached.
The additional pick gives the Giants six in next year’s draft, with the team, again, looking to add more picks wherever they can.
“We do have some guys,” Harbaugh said of the possibility without going into specifics. “We're kind of deep in a few positions, and maybe that'll happen. It doesn't happen that often, but maybe it will.”
That the Giants are in a position to make a deal speaks to the job Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen did in assembling the training camp roster.
“You know, it's not too often you can trade a player for a sixth-round pick in the middle of training camp,” Harbaugh said. “But sometimes teams have needs.
“Any time you can add picks, it's a valuable thing. It's a future thing. Doesn't seem like much now, but it'll matter on Day 3 of the draft. It'll be something that we'll be happy we've got.”
Among the leading possibilities for a trade are kicker Ben Sauls, one of receiver Darius Slayton or Darnell Mooney, and perhaps an offensive lineman like center/guard Jake Kubas and inside linebacker Darius Muasau.
But for a trade to happen, the Giants will obviously need to find a team that isn’t willing to be patient and wait out the waiver-wire game.
As for the Giants, if they can swing another deal or two and land a compensatory pick, Big Blue could put itself in position to have a full hand of seven picks—and then some.
They're also in position to acquire a fourth-round pick if former offensive lineman Austin Schlottmann, now with the Tennessee Titans, wins and holds the starting center job there.
“The draft is a little bit of a numbers game,” Harbaugh said. “The more swings you can take, the more chances you have to hit on guys. So, having more picks over time, I hope that's something that we're able to accumulate and have a lot of picks year to year.”

title: Malik Nabers Sheds the Red Jersey, but Harbaugh Won't Guarantee Receiver's Status for Week 1
full_text:
One gets the feeling that the New York Giants know it’s going to happen: that receiver Malik Nabers will indeed be ready for Week 1 of the regular season, especially after the receiver took the next step in his return by shedding the red “no-contact” jersey after wearing it last week and participating in 11-on-11 and 7-on-7 drills.
Malik Nabers with the white jersey at practice today pic.twitter.com/2GRssvh3Vk
But head coach John Harbaugh stopped short of declaring Nabers’s readiness for the start of the regular season, which will be here in a little under four weeks.
“I don’t want to make any kind of statements like that,” Harbaugh said when asked if Nabers was trending toward being ready for Week 1 of the season, barring any setbacks.
“I think it’s reasonable to assume that. Those are all things to assume based on watching him practice. The only thing I know more than you guys do is what the trainers and doctors tell me about his rehab, and he’s doing really well with it. He’s strong, in a good place. How he gets through practice and how ready he is to play and protect himself is really based on practice.”
Nabers will obviously need to take some hits during practice as the next step in his return, which he didn’t do during Monday’s shorts and shells practice.
Come Tuesday, when the Giants are next scheduled to be in pads, it’s anticipated he’ll get to experience live contact (although not tackling to the ground) for the first time in a practice.
"It'll be a protect each other kind of deal, but that'll be true for everybody right now,” he said. “We'll be in this mode this week; we'll be a little more, as far as the contact part of it, probably a little more in-season-ish in terms of taking care of one another.”
Despite Harbaugh’s reluctance to make a definitive statement about Nabers, it’s not hard to get excited about the increasing likelihood of the third-year receiver being ready for Sunday Night Football against the Cowboys.
“I thought he looked good,” Harbaugh said. “He was moving well–probably moving the best we've seen him look. It was a good practice for him today. Got the red shirt off. That was a good step.”
The players have apparently voted on the Giants' new leadership council, and eight guys were identified as part of that group : quarterbacks Jaxson Dart and Jameis Winston, outside linebacker Brian Burns, safety Jevon Holland, inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, left tackle Andrew Thomas, tight end Chris Manhertz, and punter Jordan Stout.
The group was spotted speaking with Harbaugh about what the coach described as logistical matters after the team concluded practice. It’s unclear, though, if those eight players are also viewed as the team captains.
“We've been doing it for a long time,” Harbaugh said of having a leadership group. “I do try to emphasize to the team that everybody's a leader and everybody has every opportunity to speak their mind. Talk to anybody in the organization about anything they need to, any suggestions they have.”
Besides the team leadership being defined, what’s also noteworthy about this development is that Manhertz, who some may have thought was in danger of losing his roster spot, appears to be safe for the coming season; otherwise, he wouldn’t have been part of the discussion.
Receiver Jalin Hyatt (ankle/leg), offensive lineman Joshua Ezeudu (leg), tight end Tanner Conner (unknown), receiver Braxton Berrios (soft tissue), guard Francis Mauigoa (stinger), right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (unknown), defensive lineman Shelby Harris (unknown), and linebacker Jack Kelly (unknown) did not practice.
Harbaugh said that Eluemunor will be fine and “should be back tomorrow (Tuesday),” as should Mauigoa.
Cornerback Colton Hood (quad) returned to practice.
Tight end Theo Johnson collided with outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux during practice and appeared shaken up. “I think he's okay,” Harbaugh said. “Didn't get a report back that it was serious, but they'll look at it. I haven't talked to him since, so I'll go in and find out here when we get done.”

title: John Harbaugh Opens Up on the Hardest Part of Cutdown Week: 'Very Challenging'
full_text:
And just like that, the dog days of training camp for the New York Giants are behind them as they enter the final week of the preseason, a critical week for head coach John Harbaugh, the coaching staff, and the players.
There are roster decisions to be made, regular-season routines to get used to, and, through it all, improvements still rule the daily agenda.
It’s a critical point for Harbaugh, who, in recognizing the human element of what’s to come, knows that in a matter of a week, he’ll have to be the bearer of bad news to almost half of his rostered players who have given the team everything they have, only to eventually learn that it wasn’t enough to continue on their journey with Big Blue.
John Harbaugh spoke at length when asked roster cuts looming "Everybody's pulling for everybody. Guys that are competing for the same position - they're rooting for each other. You see so many of the best things about human mature come out on a football team" pic.twitter.com/HJ1kQMltF6
“We tell them your best dream is not too big; in fact, it might not even be big enough,” Harbaugh, in response to a question posed by New York Giants On SI, said in a lengthy answer.
“If they're not laughing at your dream, then it's not big enough either, so say it, speak it, and go for it. These guys have really done that. I feel like they've really put that out there and they've talked to each other; they've committed to helping one another achieve each other's dreams. Everybody's pulling for everybody.”
The supportive structure Harbaugh described is precisely the type of culture he sought to build when hired by the Giants to lead the franchise out of its modern-day Wilderness Years.
The bond the team has built has been evident. There’s been nary a training camp scuffle, and there's also been more and more cross-training, to the point where offensive and defensive players have come together to share feedback and tips to help each other improve, while even players in direct competition share feedback between plays.
“You see it on the sideline, you see it between guys who are competing for the same position,” he said. “They're rooting for each other and helping each other along. I mean, you see so many of the best things about human nature come out on a football team, believe it or not.
“And maybe people that aren't a part of the sport would have a tough time believing that, but I think those of us who've been around the sport understand that this is how it works and it's a cool thing.”
Harbaugh, now in his 19th year as head coach, undoubtedly finds having to tell guys who have given everything they have that it wasn’t good enough one of the most gut-wrenching aspects of the job.
There is no easy way to do that, after all, but the veteran head coach, in his message to those who don’t make the initial 53-man roster, wants to leave those players with hope for the future.
“This week, to your point, is a very challenging week because there will be guys that won't be here after this week. Now, maybe they'll come back–we brought (defensive lineman) Ben (Barten) back, the defensive lineman who just got released by the Jets and came back to us again here this week,” Harbaugh said.
And if they don’t, Harbaugh said he hopes the young men who do receive a visit from “The Turk” understand that it’s not so much about what they didn’t accomplish as about how far they’ve come.
“How many of us who played football wouldn't have loved to have had an opportunity to be in a football camp in the National Football League? To be invited, to get a tryout even? All the not-so-good players like me would have loved that,” he said.
“I tell these guys, ‘You are the very best. Every single player here in this room is a great football player.’ You talk about the top .0001 percent of football players, even athletes, in the world that are going to be in a football camp.
“But then there are levels to that too, just like there are levels to anything else. I would say everybody, every one of our guys, whether they're here the next week or they're not, will look back and say they did their very best, they put their best foot forward, and it's something that they can look back on really for the rest of their life proudly.”

title: Tyler Nubin Tabbed as Giants' Breakout Candidate by PFF Amid Safety Competition
full_text:
After a disappointing second season, New York Giants safety Tyler Nubin is in a battle for his starting job .
Offseason additions Ar'Darius Washington and Jason Pinnock have been making strong cases to overtake Nubin , earning attention from head coach John Harbaugh in recent weeks.
Pro Football Focus writer Gordon McGuinness isn't concerned about the mounting pressure on Nubin, having named Nubin as the Giants' top breakout candidate for 2026, citing the safety’s slight improvement in his PFF coverage grade from 58.1 in his rookie season to 60.0 in his second year.
“Entering his third NFL season, don’t be surprised if Nubin generates more buzz, particularly if he can recapture the level of run defense he showed as a rookie," McGuinness concluded.
With 98 tackles and a forced fumble in just 13 games in his rookie season, Nubin looked like a long-term starter for the Giants. Big Blue tried to cover up his coverage deficiencies by using him as a box defender on nearly half of his snaps.
Those strengths were much less apparent in his second season. Nubin missed 16.9% of his tackles (up from 9.4% as a rookie) and made 78 tackles despite playing more snaps. He was part of the problem in the Giants' run defense, which ranked near the bottom of the league .
Nubin will have to adjust his game to thrive in new defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson's system . The safety was much stronger in man coverage than in zone coverage last season. He earned a PFF grade of 64.5 in man and a grade of 54.1 in zone.
Wilson is anticipated to use zone coverage at a significantly higher rate than previous coordinator Shane Bowen did. Last season, his Tennessee Titans ran zone coverage on 75% of their snaps , while the Giants were down at 63.6%, near the bottom of the league.
Wilson has been encouraged by Nubin's progress this offseason.
"Tyler Nubin is getting better,” he said recently. “His biggest challenge right now is just looking at the right things. When he consistently looks at the right things, he makes plays. So, that's been his focus, but he's flashed.”
Before naming Nubin for a breakout campaign, he needs to secure the Giants' starting strong safety role. If he can make the adjustments that Wilson's system requires, he'll be set up for the breakout that McGuinness projects.
If not, his time as a starter may be limited.

title: 4 Biggest Takeaways from Jets' Practice (8/25): Offense Ends Training Camp on High Note
full_text:
And that'll do it. Training camp for the 2026 New York Jets has come to a close. With that, the focus can now shift to the preseason finale against the New York Giants on Friday, and then a Week 1 bout in Tennessee against the Titans.
Gang Green should be pleased with what their roster has looked like so far. They appear more talented and better balanced than any prior year in recent memory.
So before we turn our sights to the season opener, let's break down the biggest takeaways from Tuesday's day of work.
THIS is how training camp should look for NFL offenses. After splitting early practices with the defense further ahead in their installation, New York's passing attack has won considerably over the last week. Tuesday was no exception. Geno Smith pushed the ball downfield accurately and looked comfortable spreading the ball to plenty of the team's offensive weapons.
More importantly, those weapons made big plays. Whether it was Mason Taylor "mossing" Minkah Fitzpatrick or Omar Cooper picking up where he left off on Monday, the Jets should love where they are at offensively.
It should give them hope that the team might just be turning a corner on that side of the ball.
There are both good and bad things involving the Jets' offense. While Smith and the passing unit dominated, the backup unit continued to struggle mightily against the defensive line they went up against.
It didn't matter who it was; rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik was harassed throughout practice and didn't get much of a chance to operate from the pocket. While this could be seen as a glass-half-full scenario, the rotational defensive linemen should be very good this year, but New York must hope that their entire starting unit is healthy for a full 17-game season.
Otherwise, New York's depth is not where it should be right now along the line.
Much of the Jets' defensive line already feels figured out. New York invested quality money and draft capital on both the interior and edge of their defensive front. That doesn't mean a spot can't be opened up for a camp standout, though.
Nate Lynn, a former undrafted free agent who accepted an invite to the Jets after being picked up by Glenn's Lions in 2024, has played exceedingly well over the last week.
In Tuesday's practice, he recorded a sack, which is another notch on his belt after a two-sack game in last Friday's preseason contest . It will be hard for Lynn to crack the 53-man roster, so he'll need to continue to dominate at a high level in the team's preseason finale against the Giants.
As things stand, though, Lynn is making one last push in front of Jets coaching.
Outside of left guard Dylan Parham's absence at the end of team drills, there are no major updates to report on the Jets' current core of injured players. Running back Breece Hall , tight end Kenyon Sadiq, and cornerback D'Angelo Ponds were all working out in the rehab area today.
It's easy to assume that all three will be ready for the start of the regular season, but in what capacity remains a question. Hall won't need to be on a specific pitch count because he had almost a month of camp. For Ponds and Sadiq, though, small packages appear to be best for them as draft picks.
“There’s no doubt we’ll scale it back," Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said earlier on the Jets' plan for Sadiq in the offense when he returns. "We’ll have to work him in slowly.”
Again, this won't necessarily be the end of the world, but it does highlight the work that still needs to happen even after Ponds and Sadiq are back on the field.

title: Four 53-Man Roster Decisions I'd Make If I Were Jets GM This Week
full_text:
The New York Jets made a handful of roster moves last weekend in preparation for their final preseason game on Friday, releasing Caullin Lacy, Nate Voorhis, and Sam Scott. Then on Tuesday, they waived kicker Cade York. Those moves leave the Jets with 91 players on their roster.
These aren’t the only moves that GM Darren Mougey will have to make in the coming days. He’ll need to cut 38 more players by 6 p.m. on August 30, when he'll decide which bubble players to keep and determine if he wants to make any last-minute upgrades.
With that in mind, here are the four roster decisions if I were running the Jets.
Cade Klubnik firmly established himself as the QB2 over these past few weeks with strong showings in both training camp and preseason. While Klubnik winning the QB2 job appeared to be Mougey and the coaching staff’s plan all along, New York would be wise to add a veteran quarterback to the room.
If Geno Smith were to go down with an injury early in the season, Klubnik would be thrust into the starting role. If he struggles, it could hurt his confidence and potentially hinder his development.
That’s why Mougey and the Jets’ brass should target Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Andy Dalton. The 16-year veteran has played poorly in the preseason and, as a result, is projected to not only lose the QB2 competition to Tanner McKee but also a roster spot.
Although Dalton’s best days are behind him, his experience would benefit the Jets’ quarterback room and especially Klubnik. It gives New York a reliable option instead of throwing Klubnik into the fire, while also providing him with a seasoned veteran who can serve as a valuable mentor.
While the Jets could wait until Dalton is released, there’s no guarantee that he would sign or want to play for Gang Green; therefore, trading for him should be the preferred option. A 2027 sixth-round pick should be enough to acquire Dalton.
New York has been patiently waiting for either Kiko Mauigoa, Marcelino McCrary-Ball, or Mykal Walker to emerge and prove they can be a reliable rotational contributor. That has yet to happen.
While each player has had some strong moments, none have consistently stood out. This has ultimately left room for Chase Wilson, who’s made a strong case for a roster spot with his play the last few weeks.
Against the Pittsburgh Steelers Friday night, he led the team in tackles (6) alongside Jordan Clark, earned a 68 run-defense grade, per Pro Football Focus , and recorded a sack. He also fared well in coverage, being targeted just once across 24 coverage snaps.
Although the undrafted free agent out of West Virginia still needs to develop before he can become a meaningful contributor, he’s shown enough to warrant consideration for a roster spot. If Wilson has another strong performance in the preseason finale against the New York Giants, I wouldn’t think twice about keeping him on the roster.
The Jets’ starting offensive line is great, but they lack quality depth. Anez Cooper and Xavier Newman are the top two interior backups, while Chukwuma Okorafor and Max Mitchell are solid backup tackle options.
However, none have done enough to inspire confidence if a starter goes down. With Jets OnSI’s Nick Faria highlighting the backup offensive line as a serious concern from last Friday’s preseason game and Monday’s practice, the franchise should consider strengthening its depth by adding Thayer Munford Jr. to the mix.
The four-year veteran offers versatility, having experience at both tackle positions during his time with the Las Vegas Raiders and the New England Patriots. Munford has been a solid pass protector, allowing 10 sacks and 29 hurries across 674 pass-blocking snaps.
With the Patriots last season, he served as the jumbo tight end in heavy-run blocking formations, giving the Jets another way to use his skill. Munford could be a useful addition to the Jets’ running game in this role, which ranked 10th in rushing yards per game last season (123.3).
Munford wouldn’t completely solve New York’s depth concerns, but he would give the Jets another experienced option if Armand Membou or Olu Fashanu miss time.
Braiden McGregor had two years to show that he could be a meaningful contributor. He hasn’t. Last season, despite receiving plenty of playing time, he failed to establish himself as a reliable contributor.
In 265 defensive snaps, McGregor recorded 15 total tackles (one tackle for loss), one sack, and eight pressures. He was a non-factor against the run and unreliable at generating pressure, earning a 33.1 run-defense grade, which ranked 114th among 115 qualifying edge rushers, and a 58.9 pass-rush grade, per PFF .
The Jets can’t afford to keep waiting for him to develop, and they no longer need to. With the additions of David Bailey, Kingsley Enagbare, and Joseph Ossai alongside Will McDonald IV, New York is already set at edge rusher.
If the Jets decided they wanted to keep five edge rushers, I’d still give the final spot to someone other than McGregor. Nate Lynn is a name worth watching after his performance against the Steelers, where he posted two sacks and four total tackles. While still considered a long shot to make it, I’d rather give the spot to Lynn, who has shown more upside in the preseason.
At this point, there’s little reason to continue investing a roster spot in McGregor when the team could use it to give another player an opportunity.

title: Jets Preseason Darling Is Doing All the Right Things to Secure a Roster Spot
full_text:
It is easy to overreact to a preseason game, even when it results in a shutout win and highlights the improvements made by a defense that failed to even record a single interception last season.
That is what happened for the Jets in their 17-0 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers last Friday night. Preseason game or not, it was the type of performance you w anted to see from a team that finished 3-14 last season and was the league's second-worst scoring defense (29.6 PPG).
While quarterback Geno Smith and rookie defensive end David Bailey had standout performances, and safety Andre Cisco improved his outlook with one of the two interceptions in the game , one of the most underrated stories to emerge from the game was the performance from DE Nate Lynn, who was just signed on Aug. 18.
Lynn immediately emerged, recording four tackles, four pressures, and two sacks in 27 defensive snaps, earning an 85.9 pass-rush grade from Pro Football Focus.
As the projected fourth-stringer on the Jets' depth chart, Lynn is likely staring down another season on the practice squad. However, there is no denying that he helped his chances of making the 53-man roster with a breakout performance against the Steelers.
Sure, Lynn has an extremely tall task ahead of him, considering the talent already on this defensive front. With the likelihood that Joseph Ossai, Bailey, Will McDonald IV, Kingsley Enagbare, T'Vondre Sweat, Jowon Briggs, Harrison Phillips, David Onyemata, and Darrell Jackson Jr. each make the roster, that could leave one spot, especially when you consider that most teams carry 10 defensive linemen.
Even though Mory Bamba plays cornerback, he was one of the biggest winners from the preseason opener with five total tackles and four pass deflections; his injury leaves the door open for someone like Lynn to make a statement of his own one week later.
Lynn was a zero-star recruit coming out of high school before taking his talents to William & Mary (FCS). His best season there came during his redshirt sophomore season in 2021, when he recorded 52 tackles (13.5 for loss), 12 sacks, and six forced fumbles.
However, despite setting a program record with 12 forced fumbles and a second-best 28 sacks when his career at William & Mary wrapped up, Lynn went undrafted before later signing with the Detroit Lions.
Lynn impressed during the Lions' preseason opener in his rookie season in 2024, but a torn shoulder ligament forced Detroit to place him on the injured reserve list for the rest of the season.
Despite his best effort to redeem himself with eight hurries, one sack, and a quarterback hit the following preseason, Lynn didn't make the final roster and was later signed to the Tennessee Titans practice squad.
While Lynn's NFL career has not gone according to plan so far, he does have some previous experience with Jets head coach Aaron Glenn dating back to his time with the Lions. Glenn was glad to have the opportunity to bring him in and commended him for his impressive effort on Friday night .
"Nate Lynn, he was with me in Detroit, you know, so I know him really, really well," Glenn said. "And man, listen, we liked him, you know, in Detroit, so once we had an opportunity to get him back here, it was a no-brainer to get him in, let him compete, see how he operates and he did a really good job."
s/o Nate Lynn "it was a no brainer to get him here" pic.twitter.com/bcLcKqn5Ey
In six career preseason games, Lynn has recorded 19 total pressures and four sacks, giving the Jets reason to at least consider him for one of the 53-man roster spots that must be officially determined by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.
That being said, Friday night's preseason finale against the New York Giants will give players like Lynn one last opportunity to prove that they belong on their respective rosters.
A stacked defensive line unit will not make it easy for Lynn, but another strong showing on Friday night could go a long way in deciding his fate in Gang Green and writing another chapter in his underdog story.

title: Cade York's Release Doesn't Mean Jets' Kicking Troubles Are Over
full_text:
The New York Jets finally have a clear direction they want to go in for their starting kicker role.
As first reported by Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic , Gang Green waived veteran kicker Cade York after a months-long battle for the starting job with former Miami Dolphins All-Pro Jason Sanders. After weeks of competing, though, a stumble in the team's second preseason game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, coupled with recent struggles in practice, left the Jets with a clear answer.
But that doesn't mean their kicking problems are solved, however. They might only be just beginning.
To say that Sanders "won" the starting kicking job wouldn't necessarily be accurate. While Sanders was perfect through all preseason action , he too has struggled in practice. On Monday, the veteran missed three of five field goals, all from 30 to 40 yards away. That kind of inconsistency isn't something the Jets can afford.
Even if it was better than York's performance in last Friday's game (a miss from 59 yards out and a 3/5 day on Monday). York's career has been marred by disappointing performances. As a former fourth-round pick in the 2022 draft, he's never had a field goal percentage over 82 percent in his three years in the league.
Had the Jets named him the starting kicker, there would have been a large contingent of fans who were worried about the long-term future of the position.
Not unlike the current feelings felt now.
To put it kindly, no kicker truly earned the starting job for the Jets. Sanders just "won" the competition from York.
Sure, there were some solid days from both kickers, but neither consistently looked like a player who could handle kicking duties for a full 17 games. It also means the Jets have a difficult decision to figure out before the regular season begins.
New York could hope to get the All-Pro that Sanders was before he suffered through a hip injury that cost him the 2025 season. In doing so, they would probably have a short leash on the veteran, even with his past experience. Otherwise, the Jets could look to the free agent market when kickers become available and swoop one of those men up.
Some of the available kickers in free agency are Jake Moody, Brandon McManus, Graham Gano, and Matt Prater.
For better or worse, the Jets have multiple options to pick between and still plenty of time to make a final decision. And plenty of other organizations around the league will be doing the same ahead of roster cutdown day this weekend.

title: 3 Potential Jets Trade Targets Before 53-Man Roster Deadline (Including Andy Dalton)
full_text:
Nineteen days. The Jets are 20 days away from the start of the 2026 NFL regular season. Before that, the team needs to cut its current roster to 53 players by Sunday's deadline (6 p.m. ET) and fill out some of the bigger holes.
The good news is that the Jets don't necessarily have any glaring needs compared to the last few years. They have a well-balanced roster of talent that should be fun to watch this year. That being said, there are always places where a team can improve.
For the Jets, three trade candidates could be an option for them if they want to address any lingering roster concerns sooner rather than later.
There is no guarantee the Jets will bring in a veteran quarterback, especially if they continue to like what Cade Klubnik has put on film through his first training camp . Should New York opt for a more veteran option, Andy Dalton seems like the most logical conclusion.
First, Dalton has played under Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich before, so the transition should be somewhat seamless. New York would want a veteran backup with plenty of starting reps, but also someone who understands what Reich wants to do as a play-caller.
Finally, and for the most obvious reason, Dalton has been the worst of the backup quarterbacks for the Eagles in camp.
Tanner McKee seems poised to win the job and stay ahead of late-round selection Cole Payton. New York could simply wait for Dalton to get cut, but that would mean throwing a veteran like him to the open market, where he could catch on with another team.
If the Jets want to bring in a veteran backup and are hell-bent on bringing Dalton in, a trade is the only sure-fire way to make it happen.
New York doesn't necessarily need another pass rusher. Will McDonald IV, Davis Bailey, and Joseph Ossai are all quality players who can get to the quarterback. That being said, a fifth option wouldn't be the worst in the world.
Enter Marist Liufau. The former Cowboys draft pick was originally an off-ball linebacker before new defensive coordinator Christian Parker opted to transition him to the edge. While Liufau's athleticism is something to note, the Cowboys' addition of Von Miller in free agency changes how the team will look at Liufau.
With the Jets, the former third-round pick could be a developmental piece who brings speed and athleticism to the defense. You can never have too many pass rushers.
Of all the questions surrounding the offense right now, the most important position that needs to be addressed is the interior of the offensive line. The Jets do not have a competent backup center/guard who can keep things afloat. Xavier Newman hasn't cut it.
That's where Jarrett Patterson comes in, though.
Patterson has started 21 games during his three-year career with the Texans. Last season, he was ranked 50th out of 81 guards in the league by Pro Football Focus but does have starting experience.
He would be a basic backup behind Josh Myers who wouldn't take his job, but would understand the pressure of walking in to start in an NFL game. Jets fans would feel more confident with Patterson starting at center over Newman should the issue arise.
All eyes are waiting to see what the Vikings will do with former first-round pick J.J. McCarthy. After a less-than-stellar sophomore campaign, the Vikings handed the job to Kyler Murray over the former Michigan product.
Could the Jets bring in the young signal-caller?
While McCarthy makes plenty of sense as a young quarterback, the Jets seem intrigued by their own developmental arm in Klubnik and would rather wait to see how the 2026 campaign unfolds before making any decisions at quarterback. Remember, this is a team with three first-round picks at their disposal in 2027. New York won't judge McCarthy by Klubnik, but by the young quarterbacks in the 2027 class.
Based on that, it may not be worth bringing someone in.

title: 3 Studs & 3 Duds from Jets' Training Camp Practice (8/24): Geno Smith Builds Off Preseason Debut
full_text:
Another week, another start to New York Jets training camp. By this time next week, the organization will be down to 53 players, highlighting the job ahead for general manager Darren Mougey and head coach Aaron Glenn.
However, until that time, the Jets can focus their efforts on the final few practices of training camp ahead of the preseason finale against the New York Giants. As is always the case, there are plenty of studs and duds from the day of practice.
Let's get to the list now.
New York has seen a different Geno Smith over the last week. Coming off a dominant preseason performance in which he didn't throw a single incomplete pass and led a touchdown drive, Smith was back on the field and looked quite strong in New York's move-the-ball period and in the red zone.
As always, it's important to remember that Smith can have weeks with excellent play and poor performances.
The highlight of the day was a touchdown pass from Smith to rookie Omar Cooper Jr., which displayed the former Indiana prospect's improved play. Over the last several days, though, Smith has come on. And provided Jets fans with further hope for the 2026 season.
After the first couple of weeks of spirited competition, the Jets' kicking battle has devolved into a concerning conundrum. Cade York made 3-of-5 kicks, with misses from 38 and 43 yards. Not to be outdone, Jason Sanders went just 2-of-5 with three misses all around the 40-yard mark.
While 40-yard kicks are never a guarantee, the Jets need better from this kicker battle. The longer these struggles go on, the more likely it is that New York's Week 1 kicker isn't actually on the roster.
After missing the first few weeks of camp, Ossai has been a welcome addition to the Jets' defense . Not only has he been able to generate pressure, but he's also been very good at stopping the run, an underrated reason why he was added to the organization in the offseason.
Pairing Ossai with a young edge rusher like David Bailey seems like the most obvious course of action for the Jets in Week 1. So long as Ossai continues to play well, the group should feel much better about their defensive line moving forward.
There is serious concern about the offensive line depth, especially if one of New York's most important players along the line goes down with an injury. Anez Cooper is still a developmental player, but it isn't good that Cade Klubnik was consistently pressured at practice.
Again, it might not be an issue should the Jets have to replace one player, but the group's depth remains a big question after Friday's contest against the Steelers, and it's only getting worse.
There are legitimate questions surrounding the Jets' safety room. Most pressing among them is whether the organization is prepared to play Minkah Fitzpatrick as a center-field type safety, as opposed to the box to placate Belton's skill set.
Yes, it feels like a foregone conclusion that Belton has won the starting safety job opposite Fitzpatrick thanks to his physicality and improved coverage skills. He made numerous plays in practice, particularly against the run. While Andre Cisco is a quality third safety , especially in coverage, the Jets will need to be creative with how they break down the reps for this room.
There is some good news on this score. Breece Hall was seen working out on the side field, and Nahshon Wright returned to practice. Both players will be depended on heavily throughout the 2026 season, so seeing them return to the field either in a rehab capacity or full-time is a great thing.
There is still concern, though. D'Angelo Ponds has yet to participate in training camp, and Kenyon Sadiq was seen working on the side field. Both players are still in line for Week 1, but it's hard to see any legitimate role for the rookies without getting legitimate practice time.

title: 4 Jets on Thin Ice Heading Into Preseason Finale: Cade York, Braiden McGregor Fighting to Make 53-Man Roster
full_text:
Wins and losses in August don’t reflect how good or bad a team is. Still, it’s hard not to feel excited when your team wins—especially in dominating fashion.
That’s exactly what the New York Jets did Friday night, shutting out the Pittsburgh Steelers, 17-0, at Heinz Field. Several players stood out and strengthened their roster odds in the victory, like Jason Sanders and Jelani Woods. For the others, however, the night did more harm than good.
That said, here are the four Jets who are on thin ice heading into the preseason finale against the New York Giants.
York was one of several kickers the Jets brought in after Nick Folk’s departure and is a finalist for the starting kicking job alongside Sanders. Entering the first preseason game, York appeared to have the edge in the competition given his play in recent practices.
Despite making both of his field goal attempts against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, his 38-yard field goal attempt appeared to sail wide right. Meanwhile, Sanders converted his lone 47-yard try.
Since then, York has lost all momentum , and Sanders now has the advantage. In last Monday’s practice, Sanders outdueled York , making 7-of-8 field goal attempts, while the former LSU Tiger went 5-of-8, missing from 48, 51, and 54 yards.
York’s fall continued Friday night against the Steelers, missing a 59-yard field goal, while Sanders converted a 39-yard attempt.
Although there is still time for York to turn things around with a strong showing in this week’s slate of practices, he’ll need to prove himself in the preseason finale to make a strong impression with the coaching staff.
If it feels like McGregor has received several opportunities to earn a rotational role in the Jets’ defense, it’s because he has. In his two-year tenure with Gang Green, McGregor hasn’t proved himself useful on either defense or special teams, which is especially concerning given last year’s horrendous team.
The former Michigan Wolverine had chances to solidify his roster spot in the preseason but hasn’t been much of a factor. In 58 defensive snaps, he’s recorded just two pressures and two total tackles, per Pro Football Focus .
Meanwhile, Nate Lynn, who wasn’t even on the team at the beginning of the week, has outperformed McGregor despite playing in 31 fewer snaps, posting four total tackles and two sacks. Even though McGregor’s stock has fallen, he still has a legitimate path to making the 53-man roster.
The Jets could opt to keep five edge rushers, giving McGregor another opportunity to stick around. However, he’ll need to make a noticeable impact in the preseason finale to earn that spot. Otherwise, the Jets could look elsewhere for the final spot.
Zappe appeared to be the frontrunner for the QB2 role after OTAs, but he’s since fallen on the depth chart. Poor showings in minicamp and training camp have led to Zappe being surpassed by rookie Cade Klubnik, who has firmly established himself as the backup to Geno Smith.
His underwhelming play carried over into the preseason opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he threw two interceptions. Although Zappe played better against the Steelers, completing 6-of-8 of his passes for 68 yards, Brady Cook got the better of him, capping off the game with a 31-yard touchdown pass.
Despite this, Zappe remains the favorite over Cook, as he continues to receive more reps than him. However, this doesn’t guarantee the veteran will make the 53-man roster. The Jets could look to bolster their quarterback depth through the trade market, with Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy and Eagles quarterback Andy Dalton potentially available if their respective teams decide to move on from them.
A strong performance in the preseason finale could help Zappe solidify his standing, but another underwhelming showing gives New York reason to explore its options elsewhere.
Trayanum has had a golden opportunity to earn a roster spot over these last few weeks. However, the former Toledo Rocket has failed to take advantage of increased reps with Isaiah Davis and Breece Hall sidelined with injuries.
Across two preseason games (31 offensive snaps), Trayanum has been inefficient running the ball, rushing for just 24 yards on nine attempts. Trayanum has arguably been worse in protection, allowing two pressures in five pass-blocking snaps, per PFF.
He’s also struggled to make an impact on special teams, missing a tackle and picking up a holding call on a kick return. Not only has his roster chances taken a massive hit, but Trayanum isn’t guaranteed to make New York's practice squad anymore.
If Trayanum is to remain in New York, he’ll need a strong showing against the Giants to keep his practice squad hopes alive. If not, the Jets could look elsewhere to find an RB to stash on the taxi squad.

title: 2 Reasons Why Geno Smith Can Succeed with Jets Despite Any Lingering Concerns
full_text:
The Jets have seen both the good and the bad side of veteran quarterback Geno Smith's game through the first month of training camp and the first two weeks of free agency.
When he's good, Smith is a productive thrower of the football, using his strong arm and years of experience to move the ball down the field with an assortment of weaponry by his side. However, when things aren't going well, Smith's gunslinger mentality has led to interceptions and stalled offensive production.
At 36 years old, it would be hard to find anyone who feels Smith can become a top-10 quarterback in the league. You simply can't teach an old dog new tricks, especially when that dog has thrown more interceptions than anyone in the last two years combined.
But if Friday night's 17-0 preseason win over the Steelers showed anything, it's that the Jets were not only right to bring Smith in for the 2026 season, but that he should be successful in his second stint with New York.
And there's two key reasons why.
Look at last year's offensive depth chart for the Raiders around Smith. Now look at the group playing with Smith this year in Florham Park. Most objective analysts and fans can agree that the Jets have the more impressive supporting cast than the Raiders.
While the Silver and Black have an excellent tight end in Brock Bowers, there really isn't a position last year where they had a better player than the current Jets roster does right now.
That's a fundamental difference that will aid Smith this season.
In his final year in Seattle, an organization one year away from a Super Bowl title, Smith won 10 games. He finished with 15 interceptions and at times looked like he held the team back, but still, 10 wins is nothing to scoff at.
That highlights one key part: if he has the right supporting cast, an NFL organization can win with Smith along for the ride. New York understands this reality, simply because they aren't paying him an  extreme amount of money to start for them in 2026. There is also no long-term guarantee he'll be around beyond the upcoming season.
But if the Jets' key players on offense —wide receiver Garrett Wilson, running back Breece Hall, and the stalwart tackles in Armand Membou and Olu Fashanu—all stay healthy, then Smith will have a cast that can allow him to distribute the ball evenly and on time.
Against Pittsburgh, the Jets saw that firsthand. New York's offense was unstoppable on its lone drive of the game that resulted in a touchdown. Much of that came down to Smith. But in a deeper sense, it had to do with the supporting cast as well.
That brings us to the second point too.
Smith went 7-for-7 for 65 yards and his lone touchdown pass. New York's offense converted several third downs, and four different receivers caught passes on the opening drive. That balanced distribution—coupled with a perfect passer rating—means Smith's day was efficient.
not a bad start 😮‍💨 📺: #NYJvsPIT on @NFLonCBS , @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/Ias9l0WIsu
If the Jets are going to find success in 2026, they'll need that word to be a central theme for the offense with Smith leading the way.
"Very efficient," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said of Smith's performance on Friday. "I think he had two 3rd down completions. Within that, he threw to five different receivers within that drive. He looked very comfortable, did exactly what we were looking for."
Smith's completion percentage shows of an efficient player. He has completed more than 64% of his passes in each of the last four seasons as a starter. With the Raiders, he completed 67% of his passes. It shows he wasn't the key problem for Las Vegas's offense last year.
If the Jets can get that kind of accuracy and efficiency from Smith, their offense will be significantly better than the last-place group from last season. Expectations aren't exactly too high to clear in 2026, but Gang Green should feel confident that Smith will be up to the task.
If anything, the unit showed on Friday they'll be a far better watch compared to last year.
And that might make all the distance for Jets fans.

title: Every Jet Who Helped Their 53-Man Roster Odds in the Win vs. Steelers (Including Jason Sanders)
full_text:
After falling to the Buccaneers to open the preseason, the Jets got their first exhibition win Friday night , shutting out the Steelers, 17-0.
We learned plenty from Gang Green’s victory . Geno Smith and the offense looked great in the opening drive, where he engineered a 10-play drive, going 7-for-7 for 65 yards and throwing a touchdown to Jelani Woods. At the same time, David Bailey recorded his first of (hopefully) many sacks.
The star players weren’t the only ones who shined. Several players on the bubble strengthened their chances of earning a spot on the 53-man roster with their performance. That being said, here are the five players who increased their chances of making the final roster.
Since joining the Jets in early June, Jason Sanders and Cade York have been in a back-and-forth competition for the starting kick job. While both players have made a compelling case over the last few months why they deserve the job, neither kicker had separated themselves until last week.
Sanders has emerged as the leader in the last few practices, particularly on Monday, when he converted 7-of-8 of his field goal attempts, while York made 5-of-8. The former All-Pro kicker strengthened his lead Friday night, nailing both his lone field goal and extra point attempt, while York missed his 59-yard attempt.
Although the battle is still far from being over, Sanders can establish himself as New York’s starting kicker with another solid week and by converting on all his field goal attempts.
With Kenyon Sadiq, Mason Taylor and Jeremy Ruckert at the top of the Jets’ tight end depth chart, Jelani Woods was considered an afterthought for a roster spot. Teams rarely carry four tight ends on their active roster, and the former 2022 third-round pick has played in just four games over the last three seasons combined.
For Woods to give himself any chance to earn a spot, he needed to capitalize on every opportunity. So far, he’s done just that. With Sadiq sidelined due to a setback from his hernia surgery, Woods has put together a string of solid performances in practice and has made a strong case for the final 53-man roster.
He bolstered his chances against the Steelers, capping off the opening drive with a touchdown. Woods has also made an impact as a blocker in the two preseason games, earning a 70.2 and 67.4 pass-blocking grade , respectively, per Pro Football Focus.
Another strong showing in the team’s preseason finale against the New York Giants could secure his roster spot.
Another player who was widely considered an unlikely candidate for a roster spot was Samuel Womack. With New York crowded at cornerback, the former 2022 fifth-round pick faced a challenging path to making the final roster
But with multiple injuries to the cornerback room, Womack has taken advantage of every opportunity and has been one of the standout players in the Jets' training camp. His play in coverage stood out in the victory against the Steelers, where he recorded an interception, allowed no receptions across 20 coverage snaps, and earned an 89.9 coverage grade per PFF .
Womack’s play so far has been encouraging and has put him on the right path to securing a spot on the 53-man roster. However, he’ll need to prove that he can be a reliable contributor on special teams to solidify a spot with New York.
Kiko Mauigoa, Marcelino McCrary-Ball, and Mykal Walker have been competing for the Jets’ top backup role for the last few months. While each has had some solid moments in practice, none has firmly established themselves as a legitimate candidate.
This, along with New York not upgrading at the position, allowed Chase Wilson to make his case for a roster spot. The undrafted free agent out of West Virginia played a critical role in the team’s shutout win, leading the team in tackles alongside Jordan Clark with six while also recording two pressures and a sack.
Wilson also played well in coverage, being targeted once across 24 coverage snaps. While Wilson still faces an uphill battle to make the roster, his performance against Pittsburgh showed that he deserves to be in the conversation. He’ll need to continue making plays in the preseason finale to give himself a chance.
Talk about making a strong impression, Nate Lynn played a significant role in the Jets' win. Having just signed three days earlier, Lynn had the game of his life, recording four tackles, four pressures, and two sacks in 27 defensive snaps, earning an 85.9 pass-rush grade , per PFF .
Lynn remains a long shot to make the final roster given New York’s depth at edge rusher. However, his play against the Steelers has put him on the radar for the preseason finale. His previous experience with head coach Aaron Glenn in Detroit could also give him an advantage as he competes for a spot.
s/o Nate Lynn "it was a no brainer to get him here" pic.twitter.com/bcLcKqn5Ey
Still, the practice squad remains the likely outcome for Lynn. If he can replicate another strong showing against the Giants, though, New York may have a much tougher decision to make.

title: Major Concern No More: Jets' Defense Is Clearly Turning a Corner in Key Area
full_text:
History was made last year with the Jets, and not the kind of history teams want to make .
Much has been made about the Jets' failure to record an interception last year. No team in NFL history had failed to record one for an entire season up until that point. But New York took steps along the offseason to make sure that dubious distinction.
All-Pros like Minkah Fitzpatrick were added to the secondary. New York even drafted David Bailey to improve the pass rush as a way to force quarterbacks into more mistakes .
Through two preseason games, the investments seem to be paying off early. The Jets intercepted not one, but two Steeler passes in Friday's 17-0 win in the Steel City.
Andre Cisco in the right place at the right time 😌 NYJvsPIT on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eLGuXJYqMB
While four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers didn't throw either errant pass, it did highlight the Jets' improved mindset in forcing turnovers.
Even if there's still room to grow.
Former Pro Bowl cornerback Nahshon Wright was the first player to acknowledge the team's lack of interceptions last year. Instead of harping on the record, though, New York has focused more on improving the process they run that leads to forcing turnovers.
"I honestly don't think it's been brought up at all in meetings," Wright said. "I think 2025 was 2025, and I think we're trying to turn over a new leaf, so we haven't spoken about it at all."
Their improved mindset has already paid off. Andre Cisco got the party started with an interception in the first half. Samuel Womack III responded some time later with an interception of his own. Fitzpatrick and Wright did not record any interceptions. Nor did the combination of Brandon Stephens and AZ Thomas.
But one thing the Jets and head coach Aaron Glenn should be pleased with is their thought process, leading to an improvement in forcing turnovers.
Part of the reason why the Jets were so poor at creating turnovers last year was that they were also bad at getting to the quarterback. New York was among the worst teams in the league in both pressure rate and sacks. If quarterbacks have all day to throw, they won't make so many mistakes. It's why Glenn also addressed the trenches throughout the offseason .
He understands that if the team is to end its interception drought, it won't only come from players in the secondary, but also from getting after the quarterback.
If the Jets can get both sides of the ball to work together, they could bump their interception numbers considerably from last year.
It's also important to note that while the two-INT game on Friday will have fans celebrating, it mirrors last year's preseason. New York's last recorded pick in any game setting was in the preseason finale last year. That highlights a clear part of this whole problem as well.
Getting pressure on a quarterback and recording interceptions in practice and the preseason is one thing. Doing it when the games actually matter will be the next step in improving the current Jets defense.

title: Defensive Domination:  Everything I Saw From Eagles Only Open Practice Of Training Camp
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - In the Eagles only public practice of the summer, cornerback Riq Woolen stole the show with a pick-six to lift the defense over the offense in an 11-period competitive practice that lasted nearly two hours.
The defense was credited with a 58-36 win that was capped by Woolen undercutting DeVonta Smith on a Jalen Hurts throw that didn't have much mustard on it during an end-of-game situational period. The speedy Woolen raced into the end zone and threw the football into the crowd that was over 45,000.
Earlier, Woolen had another interception, showing off his speed while covering rookie receiver Makai Lemon on a crossing route .
The offense had some highlights as well, most notably Saquon Barkley getting loose on an inside release that surprised All-Pro linebacker Zack Baun in the end zone. On the back end of the play, Barkley made a nice catch while going to the ground for a touchdown.
Lemon has trouble generating separation most of the night but offensive coordinator Sean Mannion did scheme the first-round pick open for a touchdown out of the backfield on a wheel route that fooled the defense which busted coverage.
--Before the practice head coach Nick Sirianni noted that the public practice was an operations practice so the coaching staff was also working through their duties and communications for a game day. After stretching and individiual work, passing game coordinator Josh Grizzard and a couple of other assistants were seen taking the elevator up to the coaching box at Lincoln Financial Field.
--Right tackle Lane Johnson was injured in the first few plays of practice when I was trying to get from the field up to the press box. Johnson stayed on the sideline to watch the rest of the practice but did not return. Without rookie Markel Bell (thumb/leg), Fred Johnson handled RT with the first team and John Ojukwu played left tackle.
Also nose tackle Jordan Davis banged-up his elbow in a backed-up period when the Eagles' offense went with a heavy dose of the running game. Davis was able to return wearing a brace.
-- The players who were ruled out of the practice were Bell, CB Jakorian Bennett (knee), TE Grant Calcaterra (back), Dickerson (test), CB Jonathan Jones (shoulder), TE Eli Stowers (hamstring), and S Cole Wisniewski (concussion).
CB Mac McWilliams was limited with a shoulder problem.
-- The offense started sharp early with Hurts and Smith showing off tremendous chemistry and timing on an out route during the first possession. Barkley, meanwhile, has a very good night in the receiving game.
-- Lemon had a difficult time gaining any room when he was near All-Pro CB Quinyon Mitchell. You might be able to write that off but the rookie also couldn't shake LB Jihaad Campbell in the middle of the field.
-- Andy Dalton was first up in with the twos tonight but Tanner McKee mixed in later and Cole Payton even got a few reps. Dalton's highlight was a TD to Elijah Moore on a crossing route.
-- In backed-up period the Eagles went heavy with inside zone to some success with Barkley and Tank Bigsby.
-- With Lane Johnson, Jordan Mailata and Landon Dickerson missing most of the team drills the first-team OL for most of the reps from left to right was Ojukwu, Drew Kendall, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen and Fred Johnson. The second unit from left to right was Myles Hinton, Micah Morris, Jake Majors, Willie Lampkin/Michael Jordan and Cam Williams.
-- Hurts had an opportunity for a deep TD strike on a post route to Smith but underthrew it and allowed Mitchell to get back into the play and break things up.
-- On a key fourth-down attempt Hurts found Smith while rolling right and it was a rare drop for DeVonta, turning the football over on downs. Smith has some trademarked catches as well, most notably imposing his will Mitchell on a comeback route and then doing the same to snatch the football away from the lengthy Woolen.
-- The Eagles broke up the competitive periods with a special teams break where Braden Mann was attempting to pin things deep. The returner rotation was Britain Covey, Cooper DeJean, Lemon and Elijah Moore.
-- WR Darius Cooper had a drop on a slant from Hurts. Moore, meanwhile, has several solid receptions as he makes his final run for a spot on the initial 53.
-- The offense was effective in the red zone period with Will Shipley adding a rushing TD to Barkley's brilliant catch earlier. Majors and Jordan had a great duo block to spring Shipley.
-- On a two-point conversion attempt, Hollywood Brown dropped a McKee throw at the back of the end zone with Kelee Ringo in coverage. Brown did beat Woolen on a late crossing pattern for a touchdown that could have been called a sack.
-- A.J. Epenesa recorded a sack on Dalton when the veteran QB was rolling right out of the pocket in a two-minute drill.
-- In the first two-minute period Hurts converted a 4th-and-2 after a timeout by drawing Moro Ojomo offside.
--The top kickoff-return duo was Shipley and Bigsby. The second-team was Dameon Pierce and Erik Ezukanma.

title: Eight Eagles That Earned Their Roster Spot This Training Camp
full_text:
Heading into the final week of training camp, there are several Philadelphia Eagles that are on the roster bubble. Some of these players could be traded and some of them could be cut.
What about the players that had a good training camp that started training camp on the roster bubble? These are the players that played their way off the bubble and became roster locks ahead of cutdown day.
Call them camp standouts if you wish, but these players are expected to be on the initial 53-man roster .
The release of J.T. Gray on Monday essentially sealed Ringo's roster spot . Both players were special teams standouts, but the Eagles were thin at cornerback and Ringo has had a solid summer.
Gray wasn't in the mix for the final safety spot, while Ringo did enough at cornerback to stick around. Didn't hurt Ringo is one of the best gunners in the league.
There was some concern Shipley wasn't going to be the RB3 at one point in camp. Injuries to Dameon Pierce and Elijah Mitchell, coupled with two strong preseason games locked up Shipley's spot on the roster.
Shipley isn't going to have a lot of touches this season, but the Eagles are deep at running back thanks to how Shipley has performed this preseason. The Eagles have their RB3.
Lampkin earned his roster spot thanks to how he performed at center and guard over the past month. The physicality in Lampkin's play against opposing defensive tackles and his leverage in the A-gap showed up on film.
The Eagles were hoping a few of their young interior linemen would have a standout camp. Lampkin ended up emerging from the bunch.
The No. 3 guard job was open for the taking at the beginning of camp. Through the first week, it was clear Kendall was on his way towards seizing the role.
Kendall emerged as the top option behind Landon Dickerson and Tyler Steen at guard, and is also the No. 2 center. He is arguably the most improved player this training cmap.
If Kendall started a game in 2026 and played well, it wouldn't be a surprise.
A strong start to training camp made Cooper virtually a roster lock, even through there are two receiver spots up for grabs. Cooper was the one of the best receivers through the first three weeks of camp, taking advantage to injuries at the position.
While Cooper still isn't guaranteed a spot yet, he's played his way into that roster lock consideration. Would be surprising if Cooper isn't on the roster.
Robinson started camp with the developmental players and there was considerable doubt he was going to make the 53. The Eagles were deep at defensive tackle and Robinson wasn't improving, and Vic Fangio said he "was on life support."
Over the preseason, Robinson came alive. He had 3.0 sacks in six quarters and played his way onto the 53. Robinson was a fourth-round pick last season, so he played his way onto the team.
Perhaps Robinson will even contribute to this defensive tackle rotation this year.
There was no guarantee Epps was going to be on the roster, even though it was highly likely he was going to be part of the safety equation in some way, shape, or form. Epps took the bull by the horns as the starting safety on Day 1 and never relinquished the role.
Epps is set to start Week 1 at safety. The Eagles are going to be fine with Epps starting with Andrew Mukuba.
Carter wasn't guaranteed a roster spot either, so he had to play his way into the safety equation. He didn't beat out Epps for the starting safety job, but it was clear early on Carter was going to be the No. 3 safety.
There will be an important role for Carter in this secondary, whether it's at safety or cornerback. He's one of the most versatile players in this secondary. Carter is a roster lock.
